1.10.s: ..sūta uvāca..
1.10.d: ॥सूत उवाच॥
1.10.m:
The Sūta said:
When the worlds had become thus, [and] by Brahmā, the creator of the world,
those creatures were not multiplying for whatever reason,

1.10.s:
evaṃbhūteṣu lokeṣu brahmaṇā lokakartṛṇā.
yadā tā na pravarttante prajāḥ kenāpi hetunā .. 10.1 ..
1.10.d:
एवंभूतेषु लोकेषु ब्रह्मणा लोककर्तृणा।
यदा ता न प्रवर्त्तन्ते प्रजाः केनापि हेतुना ॥ 10.1 ॥

1.10.s:
tamomātrāvṛto brahmā tadāprabhṛti duḥkhitaḥ.
tataḥ sa vidadhe buddhimarthaniścayagāminīm .. 10.2 ..
1.10.d:
तमोमात्रावृतो ब्रह्मा तदाप्रभृति दुःखितः।
ततः स विदधे बुद्धिमर्थनिश्चयगामिनीम् ॥ 10.2 ॥
1.10.m: Brahmā, enveloped by a mere fraction of darkness, was afflicted with grief from that time on. / Then he directed his intellect toward determining the matter.

1.10.s:
athātmani samasrākṣīttamomātrāṃ niyāmikām .
rājasatvaṃ parājitya varttamānaṃ sa dharmataḥ .. 10.3 ..
1.10.d:
अथात्मनि समस्राक्षीत्तमोमात्रां नियामिकाम् ।
राजसत्वं पराजित्य वर्त्तमानं स धर्मतः ॥ 10.3 ॥
1.10.m: Then within himself he emitted a regulating measure of darkness, / overcoming the passion-goodness that had proceeded according to dharma.

1.10.s:
tapyate tena duḥkhena śokañcakre jagatpatiḥ.
tamaśca vyanudattasmādrajastamasamāvṛṇot .. 10.4 ..
1.10.d:
तप्यते तेन दुःखेन शोकञ्चक्रे जगत्पतिः।
तमश्च व्यनुदत्तस्माद्रजस्तमसमावृणोत् ॥ 10.4 ॥
1.10.m: The Lord of the world was tormented by that sorrow and felt grief; / he dispelled the darkness, and from that, passion enveloped darkness.

1.10.s:
tattamaḥ pratinuttaṃ vai mithunaṃ sa vyajāyata.
adharmāccaraṇājjajñe hiṃsā śokādajāyata .. 10.5 ..
1.10.d:
तत्तमः प्रतिनुत्तं वै मिथुनं स व्यजायत।
अधर्माच्चरणाज्जज्ञे हिंसा शोकादजायत ॥ 10.5 ॥
1.10.m: From that dispelled darkness, indeed, a pair was born: / Unrighteousness was born from his conduct, and violence was born from grief.

1.10.s:
tatastasmin samudbhūte mithune caraṇātmani.
tataśca bhagavānāsīt prītaścaivamaśiśriyat .. 10.6 ..
1.10.d:
ततस्तस्मिन् समुद्भूते मिथुने चरणात्मनि।
ततश्च भगवानासीत् प्रीतश्चैवमशिश्रियत् ॥ 10.6 ॥
1.10.m: Then, when that pair born of his conduct had arisen, / the Blessed Lord was pleased, and thus he resorted [to action].

1.10.s:
svāṃ tanuṃ sa tato brahmā tāmapohadabhāsvarām.
dvidhākarotsa taṃ dehamarddhena puruṣo'bhavat .. 10.7 ..
1.10.d:
स्वां तनुं स ततो ब्रह्मा तामपोहदभास्वराम्।
द्विधाकरोत्स तं देहमर्द्धेन पुरुषोऽभवत् ॥ 10.7 ॥
1.10.m: Then Brahmā cast off that dark body of his; / he divided that body into two: with one half he became a man,

1.10.s:
arddhena nārī sā tasya śatarūpā vyajāyata.
prākṛtāṃ bhūtadhātrīṃ tāṃ kāmānvai sṛṣṭavān vibhuḥ .. 10.8 ..
1.10.d:
अर्द्धेन नारी सा तस्य शतरूपा व्यजायत।
प्राकृतां भूतधात्रीं तां कामान्वै सृष्टवान् विभुः ॥ 10.8 ॥
1.10.m: and with the other half [became] a woman; she was born as Śatarūpā. / The all-pervading lord created desires in her, the primal supporter of creatures.

1.10.s:
sā divaṃ vṛthivīñcaiva mahimnā vyāpya dhiṣṭhitā.
brahmaṇaḥ sā tanuḥ pūrvā divamāvṛttya tiṣṭhati .. 10.9 ..
1.10.d:
सा दिवं वृथिवीञ्चैव महिम्ना व्याप्य धिष्ठिता।
ब्रह्मणः सा तनुः पूर्वा दिवमावृत्त्य तिष्ठति ॥ 10.9 ॥
1.10.m: She stands pervading heaven and earth with her greatness; / that former body of Brahmā remains covering heaven.

1.10.s:
yā tvarddhāt sṛjate nārī śatarūpā vyajāyata.
sā devī niyutantaptvā tapaḥ paramaduścaram .. 10.10 ..
1.10.d:
या त्वर्द्धात् सृजते नारी शतरूपा व्यजायत।
सा देवी नियुतन्तप्त्वा तपः परमदुश्चरम् ॥ 10.10 ॥
1.10.m: The woman who was created from the half was born as Śatarūpā. / Having performed most difficult austerities for a hundred thousand [years], that goddess

1.10.s:
bhartārandīptayaśasaṃ puruṣaṃ pratyapadyata.
sa vai svāyambhuvaḥ pūrvaṃ puruṣo manurucyate .. 10.11 ..
1.10.d:
भर्तारन्दीप्तयशसं पुरुषं प्रत्यपद्यत।
स वै स्वायम्भुवः पूर्वं पुरुषो मनुरुच्यते ॥ 10.11 ॥
1.10.m: obtained as her husband a man of radiant renown. / He is called the first man, the Svāyambhuva Manu.

1.10.s:
tasyaivasaptatiyugaṃ manvantaramihocyate .
labdhā tu puruṣaḥ patnīṃ śatarūpāmayonijām .. 10.12 ..
1.10.d:
तस्यैवसप्ततियुगं मन्वन्तरमिहोच्यते ।
लब्धा तु पुरुषः पत्नीं शतरूपामयोनिजाम् ॥ 10.12 ॥
1.10.m: His cosmic age of a Manu is said here to be seventy-one yugas. / Having obtained as wife Śatarūpā, who was not born of a womb,

1.10.s:
tayā sa ramate sārddhaṃ tasmātsā ratirucyate.
prathamaḥ saṃprayogaḥ sa kalpādau samavarttata .. 10.13 ..
1.10.d:
तया स रमते सार्द्धं तस्मात्सा रतिरुच्यते।
प्रथमः संप्रयोगः स कल्पादौ समवर्त्तत ॥ 10.13 ॥
1.10.m: the man took pleasure with her; therefore she is called Rati. / That first union took place at the beginning of the aeon.

1.10.s:
virājamasṛjat brahmā so'bhavat puruṣo virāṭ .
samrāṇmānasarūpāttu vai rājastu manuḥ smṛtaḥ .. 10.14 ..
1.10.d:
विराजमसृजत् ब्रह्मा सोऽभवत् पुरुषो विराट् ।
सम्राण्मानसरूपात्तु वै राजस्तु मनुः स्मृतः ॥ 10.14 ॥
1.10.m: Brahmā created Virāj; he became the man Virāj. / From that mental form of the emperor, Manu is known as the son of Virāj.

1.10.s:
sa vairājaḥ prajāsargaḥ sa sarge puruṣo manuḥ.
vairājātpuruṣādvīrācchatarūpā vyajāyata .. 10.15 ..
1.10.d:
स वैराजः प्रजासर्गः स सर्गे पुरुषो मनुः।
वैराजात्पुरुषाद्वीराच्छतरूपा व्यजायत ॥ 10.15 ॥
1.10.m: That creation of progeny was born of Virāj; the man Manu was at the creation. / From the heroic man born of Virāj, Śatarūpā gave birth to

1.10.s:
priyavratottānapādau putrau putravatāṃ varau .
kanye dve ca mahābhāge yābhyāṃ jātāḥ prajāstvimāḥ .. 10.16 ..
1.10.d:
प्रियव्रतोत्तानपादौ पुत्रौ पुत्रवतां वरौ ।
कन्ये द्वे च महाभागे याभ्यां जाताः प्रजास्त्विमाः ॥ 10.16 ॥
1.10.m: two sons, Priyavrata and Uttānapāda, the best of those having sons, / and two most fortunate daughters, from whom these creatures were born:

1.10.s:
devī nāmnā tathākūtiḥ prasūtiścaiva te śubhe.
svāyambhuvaḥ prasūtintu dakṣāya vyasṛjat prabhuḥ .. 10.17 ..
1.10.d:
देवी नाम्ना तथाकूतिः प्रसूतिश्चैव ते शुभे।
स्वायम्भुवः प्रसूतिन्तु दक्षाय व्यसृजत् प्रभुः ॥ 10.17 ॥
1.10.m: the two auspicious goddesses named Ākūti and Prasūti. / The lord Svāyambhuva gave Prasūti to Dakṣa;

1.10.s:
prāṇo dakṣastu vijñeyaḥ saṅkalpo manurucyate.
ruceḥ prajāpateścaiva ākūtiṃ pratyapādayat .. 10.18 ..
1.10.d:
प्राणो दक्षस्तु विज्ञेयः सङ्कल्पो मनुरुच्यते।
रुचेः प्रजापतेश्चैव आकूतिं प्रत्यपादयत् ॥ 10.18 ॥
1.10.m: Dakṣa is to be known as the vital breath, and Manu is called the volition. / And he bestowed Ākūti upon the Prajāpati Ruci.

1.10.s:
ākūtyāṃ mithunaṃ yajñe mānasasya ruceḥ śubham.
yajñaśca dakṣiṇā caiva yamakau sambabhūvatuḥ .. 10.19 ..
1.10.d:
आकूत्यां मिथुनं यज्ञे मानसस्य रुचेः शुभम्।
यज्ञश्च दक्षिणा चैव यमकौ सम्बभूवतुः ॥ 10.19 ॥
1.10.m: An auspicious pair was born of Ākūti and the mind-born Ruci: / Yajña and Dakṣiṇā were born as twins.

1.10.s:
yajñasya dakṣiṇāyāñca putrā dvādaśa jajñire.
yāmā iti samākhayātā devāḥ svāyambhuve'ntare .. 10.20 ..
1.10.d:
यज्ञस्य दक्षिणायाञ्च पुत्रा द्वादश जज्ञिरे।
यामा इति समाखयाता देवाः स्वायम्भुवेऽन्तरे ॥ 10.20 ॥
1.10.m: From Yajña and in Dakṣiṇā twelve sons were born; / they are renowned as the Yāma gods in the cosmic age of Svāyambhuva.

1.10.s:
yamasya putrā yajñasya tasmādyāmāstu te smṛtāḥ.
ajitāścaiva śūkāśca gaṇau dvau brahmaṇaḥ smṛtau .. 10.21 ..
1.10.d:
यमस्य पुत्रा यज्ञस्य तस्माद्यामास्तु ते स्मृताः।
अजिताश्चैव शूकाश्च गणौ द्वौ ब्रह्मणः स्मृतौ ॥ 10.21 ॥
1.10.m: They are sons of Yama Yajña; therefore they are remembered as Yāmas. / The Ajitas and Śūkas are remembered as two hosts of Brahmā.

1.10.s:
yāmāḥ pūrvaṃ parikrāntā yataḥ saṃjñā divaukasaḥ.
svāyambhūvasutāyāntu prasūtyāṃ lokamātaraḥ .. 10.22 ..
1.10.d:
यामाः पूर्वं परिक्रान्ता यतः संज्ञा दिवौकसः।
स्वायम्भूवसुतायान्तु प्रसूत्यां लोकमातरः ॥ 10.22 ॥
1.10.m: The Yāmas were the first who traversed [the realms], whence those heaven-dwellers got their name. / In Prasūti, the daughter of Svāyambhuva, the mothers of the world [were born]:

1.10.s:
tasyāṃ kanyāścaturviṃśaddakṣastvajanayat prabhuḥ.
sarvāstāśca mahābhāgāḥ sarvāḥ kamalalocanāḥ .. 10.23 ..
1.10.d:
तस्यां कन्याश्चतुर्विंशद्दक्षस्त्वजनयत् प्रभुः।
सर्वास्ताश्च महाभागाः सर्वाः कमललोचनाः ॥ 10.23 ॥
1.10.m: the lord Dakṣa begot twenty-four daughters in her; / they were all most fortunate, all lotus-eyed,

1.10.s:
yogapatnyaśca tāḥ sarvāḥ sarvāstā yogamātaraḥ.
śraddhā lakṣmī dhṝtistuṣṭiḥ puṣṭirmedhā kriyā tathā.
buddhirllajjā vapuḥ śāntiḥ siddhiḥ kīrttistrayodaśī .. 10.24 ..
1.10.d:
योगपत्न्यश्च ताः सर्वाः सर्वास्ता योगमातरः।
श्रद्धा लक्ष्मी धॄतिस्तुष्टिः पुष्टिर्मेधा क्रिया तथा।
बुद्धिर्ल्लज्जा वपुः शान्तिः सिद्धिः कीर्त्तिस्त्रयोदशी ॥ 10.24 ॥
1.10.m: and they were all wives of Yoga, all mothers of Yoga: / Śraddhā, Lakṣmī, Dhṛti, Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, Medhā, and Kriyā, / Buddhi, Lajjā, Vapus, Śānti, Siddhi, and Kīrti as the thirteenth.

1.10.s:
patnyarthe pratijagrāha dharmo dākṣāyaṇīḥ prabhuḥ.
dvārāṇyetāni caivāsya vihitāni svayambhuvā .. 10.25 ..
1.10.d:
पत्न्यर्थे प्रतिजग्राह धर्मो दाक्षायणीः प्रभुः।
द्वाराण्येतानि चैवास्य विहितानि स्वयम्भुवा ॥ 10.25 ॥
1.10.m: The lord Dharma took these daughters of Dakṣa as his wives; / and these doors were arranged for him by Svayambhū.

1.10.s:
tābhyaḥ śiṣṭā yavīyasya ekādaśa sulocanāḥ.
khyātiḥ satyatha saṃbhūtiḥ smṛtiḥ prītiḥ kṣamā tathā .. 10.26 ..
1.10.d:
ताभ्यः शिष्टा यवीयस्य एकादश सुलोचनाः।
ख्यातिः सत्यथ संभूतिः स्मृतिः प्रीतिः क्षमा तथा ॥ 10.26 ॥
1.10.m: The remaining eleven younger ones, lovely-eyed: / Khyāti, Satī, Sambhūti, Smṛti, Prīti, Kṣamā,

1.10.s:
sannatiśacavānasūyā ca ūrjjā svāhā svadhā tathā.
tāstataḥ pratyapadyanta punaranye maharṣayaḥ .. 10.27 ..
1.10.d:
सन्नतिशचवानसूया च ऊर्ज्जा स्वाहा स्वधा तथा।
तास्ततः प्रत्यपद्यन्त पुनरन्ये महर्षयः ॥ 10.27 ॥
1.10.m: Sannati, Anasūyā, Ūrjā, Svāhā, and Svadhā. / Then other great seers took them:

1.10.s:
rudro bhṛgurmarīciśca aṅgirāḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ .
pulastyo'trirvasiṣṭhaśca pitaro'gristathaiva ca .. 10.28 ..
1.10.d:
रुद्रो भृगुर्मरीचिश्च अङ्गिराः पुलहः क्रतुः ।
पुलस्त्योऽत्रिर्वसिष्ठश्च पितरोऽग्रिस्तथैव च ॥ 10.28 ॥
1.10.m: Rudra, Bhṛgu, Marīci, Aṅgiras, Pulaha, Kratu, / Pulastya, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, the ancestors, and Agni.

1.10.s:
satīṃ bhavāya prāyacchat khyātiñca bhṛgave tathā.
marīcaye ca sambhūtiṃ smṛtimāṅgirase dadau .. 10.29 ..
1.10.d:
सतीं भवाय प्रायच्छत् ख्यातिञ्च भृगवे तथा।
मरीचये च सम्भूतिं स्मृतिमाङ्गिरसे ददौ ॥ 10.29 ॥
1.10.m: He gave Satī to Bhava, and Khyāti to Bhṛgu; / he gave Sambhūti to Marīci, and Smṛti to the son of Aṅgiras;

1.10.s:
prītiṃ caiva pulastyāya kṣamāṃ vai pulahāya ca.
kratave sannatiṃ nāma anasūyāntathātraye .. 10.30 ..
1.10.d:
प्रीतिं चैव पुलस्त्याय क्षमां वै पुलहाय च।
क्रतवे सन्नतिं नाम अनसूयान्तथात्रये ॥ 10.30 ॥
1.10.m: Prīti to Pulastya, and Kṣamā to Pulaha; / [the one] named Sannati to Kratu, and Anasūyā to Atri;

1.10.s:
ūrjjaṃ dadau vasiṣṭhāya svāhāṃ vai hyagnaye dadau .
svadhāṃ caiva pitṛbhyastu tāsvapatyāni vakṣyate .. 10.31 ..
1.10.d:
ऊर्ज्जं ददौ वसिष्ठाय स्वाहां वै ह्यग्नये ददौ ।
स्वधां चैव पितृभ्यस्तु तास्वपत्यानि वक्ष्यते ॥ 10.31 ॥
1.10.m: he gave Ūrjā to Vasiṣṭha, and Svāhā to Agni, / and Svadhā to the ancestors. Their offspring will be spoken of.

1.10.s:
ete sarve mahābhāgāḥ prajñāḥ svānuṣṭhitāḥ sthitāḥ.
manvantareṣu sarveṣu yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam .. 10.32 ..
1.10.d:
एते सर्वे महाभागाः प्रज्ञाः स्वानुष्ठिताः स्थिताः।
मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु यावदाभूतसंप्लवम् ॥ 10.32 ॥
1.10.m: All these most fortunate ones, wise, remained established in their duties / through all the cosmic ages of Manus, until the dissolution of beings.

1.10.s:
śraddhā kāmaṃ vijajñe vai darpo lakṣmīsutaḥ smṛtaḥ.
dhṛtyāstu niyamaḥ putrastuṣṭayāḥ santoṣa ucyate .. 10.33 ..
1.10.d:
श्रद्धा कामं विजज्ञे वै दर्पो लक्ष्मीसुतः स्मृतः।
धृत्यास्तु नियमः पुत्रस्तुष्टयाः सन्तोष उच्यते ॥ 10.33 ॥
1.10.m: Śraddhā gave birth to Kāma; Darpa is remembered as the son of Lakṣmī; / Niyama was the son of Dhṛti, and Santoṣa is said to be [the son] of Tuṣṭi;

1.10.s:
puṣṭyā lābhaḥ sutaścāpi medhāputraḥ śrutastathā.
kriyāyāstu nayaḥ prokto daṇḍaḥ samaya eva ca .. 10.34 ..
1.10.d:
पुष्ट्या लाभः सुतश्चापि मेधापुत्रः श्रुतस्तथा।
क्रियायास्तु नयः प्रोक्तो दण्डः समय एव च ॥ 10.34 ॥
1.10.m: Lābha was the son of Puṣṭi, and Śruta the son of Medhā; / to Kriyā were born Naya, Daṇḍa, and Samaya;

1.10.s:
buddhervaudhasutaścāpi apramādaśca tāvubhau .
lajjāyā vinayaḥ putro vyavasāyo vapuḥsutaḥ .. 10.35 ..
1.10.d:
बुद्धेर्वौधसुतश्चापि अप्रमादश्च तावुभौ ।
लज्जाया विनयः पुत्रो व्यवसायो वपुःसुतः ॥ 10.35 ॥
1.10.m: to Buddhi were born Bodha and Apramāda, both of them; / to Lajjā the son was Vinaya, and Vyavasāya was the son of Vapus.

1.10.s:
kṣemaḥ śāntisutaścāpi sukhaṃ siddhervyajāyata.
yaśaḥ kīrtteḥ sutaścāpi ityete dharmasūnavaḥ .. 10.36 ..
1.10.d:
क्षेमः शान्तिसुतश्चापि सुखं सिद्धेर्व्यजायत।
यशः कीर्त्तेः सुतश्चापि इत्येते धर्मसूनवः ॥ 10.36 ॥
1.10.m: Kṣema was born as the son of Śānti, and Sukha was born of Siddhi; / Yaśas was the son of Kīrti: these are the sons of Dharma.

1.10.s:
kāmasya harṣaḥ putro vai devyā ratyā vyajāyata.
ityeṣa vai sukhodarkkaḥ sargo dharmasya kīrttitaḥ .. 10.37 ..
1.10.d:
कामस्य हर्षः पुत्रो वै देव्या रत्या व्यजायत।
इत्येष वै सुखोदर्क्कः सर्गो धर्मस्य कीर्त्तितः ॥ 10.37 ॥
1.10.m: Harṣa was indeed born to Kāma through the goddess Rati. / Thus has the creation of Dharma, productive of happiness, been declared.

1.10.s:
jajñe hiṃsā tvadharmāddhai nikṛtiścānṛtāvubhau .
nikṛtyānṛtayorjajñe bhayaṃ naraka eva ca .. 10.38 ..
1.10.d:
जज्ञे हिंसा त्वधर्माद्धै निकृतिश्चानृतावुभौ ।
निकृत्यानृतयोर्जज्ञे भयं नरक एव च ॥ 10.38 ॥
1.10.m: From Adharma were born Hiṃsā, Nikṛti, and Anṛta, both of them. / From Nikṛti and Anṛta were born Bhaya and Naraka,

1.10.s:
māyā ca vedanā cāpi mithunadvayametayoḥ.
bhayājjajñe'tha sā māyā mṛtyuṃ bhūtāpahāriṇam .. 10.39 ..
1.10.d:
माया च वेदना चापि मिथुनद्वयमेतयोः।
भयाज्जज्ञेऽथ सा माया मृत्युं भूतापहारिणम् ॥ 10.39 ॥
1.10.m: and also Māyā and Vedanā, a pair of twins from these two. / Then from Bhaya, that Māyā gave birth to Mṛtyu, who carries away living beings.

1.10.s:
vedanāyāstataścāpi duḥkhaṃ jajñe'tha rauravāt .
mṛtyayorvyādhijvarā śokāḥ krodho'sūyā ca jajñire .
duḥkhāntarā smṛtā hyete sarve cādharmalakṣaṇāḥ .. 10.40 ..
1.10.d:
वेदनायास्ततश्चापि दुःखं जज्ञेऽथ रौरवात् ।
मृत्ययोर्व्याधिज्वरा शोकाः क्रोधोऽसूया च जज्ञिरे ।
दुःखान्तरा स्मृता ह्येते सर्वे चाधर्मलक्षणाः ॥ 10.40 ॥
1.10.m: And from Vedanā, through Raurava, Duḥkha was born. / From Mṛtyu were born diseases, fevers, sorrows, wrath, and malice; / these are considered inward pains, all having the marks of unrighteousness.

1.10.s:
teṣāṃ bhāryā'sti putro vā te sarve nidhanāḥ smṛtāḥ .
ityeṣa tāmasaḥ sargo jajñe dharmaniyāmakaḥ .. 10.41 ..
1.10.d:
तेषां भार्याऽस्ति पुत्रो वा ते सर्वे निधनाः स्मृताः ।
इत्येष तामसः सर्गो जज्ञे धर्मनियामकः ॥ 10.41 ॥
1.10.m: They have neither wives nor sons; they are all known to bring destruction. / Thus was born the dark creation, which regulates righteousness.

1.10.s:
prajāḥ sṛjeti vyādiṣṭo brahmaṇā nīlalohitaḥ .
so'bhidhyāya satīṃ bhāryānnirmame hyātmasambhavām .. 10.42 ..
1.10.d:
प्रजाः सृजेति व्यादिष्टो ब्रह्मणा नीललोहितः ।
सोऽभिध्याय सतीं भार्यान्निर्ममे ह्यात्मसम्भवाम् ॥ 10.42 ॥
1.10.m: Ordered by Brahmā, 'Create offspring!', Nīlalohita, / meditating, fashioned Satī as his wife, born of himself.

1.10.s:
nādhikānna ca hīnāṃstānmānasānātmanaḥ samān.
sahasraṃ hi sahasrāṇāmasṛjat kṛmivāsasā.
tulyā ścaivātmanaḥ sarve rūpatejobalaśrutaiḥ .. 10.43 ..
1.10.d:
नाधिकान्न च हीनांस्तान्मानसानात्मनः समान्।
सहस्रं हि सहस्राणामसृजत् कृमिवाससा।
तुल्या श्चैवात्मनः सर्वे रूपतेजोबलश्रुतैः ॥ 10.43 ॥
1.10.m: Neither superior nor inferior to himself, mental [sons] equal to himself, / wearing insect-silk, he created a thousand thousands, / all equal to himself in form, splendour, strength, and learning:

1.10.s:
piṅgalānsanniṣaṅgāṃśca sakaparddān vilohitān .
vivāsān hari keśāṃśca dṛṣṭighnāṃśca kapālinaḥ .. 10.44 ..
1.10.d:
पिङ्गलान्सन्निषङ्गांश्च सकपर्द्दान् विलोहितान् ।
विवासान् हरि केशांश्च दृष्टिघ्नांश्च कपालिनः ॥ 10.44 ॥
1.10.m: tawny-hued, bearing quivers, with matted hair, reddish, / unclothed, with golden-brown hair, eye-destroying, and skull-bearing;

1.10.s:
bahurūpān virūpāṃśca viśvarūpāṃścarūpiṇaḥ.
rathino varmiṇaścaiva dharmiṇaśca varūthinaḥ .. 10.45 ..
1.10.d:
बहुरूपान् विरूपांश्च विश्वरूपांश्चरूपिणः।
रथिनो वर्मिणश्चैव धर्मिणश्च वरूथिनः ॥ 10.45 ॥
1.10.m: multiform, grotesque, universal in form, having diverse forms; / chariot-fighters, mail-clad, righteous, and equipped with shields;

1.10.s:
sahasraśata bāhūṃśca divyān bhaumāntarikṣagān.
sthūlaśīrṣānaṣṭadaṃṣṭrānudvijihvāṃstrilocanān .. 10.46 ..
1.10.d:
सहस्रशत बाहूंश्च दिव्यान् भौमान्तरिक्षगान्।
स्थूलशीर्षानष्टदंष्ट्रानुद्विजिह्वांस्त्रिलोचनान् ॥ 10.46 ॥
1.10.m: having hundreds and thousands of arms, celestial, dwelling on earth, and moving through the atmosphere; / thick-headed, with eight fangs, two-tongued, and three-eyed;

1.10.s:
annādān piśitādāṃśa cava ājyapān somapāṃstathā.
medapāṃ svātikāyāṃśca śitikaṇṭhogramanyavaḥ .. 10.47 ..
1.10.d:
अन्नादान् पिशितादांश चव आज्यपान् सोमपांस्तथा।
मेदपां स्वातिकायांश्च शितिकण्ठोग्रमन्यवः ॥ 10.47 ॥
1.10.m: eaters of food, eaters of flesh, drinkers of clarified butter, drinkers of soma, / and drinkers of fat; having massive bodies, dark-throated, of fierce anger;

1.10.s:
sopāsaṅgatalatrāṃśca dhanvino hyupavarmiṇaḥ.
āsīnān dhāvataścaiva jṛmbhinaścaiva dhiṣṭhitān .. 10.48 ..
1.10.d:
सोपासङ्गतलत्रांश्च धन्विनो ह्युपवर्मिणः।
आसीनान् धावतश्चैव जृम्भिनश्चैव धिष्ठितान् ॥ 10.48 ॥
1.10.m: possessing quivers and armguards, archers wearing coats of mail; / seated, running, gaping, and standing firm;

1.10.s:
adhyā pino'tha japato yuñjato'dhyāyatastathā.
jvalato varṣataścaiva dyotamānān pradhūpitān .. 10.49 ..
1.10.d:
अध्या पिनोऽथ जपतो युञ्जतोऽध्यायतस्तथा।
ज्वलतो वर्षतश्चैव द्योतमानान् प्रधूपितान् ॥ 10.49 ॥
1.10.m: teaching, reciting prayers, practicing yoga, and meditating; / blazing, raining down, shining, and smoking;

1.10.s:
buddhān buddhatamāṃścaiva brahmiṣṭhān śubhadarśanān .
nīlagrī vān sahasrākṣān saṃrvāścātha kṣapācarān .. 10.50 ..
1.10.d:
बुद्धान् बुद्धतमांश्चैव ब्रह्मिष्ठान् शुभदर्शनान् ।
नीलग्री वान् सहस्राक्षान् संर्वाश्चाथ क्षपाचरान् ॥ 10.50 ॥
1.10.m: awakened and most fully awakened, most devoted to Brahman, fair to behold; / blue-necked, thousand-eyed, and all wanderers in the night;

1.10.s:
adṛśyān sarvabhūtānāṃ mahāyogān mahaujasaḥ.
rūdatodravataścaiva evaṃyuktān sahasraśaḥ.
apātayāmānasṛjat rudrarūpān surottamān .. 10.51 ..
1.10.d:
अदृश्यान् सर्वभूतानां महायोगान् महौजसः।
रूदतोद्रवतश्चैव एवंयुक्तान् सहस्रशः।
अपातयामानसृजत् रुद्ररूपान् सुरोत्तमान् ॥ 10.51 ॥
1.10.m: invisible to all beings, endowed with great yoga and mighty energy; / weeping and running: such ones by the thousands, / having the form of Rudra, the highest of gods, he brought forth and created.

1.10.s:
brahmā dṛṣṭvā'bravīdetānmāsrākṣīrīdṛśīḥ prajāḥ.
sraṣṭavyā nātmanastulyāḥ prajā naivādhikāstvayā.
anyāḥ sṛjatvaṃ bhadrante sthitohantvaṃ sṛja prajāḥ .. 10.52 ..
1.10.d:
ब्रह्मा दृष्ट्वाऽब्रवीदेतान्मास्राक्षीरीदृशीः प्रजाः।
स्रष्टव्या नात्मनस्तुल्याः प्रजा नैवाधिकास्त्वया।
अन्याः सृजत्वं भद्रन्ते स्थितोहन्त्वं सृज प्रजाः ॥ 10.52 ॥
1.10.m: Seeing them, Brahmā said: 'Do not create such offspring! / Offspring equal to yourself or superior must not be created by you. / Create others, blessings upon you! Cease, and create offspring!'

1.10.s:
ete ye vai mayā mṛṣṭā virūpā nīlalehitāḥ .
sahasrāṇāṃ sahasrantu ātmanopamaniścitāḥ .. 10.53 ..
1.10.d:
एते ये वै मया मृष्टा विरूपा नीललेहिताः ।
सहस्राणां सहस्रन्तु आत्मनोपमनिश्चिताः ॥ 10.53 ॥
1.10.m: [Rudra said:] 'These who have been created by me are grotesque and blue-red, / a thousand thousands, determined to be equal to myself.

1.10.s:
ete devā bhaviṣyanti rūdrā nāma mahābalāḥ.
pṛthivyāmantārīkṣe ca rudranāmnā pratiśrutāḥ .. 10.54 ..
1.10.d:
एते देवा भविष्यन्ति रूद्रा नाम महाबलाः।
पृथिव्यामन्तारीक्षे च रुद्रनाम्ना प्रतिश्रुताः ॥ 10.54 ॥
1.10.m: These gods shall be mighty beings called Rudras, / renowned under the name of Rudra on earth and in the atmosphere.

1.10.s:
śatarudrasamāmnātā bhaviṣyantīha yajñiyāḥ.
yajñabhājo bhaviṣyanti sarve devayugaiḥ saha .. 10.55 ..
1.10.d:
शतरुद्रसमाम्नाता भविष्यन्तीह यज्ञियाः।
यज्ञभाजो भविष्यन्ति सर्वे देवयुगैः सह ॥ 10.55 ॥
1.10.m: Recited in the Śatarudrīya, they shall be worthy of sacrifice here; / they will all partake of sacrifices together with the classes of gods.

1.10.s:
manvantareṣu ye devā bhaviṣyantīha cchandajāḥ.
taiḥ sārddhamījyamānāste sthāsyantīha yugakṣayāt .. 10.56 ..
1.10.d:
मन्वन्तरेषु ये देवा भविष्यन्तीह च्छन्दजाः।
तैः सार्द्धमीज्यमानास्ते स्थास्यन्तीह युगक्षयात् ॥ 10.56 ॥
1.10.m: Together with the gods born according to desire in the cosmic ages of Manus, / being worshipped along with them, they shall abide here until the end of the yuga.'

1.10.s:
evamuktastadā brahmā mahādevena dhīmatā.
pratyuvāca tadā bhīmaṃ hṛṣyamāṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ .. 10. 57 ..
1.10.d:
एवमुक्तस्तदा ब्रह्मा महादेवेन धीमता।
प्रत्युवाच तदा भीमं हृष्यमाणः प्रजापतिः ॥ 10. 57 ॥
1.10.m: Thus addressed then by the wise Mahādeva, / Prajāpati [Brahmā], rejoicing, answered Bhīma:

1.10.s:
evaṃ bhavatu bhadraṃ te yathā te vyāhṛtaṃ prabho.
brahmaṇā samanujñā te sadā sarvamabhūt kila .. 10.58 ..
1.10.d:
एवं भवतु भद्रं ते यथा ते व्याहृतं प्रभो।
ब्रह्मणा समनुज्ञा ते सदा सर्वमभूत् किल ॥ 10.58 ॥
1.10.m: 'So be it, blessings upon you, just as you have spoken, O lord!' / For, granted permission by Brahmā, everything always came to be.

1.10.s:
tataḥprabhṛti deveśo na prāsūyata vai prajāḥ.
ūrddhvaretāḥ sthitaḥ sthāṇuryāvadābhūtasaṃplavam.
yasmāccoktaṃ sthito'smīti tataḥ sthāṇuriti smṛtaḥ .. 10.59 ..
1.10.d:
ततःप्रभृति देवेशो न प्रासूयत वै प्रजाः।
ऊर्द्ध्वरेताः स्थितः स्थाणुर्यावदाभूतसंप्लवम्।
यस्माच्चोक्तं स्थितोऽस्मीति ततः स्थाणुरिति स्मृतः ॥ 10.59 ॥
1.10.m: From then on, the lord of gods did not produce offspring. / He remained chaste, motionless like a pillar, until the dissolution of all beings. / And because he said 'I have ceased' (sthitaḥ), he is known as Sthāṇu.

1.10.s:
jñānaṃ vairāgyamaiśvaryaṃ tapaḥ sacatyaṃ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ.
sraṣṭṛtvamātmasambodhastvadhiṣṭhātṛtvameva ca.
atha yāni daśaitāni nityantiṣṭhanti śaṅkare .. 10.60 ..
1.10.d:
ज्ञानं वैराग्यमैश्वर्यं तपः सचत्यं क्षमा धृतिः।
स्रष्टृत्वमात्मसम्बोधस्त्वधिष्ठातृत्वमेव च।
अथ यानि दशैतानि नित्यन्तिष्ठन्ति शङ्करे ॥ 10.60 ॥
1.10.m: Knowledge, dispassion, sovereign power, asceticism, truth, forbearance, firmness, / the power to create, self-awareness, and presiding authority: / these ten ever abide in Śaṅkara.

1.10.s:
sarvān devān ṛṣīṃścaiva sametānasuraiḥ saha.
atyeti tejasā devo mahādevastataḥ smṛtaḥ .. 10.61 ..
1.10.d:
सर्वान् देवान् ऋषींश्चैव समेतानसुरैः सह।
अत्येति तेजसा देवो महादेवस्ततः स्मृतः ॥ 10.61 ॥
1.10.m: Because the god surpasses all gods and seers together with the asuras / in brilliance, he is called Mahādeva.

1.10.s:
atyeti devānaiścaryādbalena ca mahāsurān.
jñānena ca munīn sarvān yogādbhūtāni sarvaśaḥ .. 10.62 ..
1.10.d:
अत्येति देवानैश्चर्याद्बलेन च महासुरान्।
ज्ञानेन च मुनीन् सर्वान् योगाद्भूतानि सर्वशः ॥ 10.62 ॥
1.10.m: He surpasses the gods in sovereign power, the great asuras in strength, / all the sages in knowledge, and all beings in yoga.

1.10.s: ..ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
1.10.d: ॥ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
1.10.m:
The seers said:
Tell us, O great sage, of yoga, asceticism, truth, and also dharma,
and the means of attaining the knowledge of Maheśvara.

1.10.s:
yogaṃ tapaśca satyañca dharmañcāpi mahāmune.
māheśvarasya jñānasya sādhanañca prajakṣva naḥ .. 10.63 ..
1.10.d:
योगं तपश्च सत्यञ्च धर्मञ्चापि महामुने।
माहेश्वरस्य ज्ञानस्य साधनञ्च प्रजक्ष्व नः ॥ 10.63 ॥

1.10.s:
yena yena ca dharmeṇa gatiṃ prāpsyanti vai dvijāḥ.
tatsarvaṃ śrotumicchāmi yogaṃ māheśvaraṃ prabho .. 10.64 ..
1.10.d:
येन येन च धर्मेण गतिं प्राप्स्यन्ति वै द्विजाः।
तत्सर्वं श्रोतुमिच्छामि योगं माहेश्वरं प्रभो ॥ 10.64 ॥
1.10.m: and by what righteousness the twice-born attain their goal: / all that yoga belonging to Maheśvara I wish to hear, O lord.'

1.10.s: .. vāyuruvāca..
1.10.d: ॥ वायुरुवाच॥
1.10.m:
Vāyu said:
Five dharmas in the Purāṇa were declared by Rudra,
as the sovereignty of Maheśvara was proclaimed by the Rudras of unwearied deeds.

1.10.s:
pañca dharmāḥ purāṇe tu rudreṇa samudāhṛtāḥ.
māheśvaryaṃ yathā proktaṃ rudrairakliṣṭakarmabhiḥ .. 10.65 ..
1.10.d:
पञ्च धर्माः पुराणे तु रुद्रेण समुदाहृताः।
माहेश्वर्यं यथा प्रोक्तं रुद्रैरक्लिष्टकर्मभिः ॥ 10.65 ॥

1.10.s:
ādityairvasubhiḥ sādhyairaśvibhyāñcaiva sarvaśaḥ.
marudbhirbhṛgubhiścaiva ye cānye vibudhālayāḥ .. 10.66 ..
1.10.d:
आदित्यैर्वसुभिः साध्यैरश्विभ्याञ्चैव सर्वशः।
मरुद्भिर्भृगुभिश्चैव ये चान्ये विबुधालयाः ॥ 10.66 ॥
1.10.m: By the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Sādhyas, and the two Aśvins everywhere, / by the Maruts and the Bhṛgus, and whoever else are dwellers in the realm of the gods,

1.10.s:
yamaśukrapurogaiśca pitṛkālāntakaistathā.
etaiśvānyaiśacava bahubhiste dharmāḥ paryupāsitāḥ .. 10.67 ..
1.10.d:
यमशुक्रपुरोगैश्च पितृकालान्तकैस्तथा।
एतैश्वान्यैशचव बहुभिस्ते धर्माः पर्युपासिताः ॥ 10.67 ॥
1.10.m: led by Yama and Śukra, and by the ancestors, Kāla, and Antaka: / by these and many others were those practices worshipped.

1.10.s:
te vai prakṣīṇakarmāṇaḥ śāradāmbaranirmalāḥ.
upāsate munigaṇāḥ sandhāyātmānamātmani .. 10.68 ..
1.10.d:
ते वै प्रक्षीणकर्माणः शारदाम्बरनिर्मलाः।
उपासते मुनिगणाः सन्धायात्मानमात्मनि ॥ 10.68 ॥
1.10.m: With their actions exhausted, pure as the autumn sky, / the hosts of sages worship [them], fixing the self within the Self.

1.10.s:
gurupriyahite yuktā gurūṇāṃ vai priyepsavaḥ.
vimucya mānuṣaṃ janma viharanti ca devavat .. 10.69 ..
1.10.d:
गुरुप्रियहिते युक्ता गुरूणां वै प्रियेप्सवः।
विमुच्य मानुषं जन्म विहरन्ति च देववत् ॥ 10.69 ॥
1.10.m: Devoted to what is pleasing and beneficial to their teachers, seeking what is dear to teachers, / freed from human birth, they wander like gods.

1.10.s:
maheśvareṇa ye proktāḥ pañca dharmāḥ sanātanāḥ.
tān sarvān kramayogena ucyamānānnibodhata .. 10.70 ..
1.10.d:
महेश्वरेण ये प्रोक्ताः पञ्च धर्माः सनातनाः।
तान् सर्वान् क्रमयोगेन उच्यमानान्निबोधत ॥ 10.70 ॥
1.10.m: The five eternal practices that were proclaimed by Maheśvara: / listen to them all as they are spoken in proper order.

1.10.s:
prāṇāyāmastathā dhyānaṃ pratyāhāro'tha dhāraṇā.
smaraṇañcaiva yoge'smin pañca dharmāḥ prakīrttitāḥ .. 10.71 ..
1.10.d:
प्राणायामस्तथा ध्यानं प्रत्याहारोऽथ धारणा।
स्मरणञ्चैव योगेऽस्मिन् पञ्च धर्माः प्रकीर्त्तिताः ॥ 10.71 ॥
1.10.m: Breath-control, meditation, withdrawal of the senses, retention, / and recollection: in this yoga these are declared the five practices.

1.10.s:
teṣāṃ kramaviśeṣeṇa lakṣaṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ tathā.
pravakṣyāmi tathā tattvaṃ yathā rudreṇa bhāṣitam .. 10.72 ..
1.10.d:
तेषां क्रमविशेषेण लक्षणं कारणं तथा।
प्रवक्ष्यामि तथा तत्त्वं यथा रुद्रेण भाषितम् ॥ 10.72 ॥
1.10.m: Their distinctive sequence, characteristics, cause, / and true reality I will explain, exactly as spoken by Rudra.

1.10.s:
prāṇāyāmagatiśvāpi prāṇasyāyāma ucyate .
sa cāpi trividhaḥ prokto mando madhyottamastathā .. 10.73 ..
1.10.d:
प्राणायामगतिश्वापि प्राणस्यायाम उच्यते ।
स चापि त्रिविधः प्रोक्तो मन्दो मध्योत्तमस्तथा ॥ 10.73 ॥
1.10.m: The movement of breath-control is called the extension of breath; / and that is said to be threefold: mild, medium, and intense.

1.10.s:
prāṇānāñca nirodhastu sa prāṇāyāmasaṃjñitaḥ .
prāṇāyāmapramāṇantu mātrā vai dvādaśa smṛtāḥ .. 10.74 ..
1.10.d:
प्राणानाञ्च निरोधस्तु स प्राणायामसंज्ञितः ।
प्राणायामप्रमाणन्तु मात्रा वै द्वादश स्मृताः ॥ 10.74 ॥
1.10.m: The restraint of the breaths is called breath-control; / the measure of breath-control is taught to be twelve morae.

1.10.s:
mando dvādaśamātrastu udvātā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ .
madhyamaśca dvirudvātaścaturviṃśatimātrikaḥ .. 10.75 ..
1.10.d:
मन्दो द्वादशमात्रस्तु उद्वाता द्वादश स्मृताः ।
मध्यमश्च द्विरुद्वातश्चतुर्विंशतिमात्रिकः ॥ 10.75 ॥
1.10.m: The mild has twelve morae, twelve expirations are prescribed; / the medium has two expirations and consists of twenty-four morae.

1.10.s:
uttamastatrtrirudvāto mātrāḥ ṣaṭ‌triṃśaducyate.
svedakampaviṣādānāṃ janano hyuttamaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 10.76 ..
1.10.d:
उत्तमस्तत्र्त्रिरुद्वातो मात्राः षट्‌त्रिंशदुच्यते।
स्वेदकम्पविषादानां जननो ह्युत्तमः स्मृतः ॥ 10.76 ॥
1.10.m: The highest [prāṇāyāma] is called threefold in exhalation, [measuring] thirty-six mātrās. / For the highest is remembered as that which produces sweat, trembling, and depression.

1.10.s:
ityetat trividhaṃ proktaṃ prāṇāyāmasya lakṣaṇam.
pramāṇañca samāsena lakṣaṇañca nibodhata .. 10.77 ..
1.10.d:
इत्येतत् त्रिविधं प्रोक्तं प्राणायामस्य लक्षणम्।
प्रमाणञ्च समासेन लक्षणञ्च निबोधत ॥ 10.77 ॥
1.10.m: Thus the threefold characteristic of prāṇāyāma has been stated. / Understand the measure and the characteristic in summary:

1.10.s:
siṃho vā kuñjaro vāpi tathā'nyo vā mṛgo vane.
gṛhītaḥ sevyamānastu mṛduḥ samupajāyate .. 10.78 ..
1.10.d:
सिंहो वा कुञ्जरो वापि तथाऽन्यो वा मृगो वने।
गृहीतः सेव्यमानस्तु मृदुः समुपजायते ॥ 10.78 ॥
1.10.m: A lion, an elephant, or another wild animal in the forest, / once captured and tended, becomes gentle.

1.10.s:
tathā prāṇo durādharṣaḥ sarveṣāmakṛtātmanām .
yogataḥ sevyamānastu sa evābhyāsato vrajet .. 10.79 ..
1.10.d:
तथा प्राणो दुराधर्षः सर्वेषामकृतात्मनाम् ।
योगतः सेव्यमानस्तु स एवाभ्यासतो व्रजेत् ॥ 10.79 ॥
1.10.m: Just so the breath, unconquerable for all who have not disciplined themselves, / when attended to through yoga, comes [under control] through that very practice.

1.10.s:
sa caiva hi yathā siṃhaḥ kuñjaro vāpi durbalaḥ.
kālāntaravaśādyogādgamyate parimarddanāt .. 10.80 ..
1.10.d:
स चैव हि यथा सिंहः कुञ्जरो वापि दुर्बलः।
कालान्तरवशाद्योगाद्गम्यते परिमर्द्दनात् ॥ 10.80 ॥
1.10.m: And just as even a lion or an elephant is made weak / and brought under control through the passage of time and yoga, by subduing it,

1.10.s:
paridhāya mano mandaṃ vaśyatvaṃ cādhigacchati .
paridhāya manodevaṃ tathā jīvati mārutaḥ .. 10.81 ..
1.10.d:
परिधाय मनो मन्दं वश्यत्वं चाधिगच्छति ।
परिधाय मनोदेवं तथा जीवति मारुतः ॥ 10.81 ॥
1.10.m: restraining the sluggish mind, it attains submissiveness. / Restraining the divine mind, the wind lives accordingly.

1.10.s:
vaśyatvaṃ hi yathā vāyurgacchate yogamāsthitaḥ.
tadā svacchandataḥ prāṇaṃ nayate yatra cecchati .. 10.82 ..
1.10.d:
वश्यत्वं हि यथा वायुर्गच्छते योगमास्थितः।
तदा स्वच्छन्दतः प्राणं नयते यत्र चेच्छति ॥ 10.82 ॥
1.10.m: For when the wind, established in yoga, attains submissiveness, / then at will it leads the breath wherever one wishes.

1.10.s:
yathā siṃho gajo vāpi vaśyatvādavatiṣṭhate.
abhayāya manuṣyāṇāṃ mṛgebhyaḥ saṃpravarttate .. 10.83 ..
1.10.d:
यथा सिंहो गजो वापि वश्यत्वादवतिष्ठते।
अभयाय मनुष्याणां मृगेभ्यः संप्रवर्त्तते ॥ 10.83 ॥
1.10.m: Just as a lion or an elephant abides in docility, / [and] acts for the fearlessness of human beings from wild beasts,

1.10.s:
yathā paricitaścāyaṃ vāyurvai viśvatomukhaḥ.
paridhyāyamānaḥ saṃruddhaḥ śarīre kilbiṣaṃ dahat .. 10.84 ..
1.10.d:
यथा परिचितश्चायं वायुर्वै विश्वतोमुखः।
परिध्यायमानः संरुद्धः शरीरे किल्बिषं दहत् ॥ 10.84 ॥
1.10.m: so this wind facing all directions, when familiarized, / meditated upon and held back, burns up the sin in the body.

1.10.s:
prāṇāyāmena yuktasya viprasya niyatātmanaḥ.
sarve doṣāḥ praṇaśyanti sattvasthaścaiva jāyate .. 10.85 ..
1.10.d:
प्राणायामेन युक्तस्य विप्रस्य नियतात्मनः।
सर्वे दोषाः प्रणश्यन्ति सत्त्वस्थश्चैव जायते ॥ 10.85 ॥
1.10.m: For the self-restrained brāhmaṇa engaged in prāṇāyāma, / all faults perish, and he becomes established in sattva.

1.10.s:
tapāṃsi yāni tapyante vratāni niyamāśca ye.
sarvayajñaphalañcaiva prāṇāyāmaśca tatsamaḥ .. 10.86 ..
1.10.d:
तपांसि यानि तप्यन्ते व्रतानि नियमाश्च ये।
सर्वयज्ञफलञ्चैव प्राणायामश्च तत्समः ॥ 10.86 ॥
1.10.m: Whatever austerities are performed, and whatever vows and observances [undertaken], / and the fruit of all sacrifices—prāṇāyāma is equal to that.

1.10.s:
abbinduṃ yaḥ kuśāgreṇa māsi māsi samaśrute.
saṃvatsaraśataṃ sāgraṃ prāṇāyāmañca tatsamam .. 10.87 ..
1.10.d:
अब्बिन्दुं यः कुशाग्रेण मासि मासि समश्रुते।
संवत्सरशतं साग्रं प्राणायामञ्च तत्समम् ॥ 10.87 ॥
1.10.m: He who eats [only] a drop of water on the tip of a blade of kuśa grass month after month / for a full hundred years—prāṇāyāma is equal to that.

1.10.s:
prāṇāyāmairdaherdoṣān dhāraṇābhiśca kilbiṣam.
pratyāhāreṇa viṣayān dhyānenānāśvarān guṇān .. 10.88 ..
1.10.d:
प्राणायामैर्दहेर्दोषान् धारणाभिश्च किल्बिषम्।
प्रत्याहारेण विषयान् ध्यानेनानाश्वरान् गुणान् ॥ 10.88 ॥
1.10.m: One should burn faults by prāṇāyāmas, and sin by concentrations; / [one should burn] sense-objects by withdrawal of the senses, and perishable qualities by meditation.

1.10.s:
tasmādyuktaḥ sadā yogī prāṇāyāmaparo bhavet .
sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā paraṃ brahmādhigacchati .. 10.89 ..
1.10.d:
तस्माद्युक्तः सदा योगी प्राणायामपरो भवेत् ।
सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा परं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति ॥ 10.89 ॥
1.10.m: Therefore, the yogin, always disciplined, should be devoted to prāṇāyāma. / With soul purified from all sin, he attains the supreme brahman.

1.10.s: iti śrīma hāpurāṇe vāyuprokte manvantarādivarṇanaṃ nāma daśamo'dhyāḥ .. 10 ..
1.10.d: इति श्रीम हापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मन्वन्तरादिवर्णनं नाम दशमोऽध्याः ॥ 10 ॥
1.10.m: Thus ends the tenth chapter, entitled “Description of the Manvantaras and Others,” in the glorious Great Purāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.11.s: .. vāyuruvāca ..
1.11.d: ॥ वायुरुवाच ॥
1.11.m:
Vāyu said:
One great day, or else a day and night,
a half-month, likewise a month, the solstitial half-years, years, and yugas,

1.11.s:
ekaṃ mahāntaṃ divasamahorātramathāpi vā.
arddhamāsaṃ tathā māsamayanābdayugāni ca .. 11.1 ..
1.11.d:
एकं महान्तं दिवसमहोरात्रमथापि वा।
अर्द्धमासं तथा मासमयनाब्दयुगानि च ॥ 11.1 ॥

1.11.s:
mahāyugasahasrāṇi ṛṣayastapasi sthitāḥ.
upāsate mahātmānaḥ prāṇaṃ divyena cakṣuṣā .. 11.2 ..
1.11.d:
महायुगसहस्राणि ऋषयस्तपसि स्थिताः।
उपासते महात्मानः प्राणं दिव्येन चक्षुषा ॥ 11.2 ॥
1.11.m: for thousands of mahāyugas, the seers, steadfast in austerity, / magnanimous, attend upon the breath with the divine eye.

1.11.s:
ataūrddhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi prāṇāyāmaprayojanam.
phalañcaiva viśeṣeṇa yathāha bhagavān prabhuḥ .. 11.3 ..
1.11.d:
अतऊर्द्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि प्राणायामप्रयोजनम्।
फलञ्चैव विशेषेण यथाह भगवान् प्रभुः ॥ 11.3 ॥
1.11.m: Hereafter I shall proclaim the purpose of prāṇāyāma / and especially its fruit, as the blessed Lord has declared.

1.11.s:
prayojanāni catvāri prāṇāyāmasya viddhivai.
śāntiḥ praśāntirdīptiśca prasādaśca catuṣṭayam .. 11.4 ..
1.11.d:
प्रयोजनानि चत्वारि प्राणायामस्य विद्धिवै।
शान्तिः प्रशान्तिर्दीप्तिश्च प्रसादश्च चतुष्टयम् ॥ 11.4 ॥
1.11.m: Know the four purposes of prāṇāyāma: / pacification, deep peace, illumination, and serenity—a group of four.

1.11.s:
ghorākāraśivānāntu karmaṇāṃ phalasambhavam.
svayaṃkṛtāni kālena ihāmutra ca dehinām .. 11.5 ..
1.11.d:
घोराकारशिवानान्तु कर्मणां फलसम्भवम्।
स्वयंकृतानि कालेन इहामुत्र च देहिनाम् ॥ 11.5 ॥
1.11.m: The arising of the fruit of actions of terrifying or auspicious nature, / committed by oneself in the course of time here and in the hereafter for embodied beings,

1.11.s:
pitṛmātṛ praduṣṭānāṃ jñātisambandhisaṅkaraiḥ.
kṣapaṇaṃ hi kaṣāyāṇāṃ pāpānāṃ śāntirucyate .. 11.6 ..
1.11.d:
पितृमातृ प्रदुष्टानां ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिसङ्करैः।
क्षपणं हि कषायाणां पापानां शान्तिरुच्यते ॥ 11.6 ॥
1.11.m: the destruction of the defilements, the sins of those corrupted by mother and father [or] by mixing with relatives and kin, / is called pacification.

1.11.s:
lobhamānātmakānāṃ hi pāpānāmapi saṃyamaḥ .
ihāmutra hitārthāya praśāntistapa ucyate .. 11.7 ..
1.11.d:
लोभमानात्मकानां हि पापानामपि संयमः ।
इहामुत्र हितार्थाय प्रशान्तिस्तप उच्यते ॥ 11.7 ॥
1.11.m: The restraint of sins consisting of greed and pride / for the sake of benefit here and in the hereafter—this austerity is called deep peace.

1.11.s:
sūryendugrahatārāṇāṃ tulyastu viṣayo bhavet.
ṛṣīṇāñca prasiddhānāṃ jñānavijñānasampadām .. 11.8 ..
1.11.d:
सूर्येन्दुग्रहताराणां तुल्यस्तु विषयो भवेत्।
ऋषीणाञ्च प्रसिद्धानां ज्ञानविज्ञानसम्पदाम् ॥ 11.8 ॥
1.11.m: The scope of the sun, moon, planets, and stars becomes equal / [for the yogin] and for renowned seers endowed with knowledge and discernment.

1.11.s:
atītānāgatānāñca darśanaṃ sāmpratasya ca .
buddhasya samatāṃ yānti dīptiḥ syāttapa ucyate .. 11.9 ..
1.11.d:
अतीतानागतानाञ्च दर्शनं साम्प्रतस्य च ।
बुद्धस्य समतां यान्ति दीप्तिः स्यात्तप उच्यते ॥ 11.9 ॥
1.11.m: The vision of past, future, and present / reaches equality with the enlightened [mind]; this austerity is called illumination.

1.11.s:
indriyāṇīndriyārthāṃśca manaḥ pañca ca mārutān .
prasādayati yenāsau prasāda iti saṃjñitaḥ .. 11.10 ..
1.11.d:
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थांश्च मनः पञ्च च मारुतान् ।
प्रसादयति येनासौ प्रसाद इति संज्ञितः ॥ 11.10 ॥
1.11.m: Because he soothes the senses and the sense-objects, / the mind, and the five winds, it is called serenity.

1.11.s:
ityeṣa dharmaḥ prathamaḥ prāṇāyāmaścaturvidhaḥ.
sannikṛṣṭaphalo jñeyaḥ sadyaḥkālaprasādajaḥ .. 11.11 ..
1.11.d:
इत्येष धर्मः प्रथमः प्राणायामश्चतुर्विधः।
सन्निकृष्टफलो ज्ञेयः सद्यःकालप्रसादजः ॥ 11.11 ॥
1.11.m: Thus this is the first dharma, the fourfold prāṇāyāma, / whose fruit is to be known as near at hand, born from instantaneous serenity.

1.11.s:
ata ūrddhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi prāṇāyāmasya lakṣaṇam.
āsanaṃ ca yathātattvaṃ yuñjato yogameva ca .. 11.12 ..
1.11.d:
अत ऊर्द्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि प्राणायामस्य लक्षणम्।
आसनं च यथातत्त्वं युञ्जतो योगमेव च ॥ 11.12 ॥
1.11.m: Hereafter I shall proclaim the characteristic of prāṇāyāma / and the posture, according to truth, for one applying yoga:

1.11.s:
oṅkāraṃ prathamaṃ kṛtvā candrasūyauṃ praṇamya ca.
āsanaṃ svastikaṃ kṛtvā pajhamarddhāsanantathā .. 11.13 ..
1.11.d:
ओङ्कारं प्रथमं कृत्वा चन्द्रसूयौं प्रणम्य च।
आसनं स्वस्तिकं कृत्वा पझमर्द्धासनन्तथा ॥ 11.13 ॥
1.11.m: First uttering the sound Om, and bowing to the moon and sun, / having assumed the svastika posture, the lotus posture, and the half-posture,

1.11.s:
samajānurekajānuruttānaḥ susthito'pi ca.
samo dṛḍhāsano bhūtvā saṃhṛtya caraṇāvubhau .. 11.14 ..
1.11.d:
समजानुरेकजानुरुत्तानः सुस्थितोऽपि च।
समो दृढासनो भूत्वा संहृत्य चरणावुभौ ॥ 11.14 ॥
1.11.m: with both knees level, or with one knee [up], supine, or well seated, / even, with a firm posture, having drawn back both feet,

1.11.s:
saṃvṛtāsyo'vabaddhākṣa uro viṣṭabhya cāgrataḥ.
pārṣṇibhyāṃ vṛṣaṇe chādya tathā prajananaṃ tataḥ .. 11.15 ..
1.11.d:
संवृतास्योऽवबद्धाक्ष उरो विष्टभ्य चाग्रतः।
पार्ष्णिभ्यां वृषणे छाद्य तथा प्रजननं ततः ॥ 11.15 ॥
1.11.m: with mouth closed, eyes restrained, supporting the chest forward, / covering the testicles and then the generative organ with the heels,

1.11.s:
kiñcidunnāmitaśirāḥ śiro grīvāṃ tathaiva ca.
samprekṣya nāsikāgraṃ svaṃ diśaścānavalokayan .. 11.16 ..
1.11.d:
किञ्चिदुन्नामितशिराः शिरो ग्रीवां तथैव च।
सम्प्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन् ॥ 11.16 ॥
1.11.m: with head slightly raised, [keeping] head and neck [straight], / looking at the tip of one's nose and not gazing at the quarters,

1.11.s:
tamaḥ pracchādya rajasā rajaḥ sattvena cchādayet .
tataḥ sattvasthito bhūtvā yogaṃ yuñjan samāhitaḥ .. 11.17 ..
1.11.d:
तमः प्रच्छाद्य रजसा रजः सत्त्वेन च्छादयेत् ।
ततः सत्त्वस्थितो भूत्वा योगं युञ्जन् समाहितः ॥ 11.17 ॥
1.11.m: one should shroud tamas with rajas, and shroud rajas with sattva. / Then, established in sattva, concentrated, applying yoga,

1.11.s:
indriyāṇīndriyārthāṃśca manaḥ pañca sa mārutān.
vigṛhya samavāyeva pratyāhāramupakramet .. 11.18 ..
1.11.d:
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थांश्च मनः पञ्च स मारुतान्।
विगृह्य समवायेव प्रत्याहारमुपक्रमेत् ॥ 11.18 ॥
1.11.m: having restrained the senses and sense-objects, / the mind, and the five winds together, one should undertake withdrawal of the senses.

1.11.s:
yastu pratyāharet kāmān kūrmo'ṅgānīva sarvataḥ.
tathātmaratirekasthaḥ paśyatyātmānamātmani .. 11.19 ..
1.11.d:
यस्तु प्रत्याहरेत् कामान् कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वतः।
तथात्मरतिरेकस्थः पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मनि ॥ 11.19 ॥
1.11.m: He who withdraws desires on all sides as a tortoise its limbs, / taking delight only in the self, concentrated, sees the self in the self.

1.11.s:
pūrayitvā śarīrantu sa bāhyābhyantaraṃ śuciḥ.
ākaṇṭhanābhiyogena pratyāhāramupakramet .. 11.20 ..
1.11.d:
पूरयित्वा शरीरन्तु स बाह्याभ्यन्तरं शुचिः।
आकण्ठनाभियोगेन प्रत्याहारमुपक्रमेत् ॥ 11.20 ॥
1.11.m: Having filled the body, both external and internal, pure, / through the union of the throat and the navel, he should undertake withdrawal of the senses.

1.11.s:
kalāmātrastu vijñeyo nimeṣonmeṣa eva ca.
tathā dvādaśamātrastu prāṇāyāmo vidhīyate .. 11.21 ..
1.11.d:
कलामात्रस्तु विज्ञेयो निमेषोन्मेष एव च।
तथा द्वादशमात्रस्तु प्राणायामो विधीयते ॥ 11.21 ॥
1.11.m: The kalāmātrā is to be understood as the twinkling of an eye, / and prāṇāyāma is prescribed as [consisting of] twelve mātrās.

1.11.s:
dhāraṇā dvādaśāyāmo yogo vai dhāraṇādvayam.
tathā vai yogayuktaśca aiśvaryaṃ pratipadyate .
vīkṣate paramātmānaṃ dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā .. 11.22 ..
1.11.d:
धारणा द्वादशायामो योगो वै धारणाद्वयम्।
तथा वै योगयुक्तश्च ऐश्वर्यं प्रतिपद्यते ।
वीक्षते परमात्मानं दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा ॥ 11.22 ॥
1.11.m: Dhāraṇā is twelve āyāmas; yoga is two dhāraṇās. / And thus united in yoga, he attains sovereign power; / he beholds the Supreme Self shining with its own radiance.

1.11.s:
prāṇāyāmena yuktasya viprasya niyatātmanaḥ.
sarve doṣāḥ praṇaśyanti sattvasthaścaiva jāyate .. 11.23 ..
1.11.d:
प्राणायामेन युक्तस्य विप्रस्य नियतात्मनः।
सर्वे दोषाः प्रणश्यन्ति सत्त्वस्थश्चैव जायते ॥ 11.23 ॥
1.11.m: For the self-restrained brāhmaṇa engaged in prāṇāyāma, / all faults perish, and he becomes established in sattva.

1.11.s:
evaṃ vai niyatāhāraḥ prāṇāyāmaparāyaṇaḥ.
jitvā jitvā sadā bhūmimārohettu sadā muniḥ .. 11.24 ..
1.11.d:
एवं वै नियताहारः प्राणायामपरायणः।
जित्वा जित्वा सदा भूमिमारोहेत्तु सदा मुनिः ॥ 11.24 ॥
1.11.m: Thus, with regulated food, devoted to prāṇāyāma, / the sage should always ascend each stage, having conquered it each time.

1.11.s:
ajitā hi mahābhūmirdoṣānutpādayedbahūn .
vivarddhayati sammohaṃ na rohedajitāṃ tataḥ .. 11.25 ..
1.11.d:
अजिता हि महाभूमिर्दोषानुत्पादयेद्बहून् ।
विवर्द्धयति सम्मोहं न रोहेदजितां ततः ॥ 11.25 ॥
1.11.m: For an unconquered great stage produces many faults; / it increases delusion; therefore, one should not ascend to an unconquered [stage].

1.11.s:
nālena tu yathā toyaṃ yantreṇaiva balānvitaḥ.
āpibeta prayatnena tathā vāyuñjitaśramaḥ .. 11.26 ..
1.11.d:
नालेन तु यथा तोयं यन्त्रेणैव बलान्वितः।
आपिबेत प्रयत्नेन तथा वायुञ्जितश्रमः ॥ 11.26 ॥
1.11.m: Just as a strong man drinks water through a tube by means of an instrument with effort, / so one who has overcome fatigue should draw in the wind.

1.11.s:
nābhyāṃ ca hṛdaye caiva kaṇṭhe urasi cānane.
nāsāgre tu tathā netre bhruvormadhye'tha mūrddhani .. 11.27 ..
1.11.d:
नाभ्यां च हृदये चैव कण्ठे उरसि चानने।
नासाग्रे तु तथा नेत्रे भ्रुवोर्मध्येऽथ मूर्द्धनि ॥ 11.27 ॥
1.11.m: In the navel, in the heart, in the throat, in the chest, in the mouth, / on the tip of the nose, in the eyes, between the eyebrows, and in the head,

1.11.s:
kiñcidūrddhvaṃ parasmiṃśca dhāraṇā paramā smṛtā.
prāṇāpānasamārodhāt prāṇāyāmaḥ sa kathyate .. 11.28 ..
1.11.d:
किञ्चिदूर्द्ध्वं परस्मिंश्च धारणा परमा स्मृता।
प्राणापानसमारोधात् प्राणायामः स कथ्यते ॥ 11.28 ॥
1.11.m: and slightly above that, in the highest, the supreme dhāraṇā is remembered. / Because of the restraint of prāṇa and apāna, it is called prāṇāyāma.

1.11.s:
manaso dhāraṇā caiva dhāraṇeti prakīrtitā.
nivṛtti rviṣayāṇāntu pratyāhārastu saṃjñitaḥ .. 11.29 ..
1.11.d:
मनसो धारणा चैव धारणेति प्रकीर्तिता।
निवृत्ति र्विषयाणान्तु प्रत्याहारस्तु संज्ञितः ॥ 11.29 ॥
1.11.m: The holding of the mind is celebrated as dhāraṇā, / and the cessation of sense-objects is called pratyāhāra.

1.11.s:
sarveṣāṃ samavāye tu siddhiḥ syādyogalakṣaṇā.
tayotpannasya yogasya dhyānaṃ vai siddhilakṣaṇam.
dhyānayuktaḥ sadā paśyedātmānaṃ sūryacandravat .. 11.30 ..
1.11.d:
सर्वेषां समवाये तु सिद्धिः स्याद्योगलक्षणा।
तयोत्पन्नस्य योगस्य ध्यानं वै सिद्धिलक्षणम्।
ध्यानयुक्तः सदा पश्येदात्मानं सूर्यचन्द्रवत् ॥ 11.30 ॥
1.11.m: When all [the limbs] combine, however, perfection characterized by yoga arises. / Of yoga thus generated, meditation indeed is the mark of perfection. / Engaged in meditation, he should always see the Self like the sun and the moon.

1.11.s:
sattvasyānupapattau tu darśanantu nava vidyate.
adeśakālayogasya darśanantu na vidyate .. 11.31 ..
1.11.d:
सत्त्वस्यानुपपत्तौ तु दर्शनन्तु नव विद्यते।
अदेशकालयोगस्य दर्शनन्तु न विद्यते ॥ 11.31 ॥
1.11.m: In the absence of inner clarity, however, vision does not occur. / For one practicing at the improper place and time, vision does not occur.

1.11.s:
agnyabhyāśe vane vāpi śuṣkaparṇacaye tathā.
jantuvyāpte śmaśāne vā jīrṇagoṣṭhe catuṣpathe .. 11.32 ..
1.11.d:
अग्न्यभ्याशे वने वापि शुष्कपर्णचये तथा।
जन्तुव्याप्ते श्मशाने वा जीर्णगोष्ठे चतुष्पथे ॥ 11.32 ॥
1.11.m: Near fire or in a forest, or upon a heap of dry leaves, / in a place infested with vermin, in a cremation ground, in a ruined cow-pen, at a crossroads,

1.11.s:
saśabde sabhaye vāpi caityavalmīkasaṃcaye.
udapāne tathā nadyānna bādhātaḥ kadācana .. 11.33 ..
1.11.d:
सशब्दे सभये वापि चैत्यवल्मीकसंचये।
उदपाने तथा नद्यान्न बाधातः कदाचन ॥ 11.33 ॥
1.11.m: where there is noise or where there is danger, near a sacred tree or an anthill, / at a well or by a river, without obstacle at any time,

1.11.s:
kṣudhāviṣstathā'prito na ca vyākulacetanaḥ.
yuñjīta paramaṃ dhyānaṃ yogī dhyānaparaḥ sadā .. 11.34 ..
1.11.d:
क्षुधाविष्स्तथाऽप्रितो न च व्याकुलचेतनः।
युञ्जीत परमं ध्यानं योगी ध्यानपरः सदा ॥ 11.34 ॥
1.11.m: afflicted by hunger, troubled, or with a perturbed mind, [he must not practice]. / The yogin, always devoted to meditation, should engage in supreme meditation.

1.11.s:
etān doṣān viniścitya pramādādyo yunakti vai.
tasya doṣāḥ prakupyanti śarīre vighnakārakāḥ .. 11.35 ..
1.11.d:
एतान् दोषान् विनिश्चित्य प्रमादाद्यो युनक्ति वै।
तस्य दोषाः प्रकुप्यन्ति शरीरे विघ्नकारकाः ॥ 11.35 ॥
1.11.m: Ascertaining these flaws, he who practices through negligence— / his bodily humors, creating obstacles, become violently agitated.

1.11.s:
jaḍatvaṃ badhiratvaṃ ca mūkatvaṃ cādhigacchati.
andhatvaṃ smṛtilopaśca jarā rogastathaiva ca .. 11.36 ..
1.11.d:
जडत्वं बधिरत्वं च मूकत्वं चाधिगच्छति।
अन्धत्वं स्मृतिलोपश्च जरा रोगस्तथैव च ॥ 11.36 ॥
1.11.m: He incurs dullness, deafness, and muteness, / blindness, loss of memory, old age, and disease as well.

1.11.s:
tasya doṣāḥ prakupyanti ajñānādyo yunakti vai.
tasmājjñānena śuddhena yogī yuñjetsamāhitaḥ .. 11.37 ..
1.11.d:
तस्य दोषाः प्रकुप्यन्ति अज्ञानाद्यो युनक्ति वै।
तस्माज्ज्ञानेन शुद्धेन योगी युञ्जेत्समाहितः ॥ 11.37 ॥
1.11.m: His bodily humors become violently agitated—he who practices through ignorance. / Therefore, with pure knowledge, concentrated, the yogin should practice.

1.11.s:
apramattaḥ sadā caiva na doṣān prāpruyāt vkacit .
teṣāṃ cikitsāṃ vakṣyāmi doṣāṇāṃ ca yathākramam.
yathā gacchanti te doṣāḥ prāṇāyāmasamutthitāḥ .. 11.38 ..
1.11.d:
अप्रमत्तः सदा चैव न दोषान् प्राप्रुयात् व्कचित् ।
तेषां चिकित्सां वक्ष्यामि दोषाणां च यथाक्रमम्।
यथा गच्छन्ति ते दोषाः प्राणायामसमुत्थिताः ॥ 11.38 ॥
1.11.m: Ever heedful, he would never incur any flaws. / I shall explain the remedy for those flaws in due order, / how those flaws arising from breath-control depart.

1.11.s:
snigdhāṃ yavāgūmatyuṣṇāṃ bhuktvāṃ tatrāvadhārayet .
etena kramayogena vātagulmaṃ praśāmyati .. 11.39 ..
1.11.d:
स्निग्धां यवागूमत्युष्णां भुक्त्वां तत्रावधारयेत् ।
एतेन क्रमयोगेन वातगुल्मं प्रशाम्यति ॥ 11.39 ॥
1.11.m: Having eaten unctuous, very hot gruel, he should fix [his attention] there. / By this sequential practice, a wind-lump is pacified.

1.11.s:
gudāvarttapratīkāramidaṃ kuryyāccikitsitam.
bhuktvā dadhi yavāgūrvā vāyurūrddhvaṃ tato vrajeta .. 11.40 ..
1.11.d:
गुदावर्त्तप्रतीकारमिदं कुर्य्याच्चिकित्सितम्।
भुक्त्वा दधि यवागूर्वा वायुरूर्द्ध्वं ततो व्रजेत ॥ 11.40 ॥
1.11.m: He should apply this remedy as a countermeasure for rectal obstruction: / having eaten curd or gruel, the breath then moves upward.

1.11.s:
vāyugraṃthiṃ tato bhittvā vāyudeśe prayojayet .
tathāpi na viśeṣaḥ syāddhāraṇāṃ mūrdhni dhārayet .. 11.41 ..
1.11.d:
वायुग्रंथिं ततो भित्त्वा वायुदेशे प्रयोजयेत् ।
तथापि न विशेषः स्याद्धारणां मूर्ध्नि धारयेत् ॥ 11.41 ॥
1.11.m: Then, having broken the knot of wind, he should direct it to the region of wind. / Even then, if there is no distinction, he should maintain concentration on the head.

1.11.s:
yuñjānasya tanuṃ tasya sattavasthasyaiva dehinaḥ.
gudāvarttapratīghāte etat kuryyāccikitsitam .. 11.42 ..
1.11.d:
युञ्जानस्य तनुं तस्य सत्तवस्थस्यैव देहिनः।
गुदावर्त्तप्रतीघाते एतत् कुर्य्याच्चिकित्सितम् ॥ 11.42 ॥
1.11.m: For that embodied being who is practicing his body, remaining in sattva, / he should apply this remedy against rectal obstruction.

1.11.s:
sarvagātraprakampena samārabdhasya yoginaḥ .
imāṃ cikitsāṃ kurvvīta tayā saṃpadyate sukhī .. 11.43 ..
1.11.d:
सर्वगात्रप्रकम्पेन समारब्धस्य योगिनः ।
इमां चिकित्सां कुर्व्वीत तया संपद्यते सुखी ॥ 11.43 ॥
1.11.m: For the yogin afflicted by trembling of all his limbs, / he should perform this remedy; through it he becomes comfortable.

1.11.s:
manasā yadvrataṃ kiñcidviṣṭambhīkṛtya dhārayet.
uroddhāte uraḥsthānaṃ kaṇṭhadeśe ca dhārayet .. 11.44 ..
1.11.d:
मनसा यद्व्रतं किञ्चिद्विष्टम्भीकृत्य धारयेत्।
उरोद्धाते उरःस्थानं कण्ठदेशे च धारयेत् ॥ 11.44 ॥
1.11.m: Whatever resolve is made in the mind, having steadied it, he should hold it. / In chest affliction, he should hold [concentration] in the region of the chest and in the region of the throat.

1.11.s:
tvaco'vadhāte tāṃ vāci bādhirye śrotrayostathā.
jihvāsthāne tṛṣārttastu agre snehāṃśca tantubhiḥ.
phalaṃ vai cintayedyogī tataḥ saṃpadyate sukhī .. 11.45 ..
1.11.d:
त्वचोऽवधाते तां वाचि बाधिर्ये श्रोत्रयोस्तथा।
जिह्वास्थाने तृषार्त्तस्तु अग्रे स्नेहांश्च तन्तुभिः।
फलं वै चिन्तयेद्योगी ततः संपद्यते सुखी ॥ 11.45 ॥
1.11.m: In skin affliction, in speech; in deafness, likewise in the ears; / afflicted by thirst, in the place of the tongue, at the tip [of the tongue], with oily threads; / the yogin should meditate on a fruit; then he becomes comfortable.

1.11.s:
kṣaye kuṣṭhe sakīlāse dhārayetsarvasātvikīm.
yasmin yasmin rajodeśe tasmin yukto vinirddiśet .. 11.46 ..
1.11.d:
क्षये कुष्ठे सकीलासे धारयेत्सर्वसात्विकीम्।
यस्मिन् यस्मिन् रजोदेशे तस्मिन् युक्तो विनिर्द्दिशेत् ॥ 11.46 ॥
1.11.m: In consumption, leprosy, and white leprosy, he should maintain concentration of an entirely sattvic nature. / In whatever region rajas is situated, focused on that, he should direct it.

1.11.s:
yogotpannasya viprasya idaṃ kuryāccikitsitam.
vaṃśakīlena mūrddhānaṃ dhārayāṇasya tāḍayet.
mūrdhni kīlaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya kāṣṭhaṃ kāṣṭhena tāḍayet .. 11.47 ..
1.11.d:
योगोत्पन्नस्य विप्रस्य इदं कुर्याच्चिकित्सितम्।
वंशकीलेन मूर्द्धानं धारयाणस्य ताडयेत्।
मूर्ध्नि कीलं प्रतिष्ठाप्य काष्ठं काष्ठेन ताडयेत् ॥ 11.47 ॥
1.11.m: For a brahmin in whom yoga has arisen, he should apply this treatment: / for one holding [the mind], he should tap the crown of the head with a bamboo peg; / having placed a peg on the head, he should strike wood with wood.

1.11.s:
bhayabhītasya sā saṃjñā tataḥ pratyāgamiṣyati.
atha vā luptasaṃjñasya hastābhyāṃ tatra dhārayet .. 11.48 ..
1.11.d:
भयभीतस्य सा संज्ञा ततः प्रत्यागमिष्यति।
अथ वा लुप्तसंज्ञस्य हस्ताभ्यां तत्र धारयेत् ॥ 11.48 ॥
1.11.m: For one terrified by fear, consciousness will then return. / Or, for one whose consciousness is lost, he should hold it there with both hands.

1.11.s:
pratilabhya tataḥ saṃjñāṃ dhāraṇāṃ mūrdhni dhārayet.
srigdhamalpaṃ ca bhuñjīta tataḥ saṃpadyate sukhī .. 11.49 ..
1.11.d:
प्रतिलभ्य ततः संज्ञां धारणां मूर्ध्नि धारयेत्।
स्रिग्धमल्पं च भुञ्जीत ततः संपद्यते सुखी ॥ 11.49 ॥
1.11.m: Then, having regained consciousness, he should maintain concentration on the head. / He should eat unctuous and small amounts; then he becomes comfortable.

1.11.s:
amānuṣeṇa sattvena yadā budhyati yogavit .
divaṃ ca pṛthivīñcaiva vāyumagniṃ ca dhārayet .. 11.50 ..
1.11.d:
अमानुषेण सत्त्वेन यदा बुध्यति योगवित् ।
दिवं च पृथिवीञ्चैव वायुमग्निं च धारयेत् ॥ 11.50 ॥
1.11.m: When the knower of yoga is possessed by an non-human being, / he should concentrate upon the sky, the earth, the wind, and the fire.

1.11.s:
prāṇāyāmena tatsarvaṃ dahyamānaṃ vaśībhavet.
athāpi praviśeddehaṃ tatastaṃ pratiṣedhayet .. 11.51 ..
1.11.d:
प्राणायामेन तत्सर्वं दह्यमानं वशीभवेत्।
अथापि प्रविशेद्देहं ततस्तं प्रतिषेधयेत् ॥ 11.51 ॥
1.11.m: Being burnt by breath-control, all that becomes submissive. / And if it should still enter the body, he should then ward it off.

1.11.s:
tataḥ saṃstabhya yogena dhārayānasya mūrddhāni.
prāṇāyāmāgninā dagdhaṃ tatsarvaṃ vilayaṃ vrajet .. 11.52 ..
1.11.d:
ततः संस्तभ्य योगेन धारयानस्य मूर्द्धानि।
प्राणायामाग्निना दग्धं तत्सर्वं विलयं व्रजेत् ॥ 11.52 ॥
1.11.m: Then, having restrained [it] through yoga, on the crown of the head of one who holds [the mind], / burnt by the fire of breath-control, all of that dissolves.

1.11.s:
kṛṣṇasarpāparādhaṃ tu dhārayeddhṛdayodare .
maharjanastapaḥ satyaṃ hṛdi kṛtvā tu dhārayet .. 11.53 ..
1.11.d:
कृष्णसर्पापराधं तु धारयेद्धृदयोदरे ।
महर्जनस्तपः सत्यं हृदि कृत्वा तु धारयेत् ॥ 11.53 ॥
1.11.m: In the case of an offense [caused] by a black serpent, he should hold [concentration] in the heart and abdomen. / Having placed Mahas, Janas, Tapas, and Satya in the heart, he should hold [them].

1.11.s:
viṣasya tu phalaṃ pītvā viśalyāṃ dhārayettataḥ .
sarvataḥ sanagāṃ pṛthvīṃ kṛtvā manasi dhārayet .. 11.54 ..
1.11.d:
विषस्य तु फलं पीत्वा विशल्यां धारयेत्ततः ।
सर्वतः सनगां पृथ्वीं कृत्वा मनसि धारयेत् ॥ 11.54 ॥
1.11.m: Having drunk the effect of poison, he should then hold Viśalyā. / Having placed the entire earth together with its mountains in his mind, he should hold it.

1.11.s:
hṛdi kṛtvā samudrāṃśca tathā sarvāśca devatāḥ .
sahasreṇa ghaṭānāñca yuktaḥ snāyīta yogavit .. 11.55 ..
1.11.d:
हृदि कृत्वा समुद्रांश्च तथा सर्वाश्च देवताः ।
सहस्रेण घटानाञ्च युक्तः स्नायीत योगवित् ॥ 11.55 ॥
1.11.m: Having placed the oceans and all the gods in his heart, / the knower of yoga, focused, should bathe with a thousand jars [of water].

1.11.s:
udake kaṇṭhamātre tu dhāraṇāṃ mūdhni dhārayet.
pratisrotoviṣāviṣṭo dhārayet sarvagātrikīm .. 11.56 ..
1.11.d:
उदके कण्ठमात्रे तु धारणां मूध्नि धारयेत्।
प्रतिस्रोतोविषाविष्टो धारयेत् सर्वगात्रिकीम् ॥ 11.56 ॥
1.11.m: In water up to the neck, he should maintain concentration on the crown of the head. / If seized by poison moving against the stream, he should maintain [concentration] over all his limbs.

1.11.s:
śīrṇo'rkapatrapuṭakaiḥ pibedvalmīkamṛttikām .
cikitsitavidhirhyeṣa viśruto yoganirmitaḥ .. 11.57 ..
1.11.d:
शीर्णोऽर्कपत्रपुटकैः पिबेद्वल्मीकमृत्तिकाम् ।
चिकित्सितविधिर्ह्येष विश्रुतो योगनिर्मितः ॥ 11.57 ॥
1.11.m: Emaciated, he should drink anthill clay using cups of calotropis leaves. / This is the famed method of treatment devised through yoga.

1.11.s:
vyākhyātastu samāsena yogadṛṣṭena hetunā.
bruvato lakṣaṇaṃ viddhi viprasya kathayet vkacit .. 11.58 ..
1.11.d:
व्याख्यातस्तु समासेन योगदृष्टेन हेतुना।
ब्रुवतो लक्षणं विद्धि विप्रस्य कथयेत् व्कचित् ॥ 11.58 ॥
1.11.m: It has been explained in brief according to the principle seen in yoga. / Know the mark as I speak; he should rarely declare it to a brahmin.

1.11.s:
athāpi kathayenmohāttadvijñānaṃ pralīyate.
tasmāt pravṛttiryyogasya na vaktavyā kathañcana .. 11.59 ..
1.11.d:
अथापि कथयेन्मोहात्तद्विज्ञानं प्रलीयते।
तस्मात् प्रवृत्तिर्य्योगस्य न वक्तव्या कथञ्चन ॥ 11.59 ॥
1.11.m: If he should speak out of delusion, that discerning knowledge vanishes. / Therefore, the onset of yoga should not be spoken of under any circumstances.

1.11.s:
sattvaṃ tathārogyamalolupatvaṃ varṇaprabhā susvarasaumyatā ca.
gandhaḥ śubho mūtrapurīṣa malpaṃ yogapravṛttiḥ prathamā śarīre .. 11.60 ..
1.11.d:
सत्त्वं तथारोग्यमलोलुपत्वं वर्णप्रभा सुस्वरसौम्यता च।
गन्धः शुभो मूत्रपुरीष मल्पं योगप्रवृत्तिः प्रथमा शरीरे ॥ 11.60 ॥
1.11.m: Inner clarity, freedom from disease, absence of greed, radiance of complexion, sweetness of voice, / a pleasant odor, and scanty urine and feces—this is the first manifestation of yoga in the body.

1.11.s:
ātmānaṃ pṛthivīñcaiva jvalantīṃ yadi paśyati.
kṛtvānyaṃ viśate caiva vidyāt siddhimupasthitām . 11.61 ..
1.11.d:
आत्मानं पृथिवीञ्चैव ज्वलन्तीं यदि पश्यति।
कृत्वान्यं विशते चैव विद्यात् सिद्धिमुपस्थिताम् । 11.61 ॥
1.11.m: If he sees himself and the earth blazing, / and having assumed another [form], enters it, he should know that perfection has arrived.

1.11.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte pāśupatayogo nāmaikādaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 11 ..
1.11.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते पाशुपतयोगो नामैकादशोऽध्यायः ॥ 11 ॥
1.11.m: Thus ends the eleventh chapter, titled 'Pāśupata Yoga', in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.12.s: .. sūta uvāca ..
1.12.d: ॥ सूत उवाच ॥
1.12.m:
The Sūta said:
Hereafter I shall explain the obstacles as they are,
whatever flaws arise for an embodied being who has perceived reality.

1.12.s:
ata ūrddhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi upasargā yathā tathā .
prādurbhavanti ye doṣā dṛṣṭatattvasya dehinaḥ .. 12.1 ..
1.12.d:
अत ऊर्द्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि उपसर्गा यथा तथा ।
प्रादुर्भवन्ति ये दोषा दृष्टतत्त्वस्य देहिनः ॥ 12.1 ॥

1.12.s:
mānuṣyān vividhān kāmān kāmayeta ṛtuṃ striyaḥ.
vidyādānaphalañcaiva upasṛṣṭastu yogavit .. 12.2 ..
1.12.d:
मानुष्यान् विविधान् कामान् कामयेत ऋतुं स्त्रियः।
विद्यादानफलञ्चैव उपसृष्टस्तु योगवित् ॥ 12.2 ॥
1.12.m: Afflicted by obstacles, the knower of yoga desires various human desires: / women at their season, and the fruit of imparting knowledge,

1.12.s:
agnihotraṃ haviryajñametat prāyatanaṃ tathā.
māyākarma dhanaṃ svargamupasṛṣṭastu kāṃkṣati .. 12.3 ..
1.12.d:
अग्निहोत्रं हविर्यज्ञमेतत् प्रायतनं तथा।
मायाकर्म धनं स्वर्गमुपसृष्टस्तु कांक्षति ॥ 12.3 ॥
1.12.m: the Agnihotra, the oblation sacrifice, this effort, / deeds of magical illusion, wealth, and heaven—afflicted by obstacles, he craves these.

1.12.s:
eṣa karmasu yuktastu so'vidyāvaśamāgataḥ.
upasṛṣṭantu jānīyādvuddhyā caiva visarjjayet.
nityaṃ brahmaparo yukta upasargāt pramucyate .. 12.4 ..
1.12.d:
एष कर्मसु युक्तस्तु सोऽविद्यावशमागतः।
उपसृष्टन्तु जानीयाद्वुद्ध्या चैव विसर्ज्जयेत्।
नित्यं ब्रह्मपरो युक्त उपसर्गात् प्रमुच्यते ॥ 12.4 ॥
1.12.m: Engaged in these rituals, he has come under the power of ignorance. / One should recognize him as afflicted by obstacles, and discard them with the intellect. / Ever devoted to Brahman, focused, he is freed from the obstacle.

1.12.s:
jitapratyupasargasya jitaśvāsasya dehinaḥ.
upasargāḥ pravarttante sāttvarājasatāmasāḥ .. 12.5 ..
1.12.d:
जितप्रत्युपसर्गस्य जितश्वासस्य देहिनः।
उपसर्गाः प्रवर्त्तन्ते सात्त्वराजसतामसाः ॥ 12.5 ॥
1.12.m: For an embodied being who has overcome counter-obstacles and mastered his breath, / obstacles arise that are of the nature of sattva, rajas, and tamas:

1.12.s:
pratibhāśravaṇe caiva na devānāñcaiva darśanam.
bhramāvartaśca ityete siddhilakṣaṇasaṃjñitāḥ .. 12.6 ..
1.12.d:
प्रतिभाश्रवणे चैव न देवानाञ्चैव दर्शनम्।
भ्रमावर्तश्च इत्येते सिद्धिलक्षणसंज्ञिताः ॥ 12.6 ॥
1.12.m: Intuition, hearing [at a distance], and the vision of the gods, / and dizziness and vertigo—these are called the signs of perfection.

1.12.s:
vidyā kāvyaṃ tathā śilpaṃ sarvaṃ vācāvṛtāni tu.
vidyārthāścopatiṣṭhanti prabhāvasyaiva lakṣaṇam .. 12.7 ..
1.12.d:
विद्या काव्यं तथा शिल्पं सर्वं वाचावृतानि तु।
विद्यार्थाश्चोपतिष्ठन्ति प्रभावस्यैव लक्षणम् ॥ 12.7 ॥
1.12.m: Sciences, poetry, and crafts—all enclosed by speech— / and the objects of knowledge attend upon him; this is the mark of power.

1.12.s:
śrṛṇoti śabdān śrotavyān yojanānāṃ śatādapi.
sarvajñaśca vidhijñaśca yogī conmattavadbhavet .. 12.8 ..
1.12.d:
श्रृणोति शब्दान् श्रोतव्यान् योजनानां शतादपि।
सर्वज्ञश्च विधिज्ञश्च योगी चोन्मत्तवद्भवेत् ॥ 12.8 ॥
1.12.m: He hears audible sounds even from a hundred yojanas away. / All-knowing and knowing the rules, the yogin may become like a madman.

1.12.s:
yakṣarākṣasagandharvvān vīkṣate divyamānuṣān.
vetti tāṃśca mahāyogī upasargasya lakṣaṇam .. 12.9 ..
1.12.d:
यक्षराक्षसगन्धर्व्वान् वीक्षते दिव्यमानुषान्।
वेत्ति तांश्च महायोगी उपसर्गस्य लक्षणम् ॥ 12.9 ॥
1.12.m: He sees yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, celestial beings and humans; / and the great yogin knows them: this is the mark of an obstacle.

1.12.s:
devadānavagandharvān ṛṣīṃścāpi tathā pitṝn.
prekṣate sarvataścaiva unmattaṃ taṃ vinirddiśet .. 12.10 ..
1.12.d:
देवदानवगन्धर्वान् ऋषींश्चापि तथा पितॄन्।
प्रेक्षते सर्वतश्चैव उन्मत्तं तं विनिर्द्दिशेत् ॥ 12.10 ॥
1.12.m: He beholds gods, dānavas, gandharvas, seers, and ancestors, / and on every side: one should declare him mad.

1.12.s:
bhrameṇa bhrāmyate yogī codyamāno'ntarātmanā.
bhrameṇa bhrāntabuddhestu jñānaṃ sarvaṃ praṇaśyati .. 12.11 ..
1.12.d:
भ्रमेण भ्राम्यते योगी चोद्यमानोऽन्तरात्मना।
भ्रमेण भ्रान्तबुद्धेस्तु ज्ञानं सर्वं प्रणश्यति ॥ 12.11 ॥
1.12.m: The yogin wanders about in delusion, urged on by the inner self; / for one whose intellect is deluded by wandering, all knowledge perishes.

1.12.s:
vārttā nāśayate cittaṃ codyamāno'ntarātmanā.
varttanākrāntabuddhestu sarvaṃ jñānaṃ praṇaśyati .. 12.12 ..
1.12.d:
वार्त्ता नाशयते चित्तं चोद्यमानोऽन्तरात्मना।
वर्त्तनाक्रान्तबुद्धेस्तु सर्वं ज्ञानं प्रणश्यति ॥ 12.12 ॥
1.12.m: Tidings destroy his mind, as he is urged on by the inner self; / for one whose intellect is overcome by worldly affairs, all knowledge perishes.

1.12.s:
āvṛtya manasā śuklaṃ paṭaṃ vā kambalaṃ tathā.
tatastu paramaṃ brahma kṣipramevānucintayet .. 12.13 ..
1.12.d:
आवृत्य मनसा शुक्लं पटं वा कम्बलं तथा।
ततस्तु परमं ब्रह्म क्षिप्रमेवानुचिन्तयेत् ॥ 12.13 ॥
1.12.m: Having mentally covered [himself] with a white cloth or a woolen blanket, / he should then immediately meditate upon the supreme Brahman.

1.12.s:
tasmāccaivātmano doṣāṃstūpasargānupasthitān .
parita tyajeta medhāvī yadīcchet siddhimātmanaḥ .. 12.14 ..
1.12.d:
तस्माच्चैवात्मनो दोषांस्तूपसर्गानुपस्थितान् ।
परित त्यजेत मेधावी यदीच्छेत् सिद्धिमात्मनः ॥ 12.14 ॥
1.12.m: Therefore, the wise man, if he desires his own perfection, / should completely abandon the faults that belong to himself—the obstacles that have arisen.

1.12.s:
ṛṣayo devagandharvā yakṣoragamahāsurāḥ.
upasargeṣu saṃyuktā āvarttante punaḥ punaḥ .. 12.15 ..
1.12.d:
ऋषयो देवगन्धर्वा यक्षोरगमहासुराः।
उपसर्गेषु संयुक्ता आवर्त्तन्ते पुनः पुनः ॥ 12.15 ॥
1.12.m: Seers, gods, gandharvas, yakṣas, uragas, and great asuras, / attached to these obstacles, revolve again and again.

1.12.s:
tasmādyuktaḥ sadā yogī laghvāhārī jitendriyaḥ.
tathā suptaḥ susūkṣmeṣu dhāraṇāṃ mūrdhni dhārayet .. 12.16 ..
1.12.d:
तस्माद्युक्तः सदा योगी लघ्वाहारी जितेन्द्रियः।
तथा सुप्तः सुसूक्ष्मेषु धारणां मूर्ध्नि धारयेत् ॥ 12.16 ॥
1.12.m: Therefore, the yogin, ever disciplined, eating light food, with senses conquered, / thus resting in the very subtle [principles], should fix concentration in the head.

1.12.s:
tatastu yogayuktasya jitanidrasya yoginaḥ.
upasargāḥ punaścānte jāyante prāṇasaṃjñakāḥ .. 12.17 ..
1.12.d:
ततस्तु योगयुक्तस्य जितनिद्रस्य योगिनः।
उपसर्गाः पुनश्चान्ते जायन्ते प्राणसंज्ञकाः ॥ 12.17 ॥
1.12.m: Then, for the disciplined yogin who has conquered sleep, / obstacles known as vital breaths arise again at the end.

1.12.s:
pṛthivīṃ dhārayetsarvāṃ tataścāpo hyanantaram.
tato'gniñcaiva sarveṣāmākāśaṃ mana eva ca .. 12.18 ..
1.12.d:
पृथिवीं धारयेत्सर्वां ततश्चापो ह्यनन्तरम्।
ततोऽग्निञ्चैव सर्वेषामाकाशं मन एव च ॥ 12.18 ॥
1.12.m: He should hold concentration on all the earth, and immediately thereafter on water, / then on fire, and on space among all of them, and on the mind.

1.12.s:
tataḥ parāṃ punarbuddhiṃ dhārayedyatnato yatī.
kiddhīnāñcaiva liṅgāni dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā parityajet .. 12.19 ..
1.12.d:
ततः परां पुनर्बुद्धिं धारयेद्यत्नतो यती।
किद्धीनाञ्चैव लिङ्गानि दृष्ट्वा दृष्ट्वा परित्यजेत् ॥ 12.19 ॥
1.12.m: Then, the striving ascetic should diligently hold concentration on the supreme intellect; / seeing again and again the marks of the psychic powers, he should abandon them.

1.12.s:
pṛthvīṃ dhārayamāṇasya mahī sūkṣmā pravartate.
apo dhārayamāṇasya āpaḥ sūkṣmā bhavanti hi.
śītā rasāḥ pravarttante sūkṣmā hyamṛtasannibhāḥ .. 12.20 ..
1.12.d:
पृथ्वीं धारयमाणस्य मही सूक्ष्मा प्रवर्तते।
अपो धारयमाणस्य आपः सूक्ष्मा भवन्ति हि।
शीता रसाः प्रवर्त्तन्ते सूक्ष्मा ह्यमृतसन्निभाः ॥ 12.20 ॥
1.12.m: For him holding concentration on the earth, the subtle earth arises. / For him holding concentration on water, the subtle waters indeed arise: / cool saps arise, subtle, resembling nectar.

1.12.s:
tejo dhārayamāṇasya tejaḥ sūkṣmā pravarttate.
ātmānaṃ manyate tejastadbhāvamanupaśyati .. 12.21 ..
1.12.d:
तेजो धारयमाणस्य तेजः सूक्ष्मा प्रवर्त्तते।
आत्मानं मन्यते तेजस्तद्भावमनुपश्यति ॥ 12.21 ॥
1.12.m: For him holding concentration on fire, the subtle fire arises. / He considers himself to be fire and perceives its nature.

1.12.s:
ātmānaṃ manyate vāyuṃ vāyuvanmaṇḍalaṃ prabho .
ākāśaṃ dhārayāṇasya vyoma sūkṣmaṃ pravarttate .. 12.22 ..
1.12.d:
आत्मानं मन्यते वायुं वायुवन्मण्डलं प्रभो ।
आकाशं धारयाणस्य व्योम सूक्ष्मं प्रवर्त्तते ॥ 12.22 ॥
1.12.m: He considers himself to be wind, like the circle of the wind, O lord. / For him holding concentration on space, subtle space arises.

1.12.s:
paśyate maṇḍalaṃ sūkṣmaṃ ghoṣaścāsya pravarttate .
ātmānaṃ manyate nityaṃ vāyuḥ sūkṣmaḥ pravarttate .. 12.23 ..
1.12.d:
पश्यते मण्डलं सूक्ष्मं घोषश्चास्य प्रवर्त्तते ।
आत्मानं मन्यते नित्यं वायुः सूक्ष्मः प्रवर्त्तते ॥ 12.23 ॥
1.12.m: He beholds a subtle circle, and a roar arises for him; / he constantly considers himself to be the subtle wind that arises.

1.12.s:
tathā mano dhārayato manaḥ sūkṣmaṃ pravarttate .
manasā sarvabhūtānāṃ manastu viśate hi saḥ.
buddhyā buddhiṃ yadā yuñjettadā vijñāya buddhayate .. 12.24 ..
1.12.d:
तथा मनो धारयतो मनः सूक्ष्मं प्रवर्त्तते ।
मनसा सर्वभूतानां मनस्तु विशते हि सः।
बुद्ध्या बुद्धिं यदा युञ्जेत्तदा विज्ञाय बुद्धयते ॥ 12.24 ॥
1.12.m: Likewise, for him holding concentration on the mind, the subtle mind arises; / with his mind, he enters into the minds of all beings. / When he unites his intellect with the [cosmic] intellect, having known it, he awakens.

1.12.s:
etāni sapta sūkṣmāṇi viditvā yastu yogavit.
parityajati medhāvī sa buddhyā paramaṃ vrajet .. 12.25 ..
1.12.d:
एतानि सप्त सूक्ष्माणि विदित्वा यस्तु योगवित्।
परित्यजति मेधावी स बुद्ध्या परमं व्रजेत् ॥ 12.25 ॥
1.12.m: Having known these seven subtle [principles], the wise knower of yoga / who abandons them with his intellect attains the Supreme.

1.12.s:
yasmin yasmiṃśca saṃyukto bhūta aiśvaryalakṣaṇe.
tatraiva saṅgaṃ bhajate tenaiva pravinaśyati .. 12.26 ..
1.12.d:
यस्मिन् यस्मिंश्च संयुक्तो भूत ऐश्वर्यलक्षणे।
तत्रैव सङ्गं भजते तेनैव प्रविनश्यति ॥ 12.26 ॥
1.12.m: Whatever [elemental] being characterized by sovereign power he is attached to, / in that very one he experiences attachment, and by that very one he perishes.

1.12.s:
tasmādviditvā sūkṣmāṇi saṃsaktāni parasparam.
parityajati yobuddhyā sa paraṃ prapnuyāddvijaḥ .. 12.27 ..
1.12.d:
तस्माद्विदित्वा सूक्ष्माणि संसक्तानि परस्परम्।
परित्यजति योबुद्ध्या स परं प्रप्नुयाद्द्विजः ॥ 12.27 ॥
1.12.m: Therefore, having known the subtle [principles] interconnected with one another, / the twice-born who abandons them with his intellect attains the Supreme.

1.12.s:
dṛśyante hi mahātmāna ṛṣayo divyacakṣuṣaḥ.
saṃsaktāḥ sūkṣmabhāveṣu te doṣāsteṣu saṃjñitāḥ..12.28
tasmānna niścayaḥ kāryaḥ sūkṣmeṣviha kadācana.
aiśvaryājjāyate rāgo virāgaṃ brahma cocyate .. 12.29 ..
1.12.d:
दृश्यन्ते हि महात्मान ऋषयो दिव्यचक्षुषः।
संसक्ताः सूक्ष्मभावेषु ते दोषास्तेषु संज्ञिताः॥12.28
तस्मान्न निश्चयः कार्यः सूक्ष्मेष्विह कदाचन।
ऐश्वर्याज्जायते रागो विरागं ब्रह्म चोच्यते ॥ 12.29 ॥
1.12.m:
For even great-souled seers with divine vision are seen
to be attached to subtle states; those are designated as flaws in them.

Therefore, no certainty should ever be placed here in subtle things.
From sovereign power passion is born, and detachment is said to be Brahman.

1.12.s:
viditvā sapta sūkṣmāṇi ṣaḍaṅgañca maheśvaram.
pradhānaṃ viniyogajñaḥ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati .. 12.30 ..
1.12.d:
विदित्वा सप्त सूक्ष्माणि षडङ्गञ्च महेश्वरम्।
प्रधानं विनियोगज्ञः परं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति ॥ 12.30 ॥
1.12.m: Knowing the seven subtle [principles] and the six-limbed Maheśvara, / the knower of application, [transcending] the Pradhāna, attains the supreme Brahman.

1.12.s:
sarvajñatā tṛptiranādibodhaḥ svatantratā nityamaluptaśaktiḥ.
anantaśaktiśca vibhorvidhijñāḥ ṣaḍāhuraṅgāni maheśvarasya .. 12.31 ..
1.12.d:
सर्वज्ञता तृप्तिरनादिबोधः स्वतन्त्रता नित्यमलुप्तशक्तिः।
अनन्तशक्तिश्च विभोर्विधिज्ञाः षडाहुरङ्गानि महेश्वरस्य ॥ 12.31 ॥
1.12.m: Omniscience, contentment, beginningless understanding, independence, ever-unfailing power, / and infinite capacity of the Lord: those who know the rules declare these to be the six limbs of Maheśvara.

1.12.s:
nityaṃ brahmadhano yukta upasargaiḥ pramucyate.
jitaśvāsopasargasya jitarāmasya yoginaḥ.
ekā bahiḥśarīre'smin dhāraṇā sarvakāmikī .. 12.32 ..
1.12.d:
नित्यं ब्रह्मधनो युक्त उपसर्गैः प्रमुच्यते।
जितश्वासोपसर्गस्य जितरामस्य योगिनः।
एका बहिःशरीरेऽस्मिन् धारणा सर्वकामिकी ॥ 12.32 ॥
1.12.m: Disciplined, constantly possessing Brahman as his wealth, he is freed from obstacles. / For the yogin who has overcome the obstacles of breath and conquered pleasure, / a single concentration outside this body fulfills all desires.

1.12.s:
viśedyadā dvijo yukto yatra yatrārppayenmanaḥ .
bhūtānyāviśate vāpi trailokyañcāpi kampayet .. 12.33 ..
1.12.d:
विशेद्यदा द्विजो युक्तो यत्र यत्रार्प्पयेन्मनः ।
भूतान्याविशते वापि त्रैलोक्यञ्चापि कम्पयेत् ॥ 12.33 ॥
1.12.m: Whenever the disciplined twice-born enters wherever he directs his mind, / he enters into beings, or he could shake the three worlds.

1.12.s:
etayā praviśeddehaṃ hitvā dehaṃ punastviha.
manodvāraṃ hi yogānāmādityañca vinirddiśet .. 12.34 ..
1.12.d:
एतया प्रविशेद्देहं हित्वा देहं पुनस्त्विह।
मनोद्वारं हि योगानामादित्यञ्च विनिर्द्दिशेत् ॥ 12.34 ॥
1.12.m: By this [concentration] he may enter a body, leaving behind a body here once more. / For one should indicate the mind as the door of yogas, and Āditya as well.

1.12.s:
ādānādikriyāṇāntu āditya iti cocyate.
etena vidhinā yogī viraktaḥ sūkṣmavarjjitaḥ.
prakṛtiṃ samatikramya rudraloke mahīyate .. 12.35 ..
1.12.d:
आदानादिक्रियाणान्तु आदित्य इति चोच्यते।
एतेन विधिना योगी विरक्तः सूक्ष्मवर्ज्जितः।
प्रकृतिं समतिक्रम्य रुद्रलोके महीयते ॥ 12.35 ॥
1.12.m: Because of actions such as taking up, he is called Āditya. / By this method, the yogin, detached and free from the subtle [principles], / having fully transcended primal matter, is glorified in the world of Rudra.

1.12.s:
aiśvaryaguṇasamprāptaṃ brahmabhūtantu taṃ prabhum.
devasthāneṣu sarveṣu sarvatastu nivarttate .. 12.36 ..
1.12.d:
ऐश्वर्यगुणसम्प्राप्तं ब्रह्मभूतन्तु तं प्रभुम्।
देवस्थानेषु सर्वेषु सर्वतस्तु निवर्त्तते ॥ 12.36 ॥
1.12.m: When that lord has attained the qualities of sovereign power and has become Brahman, / he turns away completely from all the abodes of the gods.

1.12.s:
paiśācāṃśacava piśācāṃśca rākṣasena ca rākṣasān .
gāndharveṇa ca gandharvān kaubereṇa kuberajān .. 12.37 ..
1.12.d:
पैशाचांशचव पिशाचांश्च राक्षसेन च राक्षसान् ।
गान्धर्वेण च गन्धर्वान् कौबेरेण कुबेरजान् ॥ 12.37 ॥
1.12.m: [Subduing] the piśācas by the Piśāca abode, and the rākṣasas by the Rākṣasa [abode], / and the gandharvas by the Gāndharva [abode], the descendants of Kubera by the Kaubera [abode],

1.12.s:
indramaindreṇa sthānena saumyaṃ saumyena caiva hi.
prajāpatiṃ tathā caiva prājāpatyena sādhayet .. 12.38 ..
1.12.d:
इन्द्रमैन्द्रेण स्थानेन सौम्यं सौम्येन चैव हि।
प्रजापतिं तथा चैव प्राजापत्येन साधयेत् ॥ 12.38 ॥
1.12.m: Indra by the Aindra abode, and Soma by the Saumya [abode], / and likewise he should master Prajāpati by the Prājāpatya [abode],

1.12.s:
brāhmaṃ brāhyena cāpyevamupāmantrayate prabhum.
tatra saktastu unmattastasmātsarvaṃ pravarttate .. 12.39 ..
1.12.d:
ब्राह्मं ब्राह्येन चाप्येवमुपामन्त्रयते प्रभुम्।
तत्र सक्तस्तु उन्मत्तस्तस्मात्सर्वं प्रवर्त्तते ॥ 12.39 ॥
1.12.m: and thus, by the Brāhma [abode], he addresses the Lord. / Attached to that, he is mad; from that, everything proceeds.

1.12.s:
nityaṃ brahmaparo yuktaḥ sthānānyetāni vai tyajet .
asajyamānaḥ sthāneṣu dvijaḥ sarvagato bhavet .. 12.40 ..
1.12.d:
नित्यं ब्रह्मपरो युक्तः स्थानान्येतानि वै त्यजेत् ।
असज्यमानः स्थानेषु द्विजः सर्वगतो भवेत् ॥ 12.40 ॥
1.12.m: Ever devoted to Brahman, disciplined, he should indeed abandon these abodes; / remaining unattached to these abodes, the twice-born becomes omnipresent.

1.12.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte yogopasarganirūpaṇaṃ nāma dvādaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 12 ..
1.12.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते योगोपसर्गनिरूपणं नाम द्वादशोऽध्यायः ॥ 12 ॥
1.12.m: Thus ends the twelfth chapter, named 'Determination of Yogic Obstacles', in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.13.s: .. vāyuruvāca ..
1.13.d: ॥ वायुरुवाच ॥
1.13.m:
Vāyu said:
Hereafter I shall explain the details of the qualities of sovereign power,
by which specific yoga one may transcend all worlds.

1.13.s:
ata ūrddhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi aiśvaryaguṇa vistaram.
yena yogaviśeṣeṇa sarvalokānatikramet .. 13.1 ..
1.13.d:
अत ऊर्द्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि ऐश्वर्यगुण विस्तरम्।
येन योगविशेषेण सर्वलोकानतिक्रमेत् ॥ 13.1 ॥

1.13.s:
tatrāṣṭaguṇamaiśvaryaṃ yogināṃ samudāhṛtam.
tatsarvaṃ kramayogena ucyamānaṃ nibodhata .. 13.2 ..
1.13.d:
तत्राष्टगुणमैश्वर्यं योगिनां समुदाहृतम्।
तत्सर्वं क्रमयोगेन उच्यमानं निबोधत ॥ 13.2 ॥
1.13.m: In this regard, an eightfold sovereign power has been proclaimed for yogins; / learn all of that as it is spoken in proper order.

1.13.s:
aṇimā laghimā caiva mahimā prāptireva ca.
prākāmyajcaiva sarvatra īśitvañcaiva sarvataḥ .. 13.3 ..
1.13.d:
अणिमा लघिमा चैव महिमा प्राप्तिरेव च।
प्राकाम्यज्चैव सर्वत्र ईशित्वञ्चैव सर्वतः ॥ 13.3 ॥
1.13.m: Aṇimā, laghimā, mahimā, prāpti, / prākāmya everywhere, and īśitva over all,

1.13.s:
vaśitvamatha sarvatra yatra kāmāvasāyitā.
taccāpi vividhaṃ jñeyamaiśvaryaṃ sarvakāmikam .. 13.4 ..
1.13.d:
वशित्वमथ सर्वत्र यत्र कामावसायिता।
तच्चापि विविधं ज्ञेयमैश्वर्यं सर्वकामिकम् ॥ 13.4 ॥
1.13.m: vaśitva everywhere, and yatra-kāmāvasāyitā: / that multifaceted sovereign power should be known as fulfilling all desires.

1.13.s:
sāvadyaṃ niravadyaṃ ca sūkṣmañcaiva pravarttate.
sāvadyaṃ nāma tattattvaṃ pañcabhūtātmakaṃ smṛtam .. 13.5 ..
1.13.d:
सावद्यं निरवद्यं च सूक्ष्मञ्चैव प्रवर्त्तते।
सावद्यं नाम तत्तत्त्वं पञ्चभूतात्मकं स्मृतम् ॥ 13.5 ॥
1.13.m: It operates as flawed, flawless, and subtle. / The principle called flawed is remembered as consisting of the five gross elements.

1.13.s:
niravadyaṃ tathā nāma pañcabhūtātmakaṃ smṛtam.
indriyāṇi manaścaiva ahahkāraśca vai smṛtam .. 13.6 ..
1.13.d:
निरवद्यं तथा नाम पञ्चभूतात्मकं स्मृतम्।
इन्द्रियाणि मनश्चैव अहह्कारश्च वै स्मृतम् ॥ 13.6 ॥
1.13.m: The principle called flawless is likewise remembered as consisting of the five gross elements, / the senses, the mind, and the ego-sense.

1.13.s:
tatra sūkṣmapravṛttantu pañcabhūtātmakaṃ punaḥ.
indriyāṇi manaścaiva buddhyahaṅkāra saṃjñitam .. 13.7 ..
1.13.d:
तत्र सूक्ष्मप्रवृत्तन्तु पञ्चभूतात्मकं पुनः।
इन्द्रियाणि मनश्चैव बुद्ध्यहङ्कार संज्ञितम् ॥ 13.7 ॥
1.13.m: There, operating as subtle, it is again comprised of the five gross elements, / the senses, the mind, and that which is designated intellect and ego-sense.

1.13.s:
tathā sarvamayañcaiva ātmasthā khyātireva ca.
saṃyoga evaṃ tripidhaḥ sūkṣmeṣveva pravarttate .. 13.8 ..
1.13.d:
तथा सर्वमयञ्चैव आत्मस्था ख्यातिरेव च।
संयोग एवं त्रिपिधः सूक्ष्मेष्वेव प्रवर्त्तते ॥ 13.8 ॥
1.13.m: Likewise, it consists of all things, and perception resting in the self; / thus, threefold contact operates in the subtle [principles] alone.

1.13.s:
punaraṣṭaguṇasyāpi teṣvevātha pravarttate.
tasya rūpaṃ pravakṣyāmi yathāha bhagavān prabhuḥ .. 13.9 ..
1.13.d:
पुनरष्टगुणस्यापि तेष्वेवाथ प्रवर्त्तते।
तस्य रूपं प्रवक्ष्यामि यथाह भगवान् प्रभुः ॥ 13.9 ॥
1.13.m: Moreover, of the eightfold [power] too, it operates only in them; / I shall explain its nature as the blessed Lord has spoken.

1.13.s:
trailokye sarvabūteṣu jīvasyāniyataḥ smṛtaḥ.
aṇimā ca yathāvyaktaṃ sarvaṃ yatra pratiṣṭhitam .. 13.10 ..
1.13.d:
त्रैलोक्ये सर्वबूतेषु जीवस्यानियतः स्मृतः।
अणिमा च यथाव्यक्तं सर्वं यत्र प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ 13.10 ॥
1.13.m: In the three worlds, among all living beings, the individual soul is considered indeterminate; / and aṇimā is like the unmanifest, wherein everything is established.

1.13.s:
trailokye sarvabhūtānāṃ duṣprāpyaṃ samudāhṛtam.
taccāpi bhavati prāpyaṃ prathamaṃ yogināṃ balāt .. 13.11 ..
1.13.d:
त्रैलोक्ये सर्वभूतानां दुष्प्राप्यं समुदाहृतम्।
तच्चापि भवति प्राप्यं प्रथमं योगिनां बलात् ॥ 13.11 ॥
1.13.m: It is declared difficult to obtain for all beings in the three worlds; / yet that very state is the first to be attained by yogins through their power.

1.13.s:
lambanaṃ plavanaṃ yoge rūpamasya sadā bhavet .
śīghragaṃ sarvabhūteṣu dvitīyaṃ tatpadaṃ smṛtam .. 13.12 ..
1.13.d:
लम्बनं प्लवनं योगे रूपमस्य सदा भवेत् ।
शीघ्रगं सर्वभूतेषु द्वितीयं तत्पदं स्मृतम् ॥ 13.12 ॥
1.13.m: Hanging down and leaping in yoga is always its form; / moving swiftly among all beings, that is recorded as the second stage.

1.13.s:
trailokye sarvabhūtānāṃ prāptiḥ prākāmyameva ca.
mahimā cāpi yo yasmiṃstṛtīyo yoga ucyate .. 13.13 ..
1.13.d:
त्रैलोक्ये सर्वभूतानां प्राप्तिः प्राकाम्यमेव च।
महिमा चापि यो यस्मिंस्तृतीयो योग उच्यते ॥ 13.13 ॥
1.13.m: The third yoga is spoken of as that in which / there is prāpti, prākāmya, and mahimā in all beings in the three worlds.

1.13.s:
trailokye sarvabhūteṣu trailokyamagamaṃ smṛtam.
prakāmān viṣayān bhuṅkte na ca pratihataḥ vkacit .
trailokye sarvabhūtānāṃ sukhaduḥkhaṃ prakarttate .. 13.14 ..
1.13.d:
त्रैलोक्ये सर्वभूतेषु त्रैलोक्यमगमं स्मृतम्।
प्रकामान् विषयान् भुङ्क्ते न च प्रतिहतः व्कचित् ।
त्रैलोक्ये सर्वभूतानां सुखदुःखं प्रकर्त्तते ॥ 13.14 ॥
1.13.m: Among all beings in the three worlds, it is considered able to go anywhere in the three worlds. / He enjoys objects of desire at will and is never obstructed anywhere; / he produces pleasure and pain for all beings in the three worlds.

1.13.s:
īśo bhavati sarvatra pravibhāgena yogavit.
vaśyāni caiva bhūtāni trailokye sacarācare.
bhavanti sarvakāryeṣu icchato na bhavanti ca .. 13.15 ..
1.13.d:
ईशो भवति सर्वत्र प्रविभागेन योगवित्।
वश्यानि चैव भूतानि त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे।
भवन्ति सर्वकार्येषु इच्छतो न भवन्ति च ॥ 13.15 ॥
1.13.m: The knower of yoga becomes the master everywhere according to division; / and living beings in the three worlds, moving and unmoving, are subject to his will; / at his wish they come into being in all undertakings, and at his wish they do not.

1.13.s:
yatra kāmāvasāyitvaṃ trailokye sacarācare.
icchayā cendriyāṇi syuḥ bhavanti na bhavanti ca .. 13.16 ..
1.13.d:
यत्र कामावसायित्वं त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे।
इच्छया चेन्द्रियाणि स्युः भवन्ति न भवन्ति च ॥ 13.16 ॥
1.13.m: Where there is kāmāvasāyitā in the three worlds, moving and unmoving, / the sense-faculties exist by his wish, and by his wish they come to be or cease to be.

1.13.s:
śabdaḥ sparśo raso gandho rūpaṃ caiva mana stathā.
pravarttante'sya cecchāto na bhavanti tathecchayā .. 13.17 ..
1.13.d:
शब्दः स्पर्शो रसो गन्धो रूपं चैव मन स्तथा।
प्रवर्त्तन्तेऽस्य चेच्छातो न भवन्ति तथेच्छया ॥ 13.17 ॥
1.13.m: Sound, touch, taste, smell, and form, as well as the mind, / proceed at his desire, and likewise at his desire they cease to exist.

1.13.s:
na jāyate na mriyate bhidyate na ca chidyate.
na dahyate na muhyate hīyate na ca lipyate .. 13.18 ..
1.13.d:
न जायते न म्रियते भिद्यते न च छिद्यते।
न दह्यते न मुह्यते हीयते न च लिप्यते ॥ 13.18 ॥
1.13.m: He is neither born nor dies; he is neither broken nor cut; / he is not burned, he is not deluded; he does not diminish, nor is he tainted.

1.13.s:
na kṣīyate na kṣarati na khidyati kadācana.
kriyate caiva sarvatra tathā vikriyate na ca .. 13.19 ..
1.13.d:
न क्षीयते न क्षरति न खिद्यति कदाचन।
क्रियते चैव सर्वत्र तथा विक्रियते न च ॥ 13.19 ॥
1.13.m: He is not exhausted, he does not fall away, nor is he ever distressed; / he is produced everywhere, and yet he undergoes no alteration.

1.13.s:
agandharasarūpastu sparśaśabdavivarjjitaḥ.
avarṇo hyavaraścaiva tathā varṇasya karhicit .. 13.20 ..
1.13.d:
अगन्धरसरूपस्तु स्पर्शशब्दविवर्ज्जितः।
अवर्णो ह्यवरश्चैव तथा वर्णस्य कर्हिचित् ॥ 13.20 ॥
1.13.m: Deceit of smell, taste, and form, devoid of touch and sound, / colorless and uninferior, he is never of any caste or color.

1.13.s:
bhuṅkte'tha viṣayāṃścaiva viṣayairnna ca yujyate.
jñātvā tu paramaṃ sūkṣmaṃ sūkṣmatvāccāpavargakaḥ .. 13.21 ..
1.13.d:
भुङ्क्तेऽथ विषयांश्चैव विषयैर्न्न च युज्यते।
ज्ञात्वा तु परमं सूक्ष्मं सूक्ष्मत्वाच्चापवर्गकः ॥ 13.21 ॥
1.13.m: He experiences sense-objects and yet is not bound by sense-objects; / having known the supreme subtlety, through subtlety he attains liberation.

1.13.s:
vyāpakastvapavargācca vyāpitvātpuruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ.
