puruṣaḥ sūkṣmabhāvāttu aiśvarye parataḥ sthitaḥ .. 13.22 ..
1.13.d:
व्यापकस्त्वपवर्गाच्च व्यापित्वात्पुरुषः स्मृतः।
पुरुषः सूक्ष्मभावात्तु ऐश्वर्ये परतः स्थितः ॥ 13.22 ॥
1.13.m: He is all-pervading through liberation, and because of his pervasiveness he is called puruṣa. / Through his state of subtlety, the puruṣa is situated beyond sovereign power.

1.13.s:
guṇāntarantu aiśvarye sarvataḥ sūkṣma ucyate.
aiśvaryyamapratīghāti prāpya yogamanuttamam.
apavargaṃ tato gacchet susūkṣmaṃ paramaṃ padam .. 13.23 ..
1.13.d:
गुणान्तरन्तु ऐश्वर्ये सर्वतः सूक्ष्म उच्यते।
ऐश्वर्य्यमप्रतीघाति प्राप्य योगमनुत्तमम्।
अपवर्गं ततो गच्छेत् सुसूक्ष्मं परमं पदम् ॥ 13.23 ॥
1.13.m: In sovereign power, he is said to be subtle everywhere with respect to other qualities. / Having obtained unopposed sovereign power and unexcelled yoga, / he goes then to liberation, the exceedingly subtle supreme abode.

1.13.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprākte yogaiśvaryāṇi nāma trayodaśodhyāyaḥ .. 13 ...
1.13.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्राक्ते योगैश्वर्याणि नाम त्रयोदशोध्यायः ॥ 13 ॥।
1.13.m: Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, named "The Powers of Yoga," in the holy Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.14.s: .. vāyuruvāca ..
1.14.d: ॥ वायुरुवाच ॥

1.14.s:
na caivamāgato jñānādrāgāt karmma samācaret.
rājasaṃ tāmasaṃ vāpi bhuktvā tatraiva yujyate .. 14.1 ..
1.14.d:
न चैवमागतो ज्ञानाद्रागात् कर्म्म समाचरेत्।
राजसं तामसं वापि भुक्त्वा तत्रैव युज्यते ॥ 14.1 ॥

1.14.s:
tathā sukṛtakarmmā tu phalaṃ svarge samaśrute.
tasmāt sthānāt punarbhraṣṭo mānuṣyamanupadyate .. 14.2 ..
1.14.d:
तथा सुकृतकर्म्मा तु फलं स्वर्गे समश्रुते।
तस्मात् स्थानात् पुनर्भ्रष्टो मानुष्यमनुपद्यते ॥ 14.2 ॥
1.14.m: Likewise, a person of meritorious deeds enjoys the fruit in heaven; / fallen again from that place, he falls back into human existence.

1.14.s:
tasmādbrahma paraṃ sūkṣmaṃ brahma śāśvatamucyate.
brahma eva hi seveta brahmaiva paramaṃ sukham .. 14.3 ..
1.14.d:
तस्माद्ब्रह्म परं सूक्ष्मं ब्रह्म शाश्वतमुच्यते।
ब्रह्म एव हि सेवेत ब्रह्मैव परमं सुखम् ॥ 14.3 ॥
1.14.m: Therefore Brahman is spoken of as supreme, subtle, and eternal; / one should resort only to Brahman, for Brahman alone is supreme bliss.

1.14.s:
pariśramastu yajñānāṃ mahatārthena varttate.
bhūyo mṛtyuvaśaṃ yāti tasmānmokṣaḥ paraṃ sukham .. 14.4 ..
1.14.d:
परिश्रमस्तु यज्ञानां महतार्थेन वर्त्तते।
भूयो मृत्युवशं याति तस्मान्मोक्षः परं सुखम् ॥ 14.4 ॥
1.14.m: The exhaustion of sacrifices exists for the sake of a great purpose; / yet one falls again under the sway of death, therefore liberation is supreme bliss.

1.14.s:
atha vai dhyānasaṃyukto brahmayajñaparāyaṇaḥ .
na sa syād vyāpituṃ śakyo manvantaraśatairapi .. 14.5 ..
1.14.d:
अथ वै ध्यानसंयुक्तो ब्रह्मयज्ञपरायणः ।
न स स्याद् व्यापितुं शक्यो मन्वन्तरशतैरपि ॥ 14.5 ॥
1.14.m: Now, one devoted to meditation and intent on the sacrifice of Brahman / cannot be pervaded even in hundreds of cosmic ages of a Manu.

1.14.s:
dṛṣṭvā tu puruṣaṃ divyaṃ viśvākhyaṃ viśvarūpiṇam.
viśvapāda śirogrīvaṃ viśveśaṃ viśvabhāvanam.
viśvagandhaṃ viśvamālyaṃ viśvāmbaradharaṃ prabhum .. 14.6 ..
1.14.d:
दृष्ट्वा तु पुरुषं दिव्यं विश्वाख्यं विश्वरूपिणम्।
विश्वपाद शिरोग्रीवं विश्वेशं विश्वभावनम्।
विश्वगन्धं विश्वमाल्यं विश्वाम्बरधरं प्रभुम् ॥ 14.6 ॥
1.14.m: Having beheld the divine Puruṣa, called the All, having the universe as his form, / whose feet, head, and neck are the universe, the lord of the universe, creator of the universe, / the fragrance of the universe, wearing the garland of the universe, the Lord robed in the universe;

1.14.s:
gobhirmahī saṃyatate patatriṇaṃ mahātmānaṃ paramamatiṃ vareṇyam.
kaviṃ purāṇamanuśāsitāraṃ sūkṣmācca sūkṣmaṃ mahato mahāntam.
yogena paśyanti na cakṣuṣā taṃ nirindriyaṃ puruṣaṃ rukmavarṇam .. 14.7 ..
1.14.d:
गोभिर्मही संयतते पतत्रिणं महात्मानं परममतिं वरेण्यम्।
कविं पुराणमनुशासितारं सूक्ष्माच्च सूक्ष्मं महतो महान्तम्।
योगेन पश्यन्ति न चक्षुषा तं निरिन्द्रियं पुरुषं रुक्मवर्णम् ॥ 14.7 ॥
1.14.m: Whom the earth serves with rays of light, the bird, the great Self, the supreme intellect, the most worthy of choice, / the ancient sage, the ruler, subtler than the subtle, greater than the great; / through yoga they behold him who has no sense-organs, the golden-hued Puruṣa, and not with the eye;

1.14.s:
aliṅginaṃ puruṣaṃ rukmavarṇaṃ saliṅginaṃ nirguṇaṃ cetanaṃ ca.
nityaṃ sadā sarvagatantu śaucaṃ paśyanti yuktyā hyacalaṃ prakāśam .. 14.8 ..
1.14.d:
अलिङ्गिनं पुरुषं रुक्मवर्णं सलिङ्गिनं निर्गुणं चेतनं च।
नित्यं सदा सर्वगतन्तु शौचं पश्यन्ति युक्त्या ह्यचलं प्रकाशम् ॥ 14.8 ॥
1.14.m: The Puruṣa without marks, golden-hued, yet possessing marks, devoid of qualities, conscious, / eternal, ever all-pervading, pure, immovable light, they see through yoga.

1.14.s:
tadbhāvitastejasā dīpyamānaḥ apāṇipādodarapārśvajihvaḥ.
atīndriyo'dyāpi susūkṣma ekaḥ paśyatyacakṣuḥ sa śrṛṇotyakarṇaḥ .. 14.9 ..
1.14.d:
तद्भावितस्तेजसा दीप्यमानः अपाणिपादोदरपार्श्वजिह्वः।
अतीन्द्रियोऽद्यापि सुसूक्ष्म एकः पश्यत्यचक्षुः स श्रृणोत्यकर्णः ॥ 14.9 ॥
1.14.m: Imbued with that, blazing with splendor, without hands, feet, belly, sides, or tongue, / beyond the senses, even now exceedingly subtle, one, he sees without eyes, he hears without ears.

1.14.s:
nāsyāstyabuddhaṃ na ca buddhirasti sa veda sarvaṃ na ca vedavedyaḥ.
tamāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāntaṃ sacetanaṃ sarvvagataṃ susūkṣmam .. 14.10 ..
1.14.d:
नास्यास्त्यबुद्धं न च बुद्धिरस्ति स वेद सर्वं न च वेदवेद्यः।
तमाहुरग्र्यं पुरुषं महान्तं सचेतनं सर्व्वगतं सुसूक्ष्मम् ॥ 14.10 ॥
1.14.m: There is nothing ungrasped by him, yet he has no intellect; he knows all, but he is not known by the Veda. / They call him the foremost, the great Puruṣa, conscious, all-pervading, and exceedingly subtle.

1.14.s:
tāmāhurmunayaḥ sarvve loke prasavadharmiṇīm.
prakṛtiṃ sarvvabhūtānāṃ yuktāḥ paśyanti cetasā .. 14.11 ..
1.14.d:
तामाहुर्मुनयः सर्व्वे लोके प्रसवधर्मिणीम्।
प्रकृतिं सर्व्वभूतानां युक्ताः पश्यन्ति चेतसा ॥ 14.11 ॥
1.14.m: All the sages call her, in the world, the one whose nature is procreation; / those united in yoga see in their minds primal matter, [the mother] of all beings.

1.14.s:
sarvvataḥ pāṇipādāntaṃ sarvvato'kṣiśiromukham.
sarvvataḥ śruti (ma) mām̐lloke sarvvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati .. 14.12 ..
1.14.d:
सर्व्वतः पाणिपादान्तं सर्व्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम्।
सर्व्वतः श्रुति (म) माम्̐ल्लोके सर्व्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥ 14.12 ॥
1.14.m: With hands and feet on all sides, with eyes, heads, and faces on all sides, / with ears on all sides in the world, he stands encompassing everything.

1.14.s:
yuktā yogena ceśānaṃ sarvvataśca sanātanam.
puruṣaṃ sarvvabhūtānāṃ tasmāddhyātā na muhyate .. 14.13 ..
1.14.d:
युक्ता योगेन चेशानं सर्व्वतश्च सनातनम्।
पुरुषं सर्व्वभूतानां तस्माद्ध्याता न मुह्यते ॥ 14.13 ॥
1.14.m: Those united through yoga [see] the eternal Lord on every side, / the Puruṣa of all living beings; therefore the meditator is not deluded.

1.14.s:
bhūtātmānaṃ mahātmānaṃ paramātmānamavyayam.
sarvvātmānaṃ paraṃ brahma tadvai dhyātvā na muhyati .. 14.14 ..
1.14.d:
भूतात्मानं महात्मानं परमात्मानमव्ययम्।
सर्व्वात्मानं परं ब्रह्म तद्वै ध्यात्वा न मुह्यति ॥ 14.14 ॥
1.14.m: The inner self of all beings, the great Self, the supreme Self, imperishable, / the Self of all, the supreme Brahman—having meditated indeed on that, he is not deluded.

1.14.s:
pavano hi yathā grāhyo vicaran sarvvamūrtiṣu.
puri śete tathābhre ca tasmāt puruṣa ucyate.
atha celluptadharmmāttu saviśeṣaiśca karmmābhiḥ .. 14.15 ..
1.14.d:
पवनो हि यथा ग्राह्यो विचरन् सर्व्वमूर्तिषु।
पुरि शेते तथाभ्रे च तस्मात् पुरुष उच्यते।
अथ चेल्लुप्तधर्म्मात्तु सविशेषैश्च कर्म्माभिः ॥ 14.15 ॥
1.14.m: For just as the wind is grasped as moving in all forms, / so he rests in the city [of the body] and in space; therefore he is called puruṣa. / But if his dharma has lapsed due to distinctive actions,

1.14.s:
tatastu brahma yonyāṃ vai śukraśoṇitasaṃyutam.
strīpumāṃsaprayogeṇa jāyate hi punaḥ punaḥ .. 14.16 ..
1.14.d:
ततस्तु ब्रह्म योन्यां वै शुक्रशोणितसंयुतम्।
स्त्रीपुमांसप्रयोगेण जायते हि पुनः पुनः ॥ 14.16 ॥
1.14.m: then indeed Brahman, combined with semen and menstrual blood in the womb / by the union of female and male, is born again and again.

1.14.s:
tatastu garbhakāle tu kalanaṃ nāma jāyate.
kālena kalanañcāpi budbudaśca prajāyate .. 14.17 ..
1.14.d:
ततस्तु गर्भकाले तु कलनं नाम जायते।
कालेन कलनञ्चापि बुद्बुदश्च प्रजायते ॥ 14.17 ॥
1.14.m: Then at the time of gestation, what is called the embryo's mass (kalana) arises; / and in course of time, out of that mass, a bubble is produced.

1.14.s:
mṛtpiṇḍastu yathā cakre cakravātena pīḍitaḥ.
hastābhyāṃ kriyamāṇastu viśvatvamupagacchati .. 14.18 ..
1.14.d:
मृत्पिण्डस्तु यथा चक्रे चक्रवातेन पीडितः।
हस्ताभ्यां क्रियमाणस्तु विश्वत्वमुपगच्छति ॥ 14.18 ॥
1.14.m: Just as a lump of clay on the potter's wheel, pressed by the whirlwind / and shaped by both hands, assumes diverse shapes,

1.14.s:
evamātmāsthisaṃyukto vāyunā samudīritaḥ.
jāyate mānuṣastatra yathā rūpaṃ tathā manaḥ .. 14.19 ..
1.14.d:
एवमात्मास्थिसंयुक्तो वायुना समुदीरितः।
जायते मानुषस्तत्र यथा रूपं तथा मनः ॥ 14.19 ॥
1.14.m: so the self, united with bones and impelled by the wind, / is born there as a human being, with a form corresponding to the mind.

1.14.s:
vāyuḥ sambhavate teṣāṃ vātāt sañjāyate jalam.
jalātsaṃbhavati prāṇaḥ prāṇācchukraṃ vivarddhate .. 14.20 ..
1.14.d:
वायुः सम्भवते तेषां वातात् सञ्जायते जलम्।
जलात्संभवति प्राणः प्राणाच्छुक्रं विवर्द्धते ॥ 14.20 ॥
1.14.m: Wind arises for them; from the wind, water is born; / from water, vital breath arises; and from vital breath, semen increases.

1.14.s:
raktabhāgāstrayastriṃśacchukra bhāgāścaturddaśa.
bhāgato'rddhapalaṃ kṛtvā tato garbhe niṣevate .. 14.21 ..
1.14.d:
रक्तभागास्त्रयस्त्रिंशच्छुक्र भागाश्चतुर्द्दश।
भागतोऽर्द्धपलं कृत्वा ततो गर्भे निषेवते ॥ 14.21 ॥
1.14.m: There are thirty-three parts of blood, and fourteen parts of semen; / making half a pala in proportion, it settles in the womb.

1.14.s:
tatastu garbhasaṃyuktaḥ pañcabhirvāyubhirvṛtaḥ.
pituḥ śarīrāt pratyaṅgarūpamasyopajāyate .. 14.22 ..
1.14.d:
ततस्तु गर्भसंयुक्तः पञ्चभिर्वायुभिर्वृतः।
पितुः शरीरात् प्रत्यङ्गरूपमस्योपजायते ॥ 14.22 ॥
1.14.m: Then, joined in the womb, surrounded by the five vital winds, / the form of each of its limbs develops from the father's body.

1.14.s:
tato'sya māturāhārāt pītalīḍhapraveśitam.
nābhi srotaḥpraveśena prāṇādhāro hi dehinām .. 14.23 ..
1.14.d:
ततोऽस्य मातुराहारात् पीतलीढप्रवेशितम्।
नाभि स्रोतःप्रवेशेन प्राणाधारो हि देहिनाम् ॥ 14.23 ॥
1.14.m: Then, from the mother's food, entered through what is drunk and licked, / by the entry through the channel of the navel, is indeed the support of life for embodied beings.

1.14.s:
navamāsān parikliṣṭaḥ saṃveṣṭitaśirodharaḥ .
veṣṭitaḥ sarvvagātraiśca aparyyāyakramāgataḥ.
navamāsoṣitaścaiva yonicchidrādavāṅ‌mukhaḥ .. 14.24 ..
1.14.d:
नवमासान् परिक्लिष्टः संवेष्टितशिरोधरः ।
वेष्टितः सर्व्वगात्रैश्च अपर्य्यायक्रमागतः।
नवमासोषितश्चैव योनिच्छिद्रादवाङ्‌मुखः ॥ 14.24 ॥
1.14.m: Tormented for nine months, his neck and head wrapped around, / wrapped with all his limbs, proceeding through the fixed sequence, / having resided for nine months, he [emerges] facing downwards from the aperture of the womb.

1.14.s:
tatastu karmmabhiḥ pāpairnirayaṃ pratipadyate.
asipatravanañcaiva śālmalīcchedabhedayoḥ .. 14.25 ..
1.14.d:
ततस्तु कर्म्मभिः पापैर्निरयं प्रतिपद्यते।
असिपत्रवनञ्चैव शाल्मलीच्छेदभेदयोः ॥ 14.25 ॥
1.14.m: Then, through evil deeds, he enters hell, / and the forest of sword-leaves, and the cutting and splitting upon the śālmali tree.

1.14.s:
tatra nirbhartsanañcaiva tathā śoṇitabhojanam .
etāstu yātan ghorāḥ kumbhīpākasuduḥsahāḥ .. 14.26 ..
1.14.d:
तत्र निर्भर्त्सनञ्चैव तथा शोणितभोजनम् ।
एतास्तु यातन् घोराः कुम्भीपाकसुदुःसहाः ॥ 14.26 ॥
1.14.m: There he suffers rebukes, and likewise the eating of blood; / these are the dreadful torments, and the most unbearable Kumbhīpāka.

1.14.s:
yathā hyāpastu vicchinnāḥ svarūpamupayānti vai .
tasmācchinnāśca bhinnāśca yātanāsthānamāgataḥ .. 14.27 ..
1.14.d:
यथा ह्यापस्तु विच्छिन्नाः स्वरूपमुपयान्ति वै ।
तस्माच्छिन्नाश्च भिन्नाश्च यातनास्थानमागतः ॥ 14.27 ॥
1.14.m: For just as waters, when divided, return indeed to their natural form, / so having arrived at the place of torment, though cut and split, [they regain their shape].

1.14.s:
evaṃ jīvastu taiḥ pāpaistapyamānaḥ svayaṃ kṛtaiḥ .
prāpnuyāt karmmabhirduḥkhaṃ śeṣaṃ vā yādi cetaram .. 14.28 ..
1.14.d:
एवं जीवस्तु तैः पापैस्तप्यमानः स्वयं कृतैः ।
प्राप्नुयात् कर्म्मभिर्दुःखं शेषं वा यादि चेतरम् ॥ 14.28 ॥
1.14.m: Thus the individual soul, tormented by those evils done by itself, / would incur pain through its actions, or whatever remainder [of karma] or its opposite [remains].

1.14.s:
ekenaiva tu gantavyaṃ sarvvamṛtyuniveśanam.
ekanaiva ca bhoktavyaṃ tasmāt sukṛtamācaret .. 14.29 ..
1.14.d:
एकेनैव तु गन्तव्यं सर्व्वमृत्युनिवेशनम्।
एकनैव च भोक्तव्यं तस्मात् सुकृतमाचरेत् ॥ 14.29 ॥
1.14.m: Alone indeed one must go to the dwelling of all-death; / and alone one must experience [the fruit]; therefore one should perform good deeds.

1.14.s:
na hyenaṃ prasthitaṃ kaścidgacchantamanugacchati.
yadanena kṛtaṃ karmma tadenamanugacchati .. 14.30 ..
1.14.d:
न ह्येनं प्रस्थितं कश्चिद्गच्छन्तमनुगच्छति।
यदनेन कृतं कर्म्म तदेनमनुगच्छति ॥ 14.30 ॥
1.14.m: For no one follows him who has departed, as he goes away; / whatever deed has been done by him, that alone follows him.

1.14.s:
te nityaṃ yamaviṣaye vibhinnadehāḥ krośantaḥ satatamaniṣṭasaṃprayogaiḥ.
śuṣyante parigatavedanāśarīrāḥ bahvībhiḥ subhṛśamadharmmayātanābhiḥ .. 14.31 ..
1.14.d:
ते नित्यं यमविषये विभिन्नदेहाः क्रोशन्तः सततमनिष्टसंप्रयोगैः।
शुष्यन्ते परिगतवेदनाशरीराः बह्वीभिः सुभृशमधर्म्मयातनाभिः ॥ 14.31 ॥
1.14.m: Always in the realm of Yama, their bodies torn apart, wailing incessantly through contact with unwanted [pains], / their bodies overcome by agony, they wither away severely through many torments born of unrighteousness.

1.14.s:
karmaṇāḥ manasā vācā yadabhīṣṭaṃ niṣevyate.
tat prasadya haret pāpaṃ tasmāt‌ sukṛtamācaret .. 14.32 ..
1.14.d:
कर्मणाः मनसा वाचा यदभीष्टं निषेव्यते।
तत् प्रसद्य हरेत् पापं तस्मात्‌ सुकृतमाचरेत् ॥ 14.32 ॥
1.14.m: Whatever is pursued with desire through action, mind, or speech, / having propitiated [virtue], one should destroy that sin; therefore one should perform good deeds.

1.14.s:
yādṛg jātāni pāpāni pūrvvaṃ karmmāṇi dehinaḥ.
saṃsāraṃ tāmasaṃ tādṛk ṣah‌vidhaṃ pratipadyate .. 14.33 ..
1.14.d:
यादृग् जातानि पापानि पूर्व्वं कर्म्माणि देहिनः।
संसारं तामसं तादृक् षह्‌विधं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 14.33 ॥
1.14.m: According to the evil deeds done previously by an embodied soul, / such is the sixfold cycle of rebirth dominated by darkness which he enters.

1.14.s:
mānuṣyaṃ paśubhāvañca paśubhāvānmṛgo bhavet.
mṛgatvāt pakṣibhāvantu tasmāccaiva sarīsṛpaḥ .. 14.34 ..
1.14.d:
मानुष्यं पशुभावञ्च पशुभावान्मृगो भवेत्।
मृगत्वात् पक्षिभावन्तु तस्माच्चैव सरीसृपः ॥ 14.34 ॥
1.14.m: Human state, then the state of cattle; from the state of cattle he becomes a wild animal; / from the state of a wild animal, a bird; and from that, a reptile.

1.14.s:
sarīsṛpatvādgacchoddhi.
sthāvaratvanna saṃśayaḥ.
sthāvaratvaṃ punaḥ prāpto
yāvadunmiṣate naraḥ.
kulālacakavadbhāntastatraivaparikīrtitaḥ .. 14.35 ..
1.14.d:
सरीसृपत्वाद्गच्छोद्धि।
स्थावरत्वन्न संशयः।
स्थावरत्वं पुनः प्राप्तो
यावदुन्मिषते नरः।
कुलालचकवद्भान्तस्तत्रैवपरिकीर्तितः ॥ 14.35 ॥
1.14.m: From the state of a reptile, he indeed goes / to the immobile state, without doubt. / Having reached the immobile state again, / as long as a man blinks his eye, / he is declared to turn around right there like a potter's wheel.

1.14.s:
ityevaṃ hi manuṣyādiḥ saṃsāre sthāvarāntake.
vijñeyastāmaso nāma tatraiva parivarttate .. 14.36 ..
1.14.d:
इत्येवं हि मनुष्यादिः संसारे स्थावरान्तके।
विज्ञेयस्तामसो नाम तत्रैव परिवर्त्तते ॥ 14.36 ॥
1.14.m: Thus beginning with human and ending with immobile things in the cycle of rebirth, / it is known as dominated by darkness; he revolves right there.

1.14.s:
sāttvikaścāpi saṃsāro brahmādiḥ parikīrttitaḥ.
piśācāntaḥ savijñeyaḥ svargasthāneṣu dehinām .. 14.37 ..
1.14.d:
सात्त्विकश्चापि संसारो ब्रह्मादिः परिकीर्त्तितः।
पिशाचान्तः सविज्ञेयः स्वर्गस्थानेषु देहिनाम् ॥ 14.37 ॥
1.14.m: And the cycle of rebirth dominated by purity is proclaimed to begin with Brahmā; / it is to be known as ending with piśācas in the heavenly abodes of embodied souls.

1.14.s:
brāhme tu kevalaṃ sattvaṃ sthāvare kevalaṃ tamaḥ.
caturddaśānāṃ sthānānāṃ madhye viṣṭambhakaṃ rajaḥ.
marmasu cchidyamāneṣu vedanārttasya dehinaḥ .. 14.38 ..
1.14.d:
ब्राह्मे तु केवलं सत्त्वं स्थावरे केवलं तमः।
चतुर्द्दशानां स्थानानां मध्ये विष्टम्भकं रजः।
मर्मसु च्छिद्यमानेषु वेदनार्त्तस्य देहिनः ॥ 14.38 ॥
1.14.m: In the realm of Brahmā there is pure purity; in the immobile there is pure darkness; / in the midst of the fourteen stations passion acts as a supporter. / When the vital spots are being cut of the embodied soul afflicted with agony,

1.14.s:
tatastu paramaṃ brahma kathaṃ vipraḥ smariṣyati .
saṃskārāt pūrvadharmasya bhāvanāyāṃ praṇoditaḥ.
mānuṣyaṃ bhajate nityaṃ tasmānnityaṃ samādadhet .. 14.39 ..
1.14.d:
ततस्तु परमं ब्रह्म कथं विप्रः स्मरिष्यति ।
संस्कारात् पूर्वधर्मस्य भावनायां प्रणोदितः।
मानुष्यं भजते नित्यं तस्मान्नित्यं समादधेत् ॥ 14.39 ॥
1.14.m: how then will a Brahmin remember the supreme Brahman? / Impelled toward contemplation by the impression of previous righteousness, / he always attains a human birth; therefore he should continually compose his mind.

1.14.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte pāśupatayogo nāma caturddaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 14 ..
1.14.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते पाशुपतयोगो नाम चतुर्द्दशोऽध्यायः ॥ 14 ॥
1.14.m: Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, named Pāśupata Yoga, in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.15.m:
Vāyu said:
Having understood this fourteen-fold circle of the cycle of rebirth,
one afflicted with the fear of the cycle of rebirth should undertake action accordingly.

1.15.s:
caturddaśavidhaṃ hyetadbuddhvā saṃsāramaṇḍalam.
tathā samārabhet karmma saṃsārabhayapīḍitaḥ .. 15.1 ..
1.15.d:
चतुर्द्दशविधं ह्येतद्बुद्ध्वा संसारमण्डलम्।
तथा समारभेत् कर्म्म संसारभयपीडितः ॥ 15.1 ॥

1.15.s:
tataḥ smarati saṃsāracakreṇa parivarttitaḥ.
tasmāttu satataṃ yukto dhyānatatparayuñjakaḥ.
tathā samārabhedyogaṃ yathātmānaṃ sa paśyati .. 15.2 ..
1.15.d:
ततः स्मरति संसारचक्रेण परिवर्त्तितः।
तस्मात्तु सततं युक्तो ध्यानतत्परयुञ्जकः।
तथा समारभेद्योगं यथात्मानं स पश्यति ॥ 15.2 ॥
1.15.m: Then, turned about by the wheel of the cycle of rebirth, he remembers; / therefore, always disciplined, intent on meditation and yoking [his mind], / he should undertake yoga in such a way that he perceives the Self.

1.15.s:
eṣa ādyaḥ paraṃ jyotireṣa seturanuttamaḥ.
vivṛddho hyeṣa bhūtānāṃ na sambhedaśca śāśvataḥ .. 15.3 ..
1.15.d:
एष आद्यः परं ज्योतिरेष सेतुरनुत्तमः।
विवृद्धो ह्येष भूतानां न सम्भेदश्च शाश्वतः ॥ 15.3 ॥
1.15.m: This is the primeval, supreme light; this is the unsurpassed bridge. / For this [light] of living beings is expanded, and it is eternal, without distinction.

1.15.s:
tadenaṃ setumātmānaṃ agniṃ vai viśvatomukham.
hṛdisthaṃ sarvabhūtānāmupāsīta vidhānavit .. 15.4 ..
1.15.d:
तदेनं सेतुमात्मानं अग्निं वै विश्वतोमुखम्।
हृदिस्थं सर्वभूतानामुपासीत विधानवित् ॥ 15.4 ॥
1.15.m: Therefore, one who knows the rite should worship this Self, the bridge, / the fire facing in all directions, situated in the heart of all beings.

1.15.s:
hutvāṣṭāvāhutīḥ samyak śucistadgatamānasaḥ.
vaiśvānaraṃ hṛdisthantu yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ.
apaḥ pūrva sakṛt prāśya tuṣṇīṃ bhūtvā upāsate .. 15.5 ..
1.15.d:
हुत्वाष्टावाहुतीः सम्यक् शुचिस्तद्गतमानसः।
वैश्वानरं हृदिस्थन्तु यथावदनुपूर्वशः।
अपः पूर्व सकृत् प्राश्य तुष्णीं भूत्वा उपासते ॥ 15.5 ॥
1.15.m: Having duly offered eight oblations, pure, his mind fixed on that, / [worshipping] Vaiśvānara situated in the heart properly in succession, / having first sipped water once and become silent, he worships.

1.15.s:
prāṇāyeti tatastasya prathamā hyāhutiḥ smṛtā.
apānāya dvitīyā tu samānāyeti cāparā .. 15.6 ..
1.15.d:
प्राणायेति ततस्तस्य प्रथमा ह्याहुतिः स्मृता।
अपानाय द्वितीया तु समानायेति चापरा ॥ 15.6 ॥
1.15.m: Then his first oblation is traditionally taught as: 'To Prāṇa'; / the second as: 'To Apāna'; and another as: 'To Samāna';

1.15.s:
udānāya caturthīti vyānāyeti ca pañcamī.
svāhā kāraiḥ paraṃ hutvā śeṣaṃ bhuñjīta kāmataḥ.
apaḥ punaḥ sakṛt prāśya tryācamya hṛdayaṃ spṛśet .. 15.7 ..
1.15.d:
उदानाय चतुर्थीति व्यानायेति च पञ्चमी।
स्वाहा कारैः परं हुत्वा शेषं भुञ्जीत कामतः।
अपः पुनः सकृत् प्राश्य त्र्याचम्य हृदयं स्पृशेत् ॥ 15.7 ॥
1.15.m: the fourth as: 'To Udāna'; and the fifth as: 'To Vyāna'. / Having offered the supreme [oblations] with the utterances of svāhā, he should eat the remainder as he pleases. / Having sipped water once again, performing the threefold sipping, he should touch his heart:

1.15.s:
oṃprāṇānāṃ granthirasyātmā rudro hyātmā viśāntakaḥ.
sa rudro hyātmanaḥ prāṇā evamāpyāyayet svayam .. 15.8 ..
1.15.d:
ओंप्राणानां ग्रन्थिरस्यात्मा रुद्रो ह्यात्मा विशान्तकः।
स रुद्रो ह्यात्मनः प्राणा एवमाप्याययेत् स्वयम् ॥ 15.8 ॥
1.15.m: 'Om, you are the knot of the vital breaths; its Self is Rudra, the Self that puts an end to all.' / For that Rudra is the vital breaths of oneself; thus he should refresh himself.

1.15.s:
tvaṃ devānāmapi jyeṣṭha ugrastvaṃ caturo vṛṣā .
mṛtyughno'si tvamasmabhyaṃ bhadrametaddhutaṃ haviḥ .. 15.9 ..
1.15.d:
त्वं देवानामपि ज्येष्ठ उग्रस्त्वं चतुरो वृषा ।
मृत्युघ्नोऽसि त्वमस्मभ्यं भद्रमेतद्धुतं हविः ॥ 15.9 ॥
1.15.m: 'You are the eldest even among the gods, you are fierce, clever, the bull; / you are the slayer of death for us; auspicious is this offered oblation.'

1.15.s:
evaṃ hṛdayamālabhya pādāṅguṣṭhe tu dakṣiṇe.
viśrāvya dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ nābhiṃ vai pāṇinā spṛśet .
tataḥ punarupaspṛś‌ya cātmānamabhisaṃspṛśet .. 15.10 ..
1.15.d:
एवं हृदयमालभ्य पादाङ्गुष्ठे तु दक्षिणे।
विश्राव्य दक्षिणं पाणिं नाभिं वै पाणिना स्पृशेत् ।
ततः पुनरुपस्पृश्‌य चात्मानमभिसंस्पृशेत् ॥ 15.10 ॥
1.15.m: Having thus touched the heart, then on the right big toe / having let water flow from the right hand, he should touch the navel with the hand. / Then, having sipped water again, he should touch himself all over:

1.15.s:
akṣiṇī nāsikā śrotre hṛdayaṃ śira eva ca.
dvāvātmānāvubhāvetau prāṇāpānāvudāhṛtau .. 15.11 ..
1.15.d:
अक्षिणी नासिका श्रोत्रे हृदयं शिर एव च।
द्वावात्मानावुभावेतौ प्राणापानावुदाहृतौ ॥ 15.11 ॥
1.15.m: the two eyes, the nose, the two ears, the heart, and the head. / These two, prāṇa and apāna, are declared to be both the selves.

1.15.s:
tayoḥ prāṇo'ntarātmāsya bāhyo'pāno'ta ucyate.
annaṃ prāṇastathāpānaṃ mṛtyurjjīvitameva ca .. 15.12 ..
1.15.d:
तयोः प्राणोऽन्तरात्मास्य बाह्योऽपानोऽत उच्यते।
अन्नं प्राणस्तथापानं मृत्युर्ज्जीवितमेव च ॥ 15.12 ॥
1.15.m: Between them, prāṇa is called his inner self, and apāna the outer; / food is prāṇa as well as apāna, death and life itself.

1.15.s:
annaṃ brahma ca vijñeyaṃ prajānāṃ prasavastathā.
annādbhūtāni jāyante sthitirannena ceṣyate.
varddhante tena bhūtāni tasmādannantaducyate .. 15.13 ..
1.15.d:
अन्नं ब्रह्म च विज्ञेयं प्रजानां प्रसवस्तथा।
अन्नाद्भूतानि जायन्ते स्थितिरन्नेन चेष्यते।
वर्द्धन्ते तेन भूतानि तस्मादन्नन्तदुच्यते ॥ 15.13 ॥
1.15.m: And food should be known as Brahman, and the procreation of creatures; / from food beings are born, and through food maintenance is desired; / beings grow through it, therefore it is called food (anna).

1.15.s:
tadevāgnau hutaṃ hyannaṃ bhuñjate devadānavāḥ.
gandharvayakṣarakṣāṃsi piśācāścānnameva hi .. 15.14 ..
1.15.d:
तदेवाग्नौ हुतं ह्यन्नं भुञ्जते देवदानवाः।
गन्धर्वयक्षरक्षांसि पिशाचाश्चान्नमेव हि ॥ 15.14 ॥
1.15.m: That very food offered in fire the gods and dānavas consume; / and the gandharvas, yakṣas, rakṣases, and piśācas [consume] food alone.

1.15.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyu prokte pāśupatayogo nāma pañcadaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 15 ..
1.15.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायु प्रोक्ते पाशुपतयोगो नाम पञ्चदशोऽध्यायः ॥ 15 ॥
1.15.m: Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, named Pāśupata Yoga, in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.16.s: .. vāyuruvāca ..
1.16.d: ॥ वायुरुवाच ॥
1.16.m:
Vāyu said:
Hereafter I shall explain the characteristics of purity and good conduct,
by performing which, purified in self, one would indeed attain heaven after death.

1.16.s:
ata ūddhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi śaucācārasya lakṣaṇam.
yadanuṣṭhāya śuddhātmā pretya svargaṃ hi cāpnuyāt .. 16.1 ..
1.16.d:
अत ऊद्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि शौचाचारस्य लक्षणम्।
यदनुष्ठाय शुद्धात्मा प्रेत्य स्वर्गं हि चाप्नुयात् ॥ 16.1 ॥

1.16.s:
udakārthī tu śaucānāṃ munīnāmuttamaṃ padam .
yastu teṣvapramattaḥ syāt sa munirnnāvasīdati .. 16.2 ..
1.16.d:
उदकार्थी तु शौचानां मुनीनामुत्तमं पदम् ।
यस्तु तेष्वप्रमत्तः स्यात् स मुनिर्न्नावसीदति ॥ 16.2 ॥
1.16.m: Seeking water for purifications is the highest stage for sages; / one who is heedful among them, that sage does not falter.

1.16.s:
mānāvamānau dvovetau tāvevāhurviṣāmṛte .
avamānaṃ viṣaṃ tatra mānantvamṛtamucyate .. 16.3 ..
1.16.d:
मानावमानौ द्वोवेतौ तावेवाहुर्विषामृते ।
अवमानं विषं तत्र मानन्त्वमृतमुच्यते ॥ 16.3 ॥
1.16.m: Honor and dishonor, these two they have declared to be poison and nectar; / of these, dishonor is nectar, but honor is called poison.

1.16.s:
yastu teṣvapramattaḥ syāt sa munirnnāvasīdati .
guroḥ priyahite yuktaḥ sa tu saṃvatsaraṃ vaset .. 16.4 ..
1.16.d:
यस्तु तेष्वप्रमत्तः स्यात् स मुनिर्न्नावसीदति ।
गुरोः प्रियहिते युक्तः स तु संवत्सरं वसेत् ॥ 16.4 ॥
1.16.m: He who is heedful in these matters, that sage does not falter. / Devoted to what is pleasant and beneficial to his guru, he should live [with him] for a year.

1.16.s:
niyameṣvapramattastu yameṣu ca sadā bhavet .
prāpyānujñāntataścaiva jñānāgamanamuttamam.
avirodhena dharmasya vicaret pṛthivīmimām .. 16.5 ..
1.16.d:
नियमेष्वप्रमत्तस्तु यमेषु च सदा भवेत् ।
प्राप्यानुज्ञान्ततश्चैव ज्ञानागमनमुत्तमम्।
अविरोधेन धर्मस्य विचरेत् पृथिवीमिमाम् ॥ 16.5 ॥
1.16.m: He should always be heedful in observances and in moral restraints. / Having obtained permission, and thereupon the supreme attainment of knowledge, / he should wander over this earth without contradicting dharma.

1.16.s:
cakṣuḥ pūtaṃ vrajenmārgaṃ vastrapūtaṃ jalaṃ pibet.
satyapūtāṃ vadedvāṇīmiti dharmānuśāsanam .. 16.6 ..
1.16.d:
चक्षुः पूतं व्रजेन्मार्गं वस्त्रपूतं जलं पिबेत्।
सत्यपूतां वदेद्वाणीमिति धर्मानुशासनम् ॥ 16.6 ॥
1.16.m: One should walk a path purified by sight; one should drink water purified by cloth; / one should speak speech purified by truth: this is the instruction of dharma.

1.16.s:
ātithyaṃ śrāddhayajñeṣu na gacchedyogavit vkacit.
evaṃ hyahiṃsako yogī bhavediti vicāraṇā .. 16.7 ..
1.16.d:
आतिथ्यं श्राद्धयज्ञेषु न गच्छेद्योगवित् व्कचित्।
एवं ह्यहिंसको योगी भवेदिति विचारणा ॥ 16.7 ॥
1.16.m: One who knows yoga should never accept hospitality at śrāddhas or sacrifices; / for thus a yogin becomes non-violent: this is the deliberation.

1.16.s:
vahnau vidhūme vyaṅgāre sarvṛsmin bhuktavajjane.
vicarenmatimān yogī na tu teṣveva nityaśaḥ .. 16.8 ..
1.16.d:
वह्नौ विधूमे व्यङ्गारे सर्वृस्मिन् भुक्तवज्जने।
विचरेन्मतिमान् योगी न तु तेष्वेव नित्यशः ॥ 16.8 ॥
1.16.m: When the fire is smokeless and its coals spent, when all people have finished eating, / the wise yogin may wander [for alms], but not continually among the very same [houses].

1.16.s:
yathaivamavamanyante yathā paribhavanti ca.
yuktastathā caredbhaikṣaṃ satāṃ dharmamadūṣayan .. 16.9 ..
1.16.d:
यथैवमवमन्यन्ते यथा परिभवन्ति च।
युक्तस्तथा चरेद्भैक्षं सतां धर्ममदूषयन् ॥ 16.9 ॥
1.16.m: In such a way that [people] despise him and treat him with contempt, / concentrated [in mind], he should wander for alms without debasing the duty of the virtuous.

1.16.s:
bhaikṣaṃ caredgṛhastheṣu yathācāragṛheṣu ca.
śreṣṭhā tu paramā ceyaṃ vṛttirasyopadiśyate .. 16.10 ..
1.16.d:
भैक्षं चरेद्गृहस्थेषु यथाचारगृहेषु च।
श्रेष्ठा तु परमा चेयं वृत्तिरस्योपदिश्यते ॥ 16.10 ॥
1.16.m: He should wander for alms among householders, at the houses of those who maintain righteous conduct; / and this is taught to be his highest and supreme livelihood.

1.16.s:
ata ūrddhvaṃ gṛhastheṣu śālīneṣu cared‌dvijaḥ.
śraddadhāneṣu dānteṣu śrotriyeṣu mahātmasu .. 16.11 ..
1.16.d:
अत ऊर्द्ध्वं गृहस्थेषु शालीनेषु चरेद्‌द्विजः।
श्रद्दधानेषु दान्तेषु श्रोत्रियेषु महात्मसु ॥ 16.11 ॥
1.16.m: Next to that, the twice-born should wander among householders of settled life, / faithful, self-restrained, learned in the Veda, and noble-minded.

1.16.s:
ata ūrddhvaṃ punaścāpi aduṣṭapatiteṣu ca.
bhaikṣacaryā vivarṇeṣu jaghanyā vṛttirucyate .. 16.12 ..
1.16.d:
अत ऊर्द्ध्वं पुनश्चापि अदुष्टपतितेषु च।
भैक्षचर्या विवर्णेषु जघन्या वृत्तिरुच्यते ॥ 16.12 ॥
1.16.m: Next to that again, among unblemished outcastes; / begging alms among low-caste persons is called the lowest livelihood.

1.16.s:
bhaikṣaṃ yavāgūṃ takraṃ vā payo yāvakameva ca.
phaḻamūlaṃ vipavkaṃ vā piṇyākaṃ śaktitopi vā .. 16.13 ..
1.16.d:
भैक्षं यवागूं तक्रं वा पयो यावकमेव च।
फḻअमूलं विपव्कं वा पिण्याकं शक्तितोपि वा ॥ 16.13 ॥
1.16.m: Alms-food, or barley gruel, or buttermilk, milk, and barley mash, / fruit and roots, cooked food, or oil-cake according to one's capacity—

1.16.s:
ityete vai mayā proktā yogināṃ siddhivarddhanāḥ.
āhārāsteṣu siddheṣu śreṣṭhaṃ bhaikṣamiti smṛtam .. 16.14 ..
1.16.d:
इत्येते वै मया प्रोक्ता योगिनां सिद्धिवर्द्धनाः।
आहारास्तेषु सिद्धेषु श्रेष्ठं भैक्षमिति स्मृतम् ॥ 16.14 ॥
1.16.m: these indeed have been declared by me as foods promoting attainment for yogins. / Among those cooked [foods], alms-food is remembered as the best.

1.16.s:
abbinduṃ yaḥ kuśāgreṇa māse māse samaśnute.
nyāyato yastu bhikṣeta sa pūrvoktādviśiṣyate .. 16.15 ..
1.16.d:
अब्बिन्दुं यः कुशाग्रेण मासे मासे समश्नुते।
न्यायतो यस्तु भिक्षेत स पूर्वोक्ताद्विशिष्यते ॥ 16.15 ॥
1.16.m: He who takes a drop of water on the tip of a kuśa blade month after month, / but he who begs according to the rule excels the former.

1.16.s:
yogināṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ cāndrāyaṇaṃ smṛtam .
ekaṃ dve trīṇi catvāri śaktito vā samācaret .. 16.16 ..
1.16.d:
योगिनां चैव सर्वेषां श्रेष्ठं चान्द्रायणं स्मृतम् ।
एकं द्वे त्रीणि चत्वारि शक्तितो वा समाचरेत् ॥ 16.16 ॥
1.16.m: And for all yogins the Cāndrāyaṇa [observance] is remembered as the best; / he should perform one, two, three, or four according to his capacity.

1.16.s:
asteyaṃ brahmacaryañca alobhastyāga eva ca.
vratāni caiva bhikṣūṇāmahiṃsā paramārthitā .. 16.17 ..
1.16.d:
अस्तेयं ब्रह्मचर्यञ्च अलोभस्त्याग एव च।
व्रतानि चैव भिक्षूणामहिंसा परमार्थिता ॥ 16.17 ॥
1.16.m: Non-stealing, celibacy, freedom from greed, renunciation, / and the vows of mendicants are non-violence and pursuit of the highest truth.

1.16.s:
akrodho guruśuśrūṣā śaucamāhāralāghavam.
nityaṃsvādhyāya ityete niyamāḥ parikīrtitāḥ .. 16.18 ..
1.16.d:
अक्रोधो गुरुशुश्रूषा शौचमाहारलाघवम्।
नित्यंस्वाध्याय इत्येते नियमाः परिकीर्तिताः ॥ 16.18 ॥
1.16.m: Absence of anger, service to the guru, purity, lightness of diet, / and perpetual Vedic recitation—these are proclaimed as the observances.

1.16.s:
bīcayonirguṇavapurbaddhaḥ karmabhireva ca.
yathā dvipa ivāraṇye manuṣyāṇāṃ vidhīyate .. 16.19 ..
1.16.d:
बीचयोनिर्गुणवपुर्बद्धः कर्मभिरेव च।
यथा द्विप इवारण्ये मनुष्याणां विधीयते ॥ 16.19 ॥
1.16.m: Having the seed as source, an embodiment composed of the guṇas, and bound by actions, / just as an elephant in the forest is brought under the control of men,

1.16.s:
prāpyate vācirādevāṅkuśeneva nivāritaḥ.
evaṃ jñānena śuddhena dagdhabīco hyakalmaṣaḥ.
vimuktabandhaḥ śānto'sau mukta ityabhidhīyate .. 16.20 ..
1.16.d:
प्राप्यते वाचिरादेवाङ्कुशेनेव निवारितः।
एवं ज्ञानेन शुद्धेन दग्धबीचो ह्यकल्मषः।
विमुक्तबन्धः शान्तोऽसौ मुक्त इत्यभिधीयते ॥ 16.20 ॥
1.16.m: or is mastered quickly indeed when checked by an elephant-goad, / so, having burnt the seed through pure knowledge, blemishless, / freed from bondage and tranquil, he is called liberated.

1.16.s:
vedaistutyā sarvayajñakriyāstu yajñe japyaṃ jñānināmāhuragrayam.
jñānāddhayānaṃ saṅgarāgavyapetaṃ tasmin prāpte śāśvatasyopalabdhiḥ .. 16.21 ..
1.16.d:
वेदैस्तुत्या सर्वयज्ञक्रियास्तु यज्ञे जप्यं ज्ञानिनामाहुरग्रयम्।
ज्ञानाद्धयानं सङ्गरागव्यपेतं तस्मिन् प्राप्ते शाश्वतस्योपलब्धिः ॥ 16.21 ॥
1.16.m: All sacrificial rites are praised by the Vedas, but recitation in sacrifice is said to be the foremost for the wise; / higher than knowledge is meditation free from attachment and passion; when that is attained, there is realization of the eternal.

1.16.s:
damaḥ śamaḥ satyamakalmaṣatvaṃ maunaṃ ca bhūteṣvakhileṣvathārjjavam.
atīndriyajñānamidaṃ tathārjjavaṃ prāhustathā jñānaviśuddhasattvāḥ .. 16.22 ..
1.16.d:
दमः शमः सत्यमकल्मषत्वं मौनं च भूतेष्वखिलेष्वथार्ज्जवम्।
अतीन्द्रियज्ञानमिदं तथार्ज्जवं प्राहुस्तथा ज्ञानविशुद्धसत्त्वाः ॥ 16.22 ॥
1.16.m: Self-control, tranquility, truth, purity, silence, and uprightness toward all beings; / this knowledge beyond the senses and uprightness are taught thus by those whose minds are purified through knowledge.

1.16.s:
samāhito brahmaparo'pramādī śucistathaivātmaratirjītendriyaḥ.
samāpnuyuryogamimaṃ mahādhiyo maharṣayaścaivamaninditāmalāḥ .. 16.23 ..
1.16.d:
समाहितो ब्रह्मपरोऽप्रमादी शुचिस्तथैवात्मरतिर्जीतेन्द्रियः।
समाप्नुयुर्योगमिमं महाधियो महर्षयश्चैवमनिन्दितामलाः ॥ 16.23 ॥
1.16.m: Concentrated, devoted to the supreme Brahman, unheeding of distractions, pure, finding joy in the Self, with senses conquered— / the great-minded, blameless and spotless great seers attain this yoga.

1.16.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyu prokte śaucācāralakṣaṇaṃ nāma ṣoḍaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 16 ..
1.16.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायु प्रोक्ते शौचाचारलक्षणं नाम षोडशोऽध्यायः ॥ 16 ॥
1.16.m: Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, named 'Characteristics of Purity and Conduct', in the venerable Mahāpurāṇa uttered by Vāyu.

1.17.s:
.. vāyuruvāca ..
āśramatrayamutsṛjya prāptastu paramāśramam.
ataḥ saṃvatsarasyānte prāpya jñānamanuttamam .. 17.1 ..
anujñāpya gurūṃcaiva vicaret pṛthivīmimām.
sārabhūtamupāsīta jñānaṃ yajjñeya sādhakam .. 17.2 ..
idaṃ jñānamidaṃ jñeyamiti yastuṣitaścaret .
api kalpasahasrāyurnnaiva jñeyamavāpnuyāt .. 17.3 ..
tyaktasaṅgo jitakodho laghvāhāro jitendriyaḥ.
pidhāya buddhyā dvārāṇi dhyāne hyevaṃ mano dadhet .. 17.4 ..
śūnyeṣvevāvakāśeṣu guhāsu cavane tathā.
nadīnāṃ puline caiva nityaṃ yuktaḥ sadā bhavet .. 17.5 ..
vāgdaṇḍaḥ karmadaṇḍaśca manodaṇḍaśca te trayaḥ.
yasyaite niyatā daṇḍāḥ sa tridaṇḍī vyavasthitaḥ .. 17.6 ..
avasthito dhyānaratirjitendriyaḥ śubhāśubhe hitya ca karmaṇī ubhe .
idaṃ śarīraṃ pravimucya śāstrato na jāyate mriyate vā kadācit .. 17.7 ..
iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte paramāśramaprāptikathanaṃ nāma saptadaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 17 ..
1.17.d:
॥ वायुरुवाच ॥
आश्रमत्रयमुत्सृज्य प्राप्तस्तु परमाश्रमम्।
अतः संवत्सरस्यान्ते प्राप्य ज्ञानमनुत्तमम् ॥ 17.1 ॥
अनुज्ञाप्य गुरूंचैव विचरेत् पृथिवीमिमाम्।
सारभूतमुपासीत ज्ञानं यज्ज्ञेय साधकम् ॥ 17.2 ॥
इदं ज्ञानमिदं ज्ञेयमिति यस्तुषितश्चरेत् ।
अपि कल्पसहस्रायुर्न्नैव ज्ञेयमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 17.3 ॥
त्यक्तसङ्गो जितकोधो लघ्वाहारो जितेन्द्रियः।
पिधाय बुद्ध्या द्वाराणि ध्याने ह्येवं मनो दधेत् ॥ 17.4 ॥
शून्येष्वेवावकाशेषु गुहासु चवने तथा।
नदीनां पुलिने चैव नित्यं युक्तः सदा भवेत् ॥ 17.5 ॥
वाग्दण्डः कर्मदण्डश्च मनोदण्डश्च ते त्रयः।
यस्यैते नियता दण्डाः स त्रिदण्डी व्यवस्थितः ॥ 17.6 ॥
अवस्थितो ध्यानरतिर्जितेन्द्रियः शुभाशुभे हित्य च कर्मणी उभे ।
इदं शरीरं प्रविमुच्य शास्त्रतो न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचित् ॥ 17.7 ॥
इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते परमाश्रमप्राप्तिकथनं नाम सप्तदशोऽध्यायः ॥ 17 ॥
1.17.m:
Vāyu said:
Having abandoned the three stages of life and reached the supreme stage of life,
then, at the end of a year, having attained unexcelled knowledge,

and having taken leave of one's gurus, one should wander over this earth;
one should attend to the essential knowledge that accomplishes [the realization of] the object of knowledge.

He who wanders about, satisfied [merely] with: 'This is knowledge, this is the object of knowledge,'
even living for a thousand aeons, would never attain the object of knowledge.

Abandoning attachment, conquering anger, eating light food, with senses subdued,
closing the gates [of perception] with the intellect, he should thus place his mind in meditation.

In empty spaces, in caves, and likewise in the forest,
and on the sandbanks of rivers, he should always be ever-disciplined.

Restraint of speech, restraint of action, and restraint of mind—these are the three;
he whose restraints are steadfast is established as a tridaṇḍin.

Steadfast, delighting in meditation, with senses subdued, having abandoned both auspicious and inauspicious deeds,
releasing this body according to the sacred texts, he is never born, nor does he die.

Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, titled 'The Account of Attaining the Supreme Stage of Life,' in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.18.s: .. vāyuruvāca ..
1.18.d: ॥ वायुरुवाच ॥
1.18.m:
Vāyu said:
Hereafter I shall explain the rule for ascetics in this world,
the expiations according to reality for those [transgressions] committed unintentionally;
and people who know the subtleties of dharma declare [expiations] also for what is done intentionally.

1.18.s:
ata ūrddhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi yatīnāmiha niścayam.
prāyaścittāni tattvena yānyakāmakṛtāni tu.
atha kāmakṛtepyāhuḥ sūkṣmadharmavido janāḥ .. 18.1 ..
1.18.d:
अत ऊर्द्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि यतीनामिह निश्चयम्।
प्रायश्चित्तानि तत्त्वेन यान्यकामकृतानि तु।
अथ कामकृतेप्याहुः सूक्ष्मधर्मविदो जनाः ॥ 18.1 ॥

1.18.s:
pāpañca trividhaṃ proktaṃ vāṅmanaḥkāyasambhavam.
satataṃ hidivā rātrau yenedaṃ badhyate jagat .. 18.2 ..
1.18.d:
पापञ्च त्रिविधं प्रोक्तं वाङ्मनःकायसम्भवम्।
सततं हिदिवा रात्रौ येनेदं बध्यते जगत् ॥ 18.2 ॥
1.18.m: Sin is declared to be threefold: arising from speech, mind, and body, / by which this world is constantly bound day and night.

1.18.s:
na karmāṇi na cāpyeṣa tiṣṭha tītiparā śrutiḥ.
kṣaṇameva prayojyantu āyuṣastu vidhāraṇāt .. 18.3 ..
1.18.d:
न कर्माणि न चाप्येष तिष्ठ तीतिपरा श्रुतिः।
क्षणमेव प्रयोज्यन्तु आयुषस्तु विधारणात् ॥ 18.3 ॥
1.18.m: The supreme Vedic revelation says that one should not [perform ritual] actions nor remain idle; / [effort] is to be applied only for a moment to sustain life.

1.18.s:
bhaveddhīro'pramattastu yogo hi paramaṃ balam.
na hi yogātparaṃ kiñcinnarāṇāmiha dṛśyate.
tasmādyogaṃ praśaṃsanti dharmayuktā manīṣiṇaḥ .. 18.4 ..
1.18.d:
भवेद्धीरोऽप्रमत्तस्तु योगो हि परमं बलम्।
न हि योगात्परं किञ्चिन्नराणामिह दृश्यते।
तस्माद्योगं प्रशंसन्ति धर्मयुक्ता मनीषिणः ॥ 18.4 ॥
1.18.m: The wise man should be unheeding of distractions, for yoga is the supreme power; / indeed, nothing higher than yoga is seen for men here; / therefore wise men endowed with dharma praise yoga.

1.18.s:
avidyāṃ vidyayā tīrtvā prāpyaiśvayarmanuttamam.
dṛṣṭvā parāparaṃ dhīrāḥ paraṃ gacchanti tatpadam .. 18.5 ..
1.18.d:
अविद्यां विद्यया तीर्त्वा प्राप्यैश्वयर्मनुत्तमम्।
दृष्ट्वा परापरं धीराः परं गच्छन्ति तत्पदम् ॥ 18.5 ॥
1.18.m: Crossing over ignorance by knowledge, gaining unsurpassed sovereign power, / and perceiving the higher and the lower, the wise reach that supreme state.

1.18.s:
vratāni yāni bhikṣūṇāṃ tathaivopavratāni ca.
ekaikāpakrame teṣāṃ prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate .. 18.6 ..
1.18.d:
व्रतानि यानि भिक्षूणां तथैवोपव्रतानि च।
एकैकापक्रमे तेषां प्रायश्चित्तं विधीयते ॥ 18.6 ॥
1.18.m: Whatever vows and minor vows there are for mendicants, / an expiation is prescribed for the breach of each one of them.

1.18.s:
upetya tu striyaṃ kāmāt prāyaścittaṃ vinirdiśet .
prāṇāyāmasamāyuktaṃ kuryātsāntapanaṃ tathā .. 18.7 ..
1.18.d:
उपेत्य तु स्त्रियं कामात् प्रायश्चित्तं विनिर्दिशेत् ।
प्राणायामसमायुक्तं कुर्यात्सान्तपनं तथा ॥ 18.7 ॥
1.18.m: If he approaches a woman out of lust, one should prescribe an expiation: / he should perform the Sāntapana penance accompanied by breath-control.

1.18.s:
tata ścarati nirddeśaṃ kṛcchrasyānte samāhitaḥ.
punarāśramamāgamya caredbhikṣuratandritaḥ .
na marmayuktaṃ vacanaṃ hinastīti manīṣiṇaḥ .. 18.8 ..
1.18.d:
तत श्चरति निर्द्देशं कृच्छ्रस्यान्ते समाहितः।
पुनराश्रममागम्य चरेद्भिक्षुरतन्द्रितः ।
न मर्मयुक्तं वचनं हिनस्तीति मनीषिणः ॥ 18.8 ॥
1.18.m: Then, concentrated, he carries out the prescribed instruction at the end of the Kṛcchra penance; / returning again to his stage of life, the mendicant should wander unwearied. / Wise men say that speech devoid of cutting words does not injure.

1.18.s:
tathāpi ca na karttavyaḥ prasaṅgo hyeṣa dāruṇaḥ.
ahorātrādhikaḥ kaścinnāstyadharma iti śrutiḥ .. 18.9 ..
1.18.d:
तथापि च न कर्त्तव्यः प्रसङ्गो ह्येष दारुणः।
अहोरात्राधिकः कश्चिन्नास्त्यधर्म इति श्रुतिः ॥ 18.9 ॥
1.18.m: Even so, such disastrous association must not be formed; / the Vedic revelation says that there is no adharma exceeding a whole day and night.

1.18.s:
hiṃsā hyeṣā parā sṛṣṭā daivatairmunibhistathā.
yadetaddraviṇaṃ nāma prāṇā hyete bahiścarāḥ.
sa tasya harati prāṇān yo yasya harate dhanam .. 18.10 ..
1.18.d:
हिंसा ह्येषा परा सृष्टा दैवतैर्मुनिभिस्तथा।
यदेतद्द्रविणं नाम प्राणा ह्येते बहिश्चराः।
स तस्य हरति प्राणान् यो यस्य हरते धनम् ॥ 18.10 ॥
1.18.m: For this violence has been created as the highest by the deities and seers; / that which is called wealth—these are vital breaths circulating outside; / whoever takes away another's wealth takes away his vital breaths.

1.18.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā sa duṣṭātmā bhinnavṛtto vratāccyutaḥ.
bhūyo nirvedamāpannaścareccāndrāyaṇaṃ vratam .. 18.11 ..
1.18.d:
एवं कृत्वा स दुष्टात्मा भिन्नवृत्तो व्रताच्च्युतः।
भूयो निर्वेदमापन्नश्चरेच्चान्द्रायणं व्रतम् ॥ 18.11 ॥
1.18.m: Having done this, that evil-minded one, broken in conduct and fallen from his vow, / having attained disgust with worldly life once more, should perform the Cāndrāyaṇa vow.

1.18.s:
vidhinā śāstradṛṣṭena saṃvatsaramiti śrutiḥ.
tataḥ saṃvatsarasyānte bhūyaḥ prakṣīṇakalmaṣaḥ.
bhūyo nirvedamāpannaścareccāndrāyaṇaṃ vratam .. 18.12 ..
1.18.d:
विधिना शास्त्रदृष्टेन संवत्सरमिति श्रुतिः।
ततः संवत्सरस्यान्ते भूयः प्रक्षीणकल्मषः।
भूयो निर्वेदमापन्नश्चरेच्चान्द्रायणं व्रतम् ॥ 18.12 ॥
1.18.m: For a year according to the rule seen in scripture—so is the Vedic text. / Then, at the end of the year, his sins completely destroyed, / having attained disgust with worldly life once more, he should perform the Cāndrāyaṇa vow.

1.18.s:
ahiṃsā sarvabhūtānāṃ karmaṇā manasā girā .
akāmādapi hiṃseta yadi bhikṣuḥ paśūn mṛgān.
kṛcchrātikṛcchraṃ kurvīta cāndrāyaṇamathīpi vā .. 18.13 ..
1.18.d:
अहिंसा सर्वभूतानां कर्मणा मनसा गिरा ।
अकामादपि हिंसेत यदि भिक्षुः पशून् मृगान्।
कृच्छ्रातिकृच्छ्रं कुर्वीत चान्द्रायणमथीपि वा ॥ 18.13 ॥
1.18.m: Non-violence toward all beings in action, mind, and speech: / if a mendicant should unintentionally kill domestic or wild animals, / he should perform the Kṛcchrātikṛcchra penance, or else the Cāndrāyaṇa.

1.18.s:
skandedindriyadaurbalyāt striyaṃ dṛṣṭvā yatiryadi.
tena dhārayitavyā vai prāṇāyāmāstu ṣoḍaśa .. 18.14 ..
1.18.d:
स्कन्देदिन्द्रियदौर्बल्यात् स्त्रियं दृष्ट्वा यतिर्यदि।
तेन धारयितव्या वै प्राणायामास्तु षोडश ॥ 18.14 ॥
1.18.m: If an ascetic should discharge semen out of weakness of the senses upon seeing a woman, / he must indeed retain sixteen breath-controls.

1.18.s:
divā skannasya viprasya prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate.
trirātramupavāsaśca prāṇāyāmaśataṃ tathā .. 18.15 ..
1.18.d:
दिवा स्कन्नस्य विप्रस्य प्रायश्चित्तं विधीयते।
त्रिरात्रमुपवासश्च प्राणायामशतं तथा ॥ 18.15 ॥
1.18.m: For a Brahmin who has discharged during the day, an expiation is prescribed: / a fast of three nights and a hundred breath-controls.

1.18.s:
rātrau skannaḥ śuciḥ srātodvādaśaiva tu dhāraṇāḥ.
prāṇāyāmena śuddhātmā virajā jāyate dvijaḥ .. 18.16 ..
1.18.d:
रात्रौ स्कन्नः शुचिः स्रातोद्वादशैव तु धारणाः।
प्राणायामेन शुद्धात्मा विरजा जायते द्विजः ॥ 18.16 ॥
1.18.m: If he has nocturnal emission, [becoming] pure and bathed, [performing] twelve dhāraṇās / with breath-control, the twice-born becomes purified in self and free of passion.

1.18.s:
ekānnaṃ madhu māṃsaṃ vā hyāmaśrāddhaṃ tathaiva ca.
abhojyāni yatīnāñca pratyakṣalavaṇāni ca .. 18.17 ..
1.18.d:
एकान्नं मधु मांसं वा ह्यामश्राद्धं तथैव च।
अभोज्यानि यतीनाञ्च प्रत्यक्षलवणानि च ॥ 18.17 ॥
1.18.m: Food from a single house, honey, meat, or uncooked food from an ancestral rite, / and visible salt—these are unfit for ascetics to eat.

1.18.s:
ekaikātikrame teṣāṃ prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate.
prājāpatyena kṛcchreṇa tataḥ pāpāt pramucyate .. 18.18 ..
1.18.d:
एकैकातिक्रमे तेषां प्रायश्चित्तं विधीयते।
प्राजापत्येन कृच्छ्रेण ततः पापात् प्रमुच्यते ॥ 18.18 ॥
1.18.m: For each transgression of these, an expiation is prescribed: / by means of the Prājāpatya penance, he is freed from that sin.

1.18.s:
vyatikramācca ye kecidvāṅmanaḥkāyasambhavam.
sadbhiḥ saha viniścitya yadbrūyustatsamācaret .. 18.19 ..
1.18.d:
व्यतिक्रमाच्च ये केचिद्वाङ्मनःकायसम्भवम्।
सद्भिः सह विनिश्चित्य यद्ब्रूयुस्तत्समाचरेत् ॥ 18.19 ॥
1.18.m: And whatever transgressions may arise from speech, mind, and body, / having determined [them] with the virtuous, he should perform whatever they say.

1.18.s:
viśuddhabuddhiḥ samaloṣṭakāñcanaḥ samastabhūteṣu caran sa māhitaḥ .
sthānaṃ dhruvaṃ śāśvatamavyayaṃ satāṃ paraṃ sa gatvā na punarhi jāyate .. 18.20 ..
1.18.d:
विशुद्धबुद्धिः समलोष्टकाञ्चनः समस्तभूतेषु चरन् स माहितः ।
स्थानं ध्रुवं शाश्वतमव्ययं सतां परं स गत्वा न पुनर्हि जायते ॥ 18.20 ॥
1.18.m: Purified in intellect, viewing a lump of earth and gold as equal, moving among all beings collected in mind, / having gone to the supreme, firm, eternal, and imperishable abode of the virtuous, he is indeed not born again.

1.18.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte yatiprāyaśvittavidhirnāmāṣṭādaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 18 ..
1.18.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते यतिप्रायश्वित्तविधिर्नामाष्टादशोऽध्यायः ॥ 18 ॥
1.18.m: Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, named ‘The Rules of Expiation for Ascetics,’ in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.19.s: .. vāyuruvāca ..
1.19.d: ॥ वायुरुवाच ॥
1.19.m:
Vāyu said:
Hereafter I shall explain the portents of death; listen,
by which particular knowledge one sees one's own death.

1.19.s:
ata ūrddhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi ariṣṭāni nibodhata.
yena jñānaviśeṣeṇa mṛtyuṃ paśyati cātmanaḥ .. 19.1 ..
1.19.d:
अत ऊर्द्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि अरिष्टानि निबोधत।
येन ज्ञानविशेषेण मृत्युं पश्यति चात्मनः ॥ 19.1 ॥

1.19.s:
arundhatīṃ dhruvañcaiva somacchāyāṃ mahāpatham.
yo na paśyetsa no jīvennaraḥ saṃvatsarātparam .. 19.2 ..
1.19.d:
अरुन्धतीं ध्रुवञ्चैव सोमच्छायां महापथम्।
यो न पश्येत्स नो जीवेन्नरः संवत्सरात्परम् ॥ 19.2 ॥
1.19.m: A man who cannot see Arundhatī, the Pole Star, the shadow of the moon, or the great highway [of the sky] / will not live beyond a year.

1.19.s:
araśmivantamādityaṃ raśmivantañca pāvakam.
yaḥ paśyenna ca jīveta māsādekādaśātparam .. 19.3 ..
1.19.d:
अरश्मिवन्तमादित्यं रश्मिवन्तञ्च पावकम्।
यः पश्येन्न च जीवेत मासादेकादशात्परम् ॥ 19.3 ॥
1.19.m: One who sees the sun without rays and the fire with rays / will not live beyond eleven months.

1.19.s:
vamenmūtraṃ karīṣaṃ vā suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tathā.
pratyakṣamatha vā svapne daśamāsān sa jīvati .. 19.4 ..
1.19.d:
वमेन्मूत्रं करीषं वा सुवर्णं रजतं तथा।
प्रत्यक्षमथ वा स्वप्ने दशमासान् स जीवति ॥ 19.4 ॥
1.19.m: If one vomits urine or feces, or gold or silver, / whether in waking reality or in a dream, he lives for ten months.

1.19.s:
agrataḥ pṛṣṭhato vāpi khaṇṭaṃ yasya padambhavet.
pāṃsule kardame vāpi saptamāsān sa jīvati .. 19.5 ..
1.19.d:
अग्रतः पृष्ठतो वापि खण्टं यस्य पदम्भवेत्।
पांसुले कर्दमे वापि सप्तमासान् स जीवति ॥ 19.5 ॥
1.19.m: He whose footprint is missing in front or behind, / whether in dust or in mud, lives for seven months.

1.19.s:
kākaḥ kapoto gṛdhro vā nilīyedyasya mūrddhani.
kravyādo vā khagaḥ kaścit ṣaṇmāsānnātivarttate .. 19.6 ..
1.19.d:
काकः कपोतो गृध्रो वा निलीयेद्यस्य मूर्द्धनि।
क्रव्यादो वा खगः कश्चित् षण्मासान्नातिवर्त्तते ॥ 19.6 ॥
1.19.m: He upon whose head a crow, a pigeon, or a vulture perches, / or any flesh-eating bird, does not survive past six months.

1.19.s:
badhye dvāyasapaṅktībhiḥ pāṃśuvarṣaiṇa vā punaḥ.
chāyāṃ vā vikṛtāṃ paśyeccatuḥpañca sa jīvati .. 19.7 ..
1.19.d:
बध्ये द्वायसपङ्क्तीभिः पांशुवर्षैण वा पुनः।
छायां वा विकृतां पश्येच्चतुःपञ्च स जीवति ॥ 19.7 ॥
1.19.m: If one is beset by rows of crows or by showers of dust, / or sees a distorted shadow, he lives for four or five [months].

1.19.s:
anabhre vidyutaṃ paśyeddakṣiṇāṃ diśamāśritām.
udakendradha nurvāpi trayo dvauvā sa jīvati .. 19.8 ..
1.19.d:
अनभ्रे विद्युतं पश्येद्दक्षिणां दिशमाश्रिताम्।
उदकेन्द्रध नुर्वापि त्रयो द्वौवा स जीवति ॥ 19.8 ॥
1.19.m: If one sees lightning in a cloudless sky resting in the southern direction, / or a rainbow in the north, he lives for three or two [months].

1.19.s:
apsu vā yadi vā''darśe ātmānaṃ yo na paśyati.
aśiraskaṃ tathātmānaṃ māsādūrddhvaṃ na jīvati .. 19.9 ..
1.19.d:
अप्सु वा यदि वा'ऽदर्शे आत्मानं यो न पश्यति।
अशिरस्कं तथात्मानं मासादूर्द्ध्वं न जीवति ॥ 19.9 ॥
1.19.m: One who does not see himself in water or in a mirror, / or likewise [sees] himself headless, does not live beyond a month.

1.19.s:
śavagandhi bhavedgātraṃ vasāgandhi hyathāpi vā.
mṛtyurhyupasthitastasya arddhamāsaṃ sa jīvati .. 19.10 ..
1.19.d:
शवगन्धि भवेद्गात्रं वसागन्धि ह्यथापि वा।
मृत्युर्ह्युपस्थितस्तस्य अर्द्धमासं स जीवति ॥ 19.10 ॥
1.19.m: If his body smells like a corpse or smells like marrow, / death is indeed near for him; he lives for half a month.

1.19.s:
sambhinno māruto yasya marmasthānāni kṛntati .
adbhiḥ spṛṣṭo na dṛṣyecca tasya mṛtyurupasthitaḥ .. 19.11 ..
1.19.d:
सम्भिन्नो मारुतो यस्य मर्मस्थानानि कृन्तति ।
अद्भिः स्पृष्टो न दृष्येच्च तस्य मृत्युरुपस्थितः ॥ 19.11 ॥
1.19.m: He whose disturbed vital wind tears his vital spots, / and does not dry when touched by water—death is near for him.

1.19.s:
ṛkṣavānarayuktena rathenāśāntu dakṣiṇām .
gāyannatha vrajet svapne vidyānmṛtyurupasthitaḥ .. 19.12 ..
1.19.d:
ऋक्षवानरयुक्तेन रथेनाशान्तु दक्षिणाम् ।
गायन्नथ व्रजेत् स्वप्ने विद्यान्मृत्युरुपस्थितः ॥ 19.12 ॥
1.19.m: If one should go toward the southern quarter in a chariot yoked with bears and monkeys / while singing in a dream, one should know that death is near.

1.19.s:
kṛṣṇāmba radharā śyāmā gāyantī vātha cāṅganā.
yannayeddakṣiṇāmāśāṃ svapne so'pi na jīvati .. 19.13 ..
1.19.d:
कृष्णाम्ब रधरा श्यामा गायन्ती वाथ चाङ्गना।
यन्नयेद्दक्षिणामाशां स्वप्ने सोऽपि न जीवति ॥ 19.13 ॥
1.19.m: Or if a dark woman wearing black garments and singing / should lead him to the southern quarter in a dream, he also does not live.

1.19.s:
chidraṃ vāsaśacava kṛṣṇañca svapre yo vidhṛyānnaraḥ .
bhagnaṃ vā śravaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā vidyānmṛtyurupasthitaḥ .. 19.14 ..
1.19.d:
छिद्रं वासशचव कृष्णञ्च स्वप्रे यो विधृयान्नरः ।
भग्नं वा श्रवणं दृष्ट्वा विद्यान्मृत्युरुपस्थितः ॥ 19.14 ॥
1.19.m: A man who wears torn or black clothing in a dream, / or sees an ear broken, should know that death is near.

1.19.s:
āmastakatalādyastu nimajjetpaṅkasāgare.
dṛṣṭvā tu tādṛśaṃ svapnaṃ sadya eva na jīvati .. 19.15 ..
1.19.d:
आमस्तकतलाद्यस्तु निमज्जेत्पङ्कसागरे।
दृष्ट्वा तु तादृशं स्वप्नं सद्य एव न जीवति ॥ 19.15 ॥
1.19.m: One who plunges up to the crown of his head into a sea of mud— / having seen such a dream, he does not live long at all.

1.19.s:
bhasmāṅgārāśca keśāṃśca nadīṃ śuṣkāṃ bhujaṅgamān.
paśyedyo daśarātrantu na sa jīveta tādṛśaḥ .. 19.16 ..
1.19.d:
भस्माङ्गाराश्च केशांश्च नदीं शुष्कां भुजङ्गमान्।
पश्येद्यो दशरात्रन्तु न स जीवेत तादृशः ॥ 19.16 ॥
1.19.m: One who sees ashes, coals, hair, a dried-up river, and serpents / for ten nights—such a person will not live.

1.19.s:
kṛṣṇaiśca vikaṭaiścaiva puruṣairudyatāyudhaiḥ.
pāṣāṇaistāḍyate svapne yaḥ sadyo na sa jīvati .. 19.17 ..
1.19.d:
कृष्णैश्च विकटैश्चैव पुरुषैरुद्यतायुधैः।
पाषाणैस्ताड्यते स्वप्ने यः सद्यो न स जीवति ॥ 19.17 ॥
1.19.m: One who is struck with stones in a dream by black, hideous men / with upraised weapons does not live long at all.

1.19.s:
sūryodaye pratyuṣasi pratyakṣaṃ yasya vai śivā.
krośantī sammukhābhyeti ma gatāyurbhavennaraḥ .. 19.18 ..
1.19.d:
सूर्योदये प्रत्युषसि प्रत्यक्षं यस्य वै शिवा।
क्रोशन्ती सम्मुखाभ्येति म गतायुर्भवेन्नरः ॥ 19.18 ॥
1.19.m: At sunrise or at dawn, a man toward whom a female jackal / comes facing him and howling before his eyes, his life has come to an end.

1.19.s:
yasya vai srātamātrasya hṛdayaṃ pīṅyate bhṛśam.
jāyate dantaharṣaśca taṃ gatāyuṣamādiśet .. 19.19 ..
1.19.d:
यस्य वै स्रातमात्रस्य हृदयं पीङ्यते भृशम्।
जायते दन्तहर्षश्च तं गतायुषमादिशेत् ॥ 19.19 ॥
1.19.m: He whose heart aches severely just after bathing, / and whose teeth chatter, one should declare his life to have come to an end.

1.19.s:
bhūyo bhūyaḥ śvasedyastu rātrau vā yadi vā divā.
dīpagandhañca no vetti vidyānmṛtyumupasthitam .. 19.20 ..
1.19.d:
भूयो भूयः श्वसेद्यस्तु रात्रौ वा यदि वा दिवा।
दीपगन्धञ्च नो वेत्ति विद्यान्मृत्युमुपस्थितम् ॥ 19.20 ॥
1.19.m: One who gasps again and again, whether at night or by day, / and does not perceive the smell of a lamp, should know that death is near.

1.19.s:
rātrau cendrāyudhaṃ paśyeddivā nakṣatramaṇḍalam.
paranetreṣu cātmānaṃ na paśyenna sa jīvati .. 19.21 ..
1.19.d:
रात्रौ चेन्द्रायुधं पश्येद्दिवा नक्षत्रमण्डलम्।
परनेत्रेषु चात्मानं न पश्येन्न स जीवति ॥ 19.21 ॥
1.19.m: If one sees a rainbow at night and a circle of stars by day, / and does not see himself in the eyes of others, he does not live.

1.19.s:
netramekaṃ sravedyasya karṇau sthānācca bhraśyataḥ.
nāsā ca vakrā bhavati sa jñeyo gatajīvitaḥ .. 19.22 ..
1.19.d:
नेत्रमेकं स्रवेद्यस्य कर्णौ स्थानाच्च भ्रश्यतः।
नासा च वक्रा भवति स ज्ञेयो गतजीवितः ॥ 19.22 ॥
1.19.m: He whose one eye waters, whose ears slip from their place, / and whose nose becomes crooked, is to be known as one whose life is gone.

1.19.s:
yasya kṛṣṇā kharā jihvā paṅkabhāsañca vai mukham.
gaṇḍe cipiṭake rakte tasya mṛtyurupasthitaḥ .. 19.23 ..
1.19.d:
यस्य कृष्णा खरा जिह्वा पङ्कभासञ्च वै मुखम्।
गण्डे चिपिटके रक्ते तस्य मृत्युरुपस्थितः ॥ 19.23 ॥
1.19.m: He whose tongue is black and rough, whose face looks like mud, / and whose cheeks are flattened and red—death is near for him.

1.19.s:
muktakeśo hasaṃścaiva gāyan nṛtyaṃśca yo naraḥ.
yāmyāśābhimukho gacchettadantaṃ tasya jīvitam .. 19.24 ..
1.19.d:
मुक्तकेशो हसंश्चैव गायन् नृत्यंश्च यो नरः।
याम्याशाभिमुखो गच्छेत्तदन्तं तस्य जीवितम् ॥ 19.24 ॥
1.19.m: A man with disheveled hair, laughing, singing, and dancing, / who walks facing the southern quarter—his life is at an end.

1.19.s:
yasya svedasamudbhūtāḥ śvetasarṣapasannibhāḥ.
svedā bhavanti hyasakṛttasya mṛtyurupaśthitaḥ .. 19.25 ..
1.19.d:
यस्य स्वेदसमुद्भूताः श्वेतसर्षपसन्निभाः।
स्वेदा भवन्ति ह्यसकृत्तस्य मृत्युरुपश्थितः ॥ 19.25 ॥
1.19.m: He on whose body sweat resembling white mustard seeds arises / repeatedly—death is near for him.

1.19.s:
uṣṭhrā vā rāsabhā vāpi yuktāḥ svpare rathe'śubhāḥ.
yasya sopi na jīveta dakṣiṇābhimukho gataḥ .. 19.26 ..
1.19.d:
उष्ठ्रा वा रासभा वापि युक्ताः स्व्परे रथेऽशुभाः।
यस्य सोपि न जीवेत दक्षिणाभिमुखो गतः ॥ 19.26 ॥
1.19.m: He whose inauspicious chariot in a dream has camels or donkeys yoked to it, / and who goes facing the south, will not live either.

1.19.s:
dve cātra parame'riṣṭe etadrūpaṃ paraṃ bhavet.
ghoṣaṃ na śrṛṇuyāt karṇe jyotirnnetre na paśyati .. 19.27 ..
1.19.d:
द्वे चात्र परमेऽरिष्टे एतद्रूपं परं भवेत्।
घोषं न श्रृणुयात् कर्णे ज्योतिर्न्नेत्रे न पश्यति ॥ 19.27 ॥
1.19.m: And here are two supreme portents; this supreme sign occurs: / he does not hear a sound in his ear, and he does not see light in his eye.

1.19.s:
śvabhreyo nipatet svapne dvārañcāsya na vidyate.
na cotiṣṭhati yaḥ śvabrāttadantaṃ tasya jīvitam .. 19.28 ..
1.19.d:
श्वभ्रेयो निपतेत् स्वप्ने द्वारञ्चास्य न विद्यते।
न चोतिष्ठति यः श्वब्रात्तदन्तं तस्य जीवितम् ॥ 19.28 ॥
1.19.m: He who falls into a pit in a dream and there is no exit for him, / and who does not rise from the pit—his life is at an end.

1.19.s:
ūrddhvā ca dṛṣṭirna ca sampratiṣṭhā raktā punaḥ samparivarttamānā.
mukhasya coṣmā muṣirā ca nābhiratyuṣṇamūtro viṣamastha eva .. 19.29 ..
1.19.d:
ऊर्द्ध्वा च दृष्टिर्न च सम्प्रतिष्ठा रक्ता पुनः सम्परिवर्त्तमाना।
मुखस्य चोष्मा मुषिरा च नाभिरत्युष्णमूत्रो विषमस्थ एव ॥ 19.29 ॥
1.19.m: Upward gaze with no fixed focus, red and rolling, / heat in the mouth, a hollow navel, and very hot urine—he is in a critical condition.

1.19.s:
divā vā yati vā rātrau pratyakṣaṃ yo'bhihanyate.
taṃ paśyedatha hantāraṃ sa hatastu na jīvati .. 19.30 ..
1.19.d:
दिवा वा यति वा रात्रौ प्रत्यक्षं योऽभिहन्यते।
तं पश्येदथ हन्तारं स हतस्तु न जीवति ॥ 19.30 ॥
1.19.m: He who is struck down visibly, by day or by night, / and sees the slayer—struck down, he does not live.

1.19.s:
agnipraveśaṃ kurute svapnānte yastu mānavaḥ.
smṛtiṃ nopalabheccāpi tadantaṃ tasya jīvitam .. 19.31 ..
1.19.d:
अग्निप्रवेशं कुरुते स्वप्नान्ते यस्तु मानवः।
स्मृतिं नोपलभेच्चापि तदन्तं तस्य जीवितम् ॥ 19.31 ॥
1.19.m: A person who enters into fire at the end of a dream / and does not regain consciousness—his life is at an end.

1.19.s:
yastu prāvaraṇaṃ śuklaṃ svakaṃ paśyati mānavaḥ.
raktaṃ kṛṣṇamapi svapne tasya mṛtyurupasthitaḥ .. 19.32 ..
1.19.d:
यस्तु प्रावरणं शुक्लं स्वकं पश्यति मानवः।
रक्तं कृष्णमपि स्वप्ने तस्य मृत्युरुपस्थितः ॥ 19.32 ॥
1.19.m: A person who sees his own white upper garment / as red or black in a dream—death is near for him.

1.19.s:
ariṣṭasūcite dehe tasmin kāla upāgate.
tyaktvā bhayaviṣādañca udgacchedūbhuddhimānnaraḥ .. 19.33 ..
1.19.d:
अरिष्टसूचिते देहे तस्मिन् काल उपागते।
त्यक्त्वा भयविषादञ्च उद्गच्छेदूभुद्धिमान्नरः ॥ 19.33 ॥
1.19.m: When that time arrives, indicated by portents in the body, / the wise man, having abandoned fear and despondency, should depart.

1.19.s:
prācīṃ vā yadi vodīcīṃ diśaṃ niṣkramya vai śuciḥ.
same'tisthāvare deśe vivikte janavarjjite .. 19.34 ..
1.19.d:
प्राचीं वा यदि वोदीचीं दिशं निष्क्रम्य वै शुचिः।
समेऽतिस्थावरे देशे विविक्ते जनवर्ज्जिते ॥ 19.34 ॥
1.19.m: Having gone out pure toward the eastern or northern quarter, / in an even, very firm place, solitary and devoid of people,

1.19.s:
udaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukho vā svasthaḥ svācānta eva ca.
svastikopaniviṣṭaśca namaskṛtya maheśvaram.
samakāyaśirogrīvaṃ dhāryennāvalokayet .. 19.35 ..
1.19.d:
उदङ्मुखः प्राङ्मुखो वा स्वस्थः स्वाचान्त एव च।
स्वस्तिकोपनिविष्टश्च नमस्कृत्य महेश्वरम्।
समकायशिरोग्रीवं धार्येन्नावलोकयेत् ॥ 19.35 ॥
1.19.m: facing north or facing east, composed and having sipped water, / seated in the svastika posture, having bowed to Maheśvara, / holding body, head, and neck aligned, he should not look around.

1.19.s:
yathā dīpo nivātasyo neṅgate sopamā smṛtā.
prāgudakpravaṇe deśe tasmādyuñjīta yogavit .. 19.36 ..
1.19.d:
यथा दीपो निवातस्यो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता।
प्रागुदक्प्रवणे देशे तस्माद्युञ्जीत योगवित् ॥ 19.36 ॥
1.19.m: ‘As a lamp placed in a windless spot does not flicker’—that traditional simile is recalled; / therefore, in a place sloping to the east or north, the knower of yoga should engage in yoga.

1.19.s:
prāṇe ca ramate nityaṃ cakṣuṣoḥ sparśane tathā.
śrotre manasi buddhau ca tathā vakṣasi dhārayet.
na tasya dhāraṇāyogādvāyuḥ sarvaṃ pravarttate .. 19.37 ..
1.19.d:
प्राणे च रमते नित्यं चक्षुषोः स्पर्शने तथा।
श्रोत्रे मनसि बुद्धौ च तथा वक्षसि धारयेत्।
न तस्य धारणायोगाद्वायुः सर्वं प्रवर्त्तते ॥ 19.37 ॥
1.19.m:
And he always delights in the breath; likewise, in the eyes and the sense of touch,
in the ears, the mind, and the intellect, and thus one should hold [it] in the chest.
Through the practice of fixation, his wind does not stir at all.

1.19.s:
kālagharmajhca vijñāya samūha़ñcaiva sarvaśaḥ.
dvādaśādhyātmamityevaṃ yogadhāraṇamucyate .. 19.38 ..
1.19.d:
कालघर्मझ्च विज्ञाय समूह़ञ्चैव सर्वशः।
द्वादशाध्यात्ममित्येवं योगधारणमुच्यते ॥ 19.38 ॥
1.19.m:
Having understood time, heat, and the gathering [of elements] in every respect,
fixation in yoga is said to consist of twelve internal faculties.

1.19.s:
śatamaṣṭa śataṃ vāpi dhāraṇāṃ mūrdhni dhārayet.
na tasya dhāraṇāyogādvāyuḥ sarvaṃ pravartate .. 19.39 ..
1.19.d:
शतमष्ट शतं वापि धारणां मूर्ध्नि धारयेत्।
न तस्य धारणायोगाद्वायुः सर्वं प्रवर्तते ॥ 19.39 ॥
1.19.m:
One should hold the fixation in the crown of the head for a hundred or a hundred and eight [measures].
Through the practice of fixation, his wind does not stir at all.

1.19.s:
tatastvāpūrayeddehamoṅkāreṇa samāhitaḥ.
athoṅkāramayo yogī na kṣarettvakṣarī bhavet . 19.40 ..
1.19.d:
ततस्त्वापूरयेद्देहमोङ्कारेण समाहितः।
अथोङ्कारमयो योगी न क्षरेत्त्वक्षरी भवेत् । 19.40 ॥
1.19.m:
Then, collected in mind, one should fill the body with the syllable Om;
then the yogin who consists of the syllable Om will not perish, but becomes imperishable.

1.19.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte ariṣṭāni nāmaikonaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 19 ..
1.19.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते अरिष्टानि नामैकोनविंशोऽध्यायः ॥ 19 ॥
1.19.m: Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, named 'The Portents of Death', in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa proclaimed by Vāyu.

1.20.s: .. vāyuruvāca ..
1.20.d: ॥ वायुरुवाच ॥
1.20.m:
Vāyu said:
Hereafter I shall explain the characteristics of the attainment of the syllable Om.
This is to be known as having three morae, with consonant and vowel here.

1.20.s:
ata ūrddhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi oṅkāraprāptilakṣaṇam.
eṣa trimātro vijñeyo vyañjanañcātra sasvaram .. 20.1 ..
1.20.d:
अत ऊर्द्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि ओङ्कारप्राप्तिलक्षणम्।
एष त्रिमात्रो विज्ञेयो व्यञ्जनञ्चात्र सस्वरम् ॥ 20.1 ॥

1.20.s:
prathamā vaidyutī mātrā dvitīyā tāmasī smṛtā.
tṛtīyā nirguṇī vidyānmātrāmakṣaragāminīm .. 20.2 ..
1.20.d:
प्रथमा वैद्युती मात्रा द्वितीया तामसी स्मृता।
तृतीया निर्गुणी विद्यान्मात्रामक्षरगामिनीम् ॥ 20.2 ॥
1.20.m:
The first measure is flash-like; the second is remembered as dark;
one should know the third measure to be devoid of qualities and entering the imperishable.

1.20.s:
gandharvīti ca vijñeyo gāndhārasvarasambhavā.
pipīlikāsamasparśā prayuktā mūrdni lakṣyate .. 20.3 ..
1.20.d:
गन्धर्वीति च विज्ञेयो गान्धारस्वरसम्भवा।
पिपीलिकासमस्पर्शा प्रयुक्ता मूर्द्नि लक्ष्यते ॥ 20.3 ॥
1.20.m:
It is also known as gandharvī, arising from the gāndhāra musical note;
applied, its touch is like that of an ant, and it is perceived in the crown of the head.

1.20.s:
tathā prayuktamoṅkāraṃ pratinirvāti mūrddhani .
tathoṅkāramayo yogī hyakṣare tvakṣarī bhavet .. 20.4 ..
1.20.d:
तथा प्रयुक्तमोङ्कारं प्रतिनिर्वाति मूर्द्धनि ।
तथोङ्कारमयो योगी ह्यक्षरे त्वक्षरी भवेत् ॥ 20.4 ॥
1.20.m:
The syllable Om applied in this manner is extinguished in the crown of the head;
then the yogin who consists of the syllable Om indeed becomes imperishable in the Imperishable.

1.20.s:
praṇavo dhanuḥ śaro hyātmā brahma tallakṣyamucyate.
apramattena cedvadhyaṃ śaravattanmayo bhavet .. 20.5 ..
1.20.d:
प्रणवो धनुः शरो ह्यात्मा ब्रह्म तल्लक्ष्यमुच्यते।
अप्रमत्तेन चेद्वध्यं शरवत्तन्मयो भवेत् ॥ 20.5 ॥
1.20.m:
The praṇava is the bow, the self is the arrow, and Brahman is said to be its target.
It is to be pierced without distraction; like an arrow, one should become one with it.

1.20.s:
omityekākṣaraṃ brahma guhāyāṃ nihitaṃ padam.
omityetatrayo vedāstrayo lokāstrayo'gnayaḥ.
viṣṇukramāstrayastvete ṛksāmāni yajūṃṣi ca .. 20.6 ..
1.20.d:
ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म गुहायां निहितं पदम्।
ओमित्येतत्रयो वेदास्त्रयो लोकास्त्रयोऽग्नयः।
विष्णुक्रमास्त्रयस्त्वेते ऋक्सामानि यजूंषि च ॥ 20.6 ॥

1.20.s:
mātrāścātra catasrastu vijñeyāḥ paramārthataḥ.
tatra yuktaśca yo yogī tasya sālokyatāṃ vrajet .. 20.7 ..
1.20.d:
मात्राश्चात्र चतस्रस्तु विज्ञेयाः परमार्थतः।
तत्र युक्तश्च यो योगी तस्य सालोक्यतां व्रजेत् ॥ 20.7 ॥
1.20.m:
Four measures are to be recognized here in the ultimate truth;
and the yogin who is joined to it attains co-residence in its realm.

1.20.s:
akārastvakṣaro jñeya ukāraḥ svaritaḥ smṛtaḥ.
makārastu pluto jñeyastrimātra iti saṃjñitaḥ .. 20.8 ..
1.20.d:
अकारस्त्वक्षरो ज्ञेय उकारः स्वरितः स्मृतः।
मकारस्तु प्लुतो ज्ञेयस्त्रिमात्र इति संज्ञितः ॥ 20.8 ॥
1.20.m:
The sound 'a' should be known as imperishable; the sound 'u' is considered accented;
and the sound 'm' is known as prolated, termed three-measured.

1.20.s:
akārastvatha bhūrloka ukāro bhuvarucyate.
savyañjano makāraśca svarllokaśca vidhīyate .. 20.9 ..
1.20.d:
अकारस्त्वथ भूर्लोक उकारो भुवरुच्यते।
सव्यञ्जनो मकारश्च स्वर्ल्लोकश्च विधीयते ॥ 20.9 ॥
1.20.m:
The sound 'a' is the Bhūrloka; the sound 'u' is called Bhuvar;
and the sound 'm', with its consonant, is designated as the Svarloka.

1.20.s:
oṅkārastu trayo lokāḥ śirastasya triviṣṭapam.
bhuvanāntañca tatsarvaṃ brāhmaṃ tatpadamucyate .. 20.10 ..
1.20.d:
ओङ्कारस्तु त्रयो लोकाः शिरस्तस्य त्रिविष्टपम्।
भुवनान्तञ्च तत्सर्वं ब्राह्मं तत्पदमुच्यते ॥ 20.10 ॥
1.20.m:
The syllable Om is the three worlds; its head is heaven.
And all that extends to the end of the worlds is called the realm of Brahman.

1.20.s:
mātrāpadaṃ rudraloko hyamātrastu śivaṃ padam.
evandhyānaviśeṣeṇa tatpadaṃ samupāsate .. 20.11 ..
1.20.d:
मात्रापदं रुद्रलोको ह्यमात्रस्तु शिवं पदम्।
एवन्ध्यानविशेषेण तत्पदं समुपासते ॥ 20.11 ॥
1.20.m:
The state with measures is the realm of Rudra; the measureless is the state of Śiva.
In this way, through distinct meditation, they worship that state.

1.20.s:
tasmāddhayānaratirnityamamātraṃ hi tadakṣaram.
upāsyaṃ hi prayatnena śāśvataṃ padamicchatā .. 20.12 ..
1.20.d:
तस्माद्धयानरतिर्नित्यममात्रं हि तदक्षरम्।
उपास्यं हि प्रयत्नेन शाश्वतं पदमिच्छता ॥ 20.12 ॥
1.20.m:
Therefore, constantly delighting in meditation, that measureless, imperishable state
must be worshipped with effort by one who desires the eternal realm.

1.20.s:
hṛsvā tu prathamā mātrā tato dīrghā tvanantaram.
tataḥ plutavatī caiva tṛtīyā upadiśyate .. 20.13 ..
1.20.d:
हृस्वा तु प्रथमा मात्रा ततो दीर्घा त्वनन्तरम्।
ततः प्लुतवती चैव तृतीया उपदिश्यते ॥ 20.13 ॥
1.20.m:
The first measure is short; immediately following it is the long;
and then the third is taught as prolated.

1.20.s:
etāstu mātrā vijñeyā yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ .
yāvaccaiva tu śakyante dhāryante tāvadeva hi .. 20.14 ..
1.20.d:
एतास्तु मात्रा विज्ञेया यथावदनुपूर्वशः ।
यावच्चैव तु शक्यन्ते धार्यन्ते तावदेव हि ॥ 20.14 ॥
1.20.m:
These measures are to be understood in their proper sequence;
they are sustained as far and as long as one is able.

1.20.s:
indriyāṇi mano buddhiṃ dhyāyannātmani yaḥ sadā .
atrāṣṭamātramapicecchṛṇuyātphalamāpnuyāt .. 20.15 ..
1.20.d:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिं ध्यायन्नात्मनि यः सदा ।
अत्राष्टमात्रमपिचेच्छृणुयात्फलमाप्नुयात् ॥ 20.15 ॥
1.20.m:
He who, always meditating on the senses, mind, and intellect within the self,
were to hear here even an eighth of a measure, would attain the fruit:

1.20.s:
māse māse'śvamedhena yo yajeta śataṃ samāḥ .
na sa tat prāpnuyāt puṇyaṃ mātrayā yadavāpnuyāt .. 20.16 ..
1.20.d:
मासे मासेऽश्वमेधेन यो यजेत शतं समाः ।
न स तत् प्राप्नुयात् पुण्यं मात्रया यदवाप्नुयात् ॥ 20.16 ॥
1.20.m:
He who would sacrifice month after month with the horse sacrifice for a hundred years
would not attain the religious merit that one attains through a single measure.

1.20.s:
abbinduṃ yaḥ kuśāgreṇa māse māse pibennaraḥ.
saṃvatsaraśataṃ pūrṇaṃ mātrayā tadavāpnuyāt .. 20.17 ..
1.20.d:
अब्बिन्दुं यः कुशाग्रेण मासे मासे पिबेन्नरः।
संवत्सरशतं पूर्णं मात्रया तदवाप्नुयात् ॥ 20.17 ॥
1.20.m:
The man who would drink a drop of water with the tip of a kuśa blade month after month
for a full hundred years attains that through a single measure.

1.20.s:
iṣṭāpūrttasya yajñasya satyavākye ca yat phalam.
abhakṣaṇe ca māṃsasya mātrayā tadavāpnuyāt .. 20.18 ..
1.20.d:
इष्टापूर्त्तस्य यज्ञस्य सत्यवाक्ये च यत् फलम्।
अभक्षणे च मांसस्य मात्रया तदवाप्नुयात् ॥ 20.18 ॥
1.20.m:
Whatever fruit comes from sacrifices, charitable works, and speaking the truth,
and from refraining from eating meat, one attains through a single measure.

1.20.s:
svāmyarthe yudhyamānānāṃ śūrāṇāmanivarttinām.
yadbhavettat phalaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ mātrayā tadavāpnuyāt .. 20.19 ..
1.20.d:
स्वाम्यर्थे युध्यमानानां शूराणामनिवर्त्तिनाम्।
यद्भवेत्तत् फलं दृष्टं मात्रया तदवाप्नुयात् ॥ 20.19 ॥
1.20.m:
Whatever recognized fruit belongs to heroes fighting for their lord without turning back,
that one attains through a single measure.

1.20.s:
na tathā tapasogreṇa na yajñairbhūridakṣiṇaiḥ.
yat phalaṃ prāpnuyāt samyag mātrayā tadavāpnuyāt .. 20.20 ..
1.20.d:
न तथा तपसोग्रेण न यज्ञैर्भूरिदक्षिणैः।
यत् फलं प्राप्नुयात् सम्यग् मात्रया तदवाप्नुयात् ॥ 20.20 ॥
1.20.m:
Not by severe asceticism, nor by sacrifices with lavish gifts,
does one attain the fruit that one attains properly through a single measure.

1.20.s:
tatra vai yo'rddhamātro yaḥ pluto nāmopadiśyate.
eṣā eva bhavet kāryā gṛhasthānāntu yoginām .. 20.21 ..
1.20.d:
तत्र वै योऽर्द्धमात्रो यः प्लुतो नामोपदिश्यते।
एषा एव भवेत् कार्या गृहस्थानान्तु योगिनाम् ॥ 20.21 ॥
1.20.m:
Among them, that which is half a measure, taught under the name 'prolated'—
this alone is to be practiced by householder yogins.

1.20.s:
eṣā caiva viśeṣeṇa aiśvaryasamalakṣaṇā.
yogināntu viśeṣeṇa aiśvarye hyaṣṭalakṣaṇe.
aṇimādyeti vijñeyā tasmādyuñjīta tāṃ dvijaḥ .. 20.22 ..
1.20.d:
एषा चैव विशेषेण ऐश्वर्यसमलक्षणा।
योगिनान्तु विशेषेण ऐश्वर्ये ह्यष्टलक्षणे।
अणिमाद्येति विज्ञेया तस्माद्युञ्जीत तां द्विजः ॥ 20.22 ॥

1.20.s:
evaṃ hi yogī saṃyuktaḥ śucirddānto jitendriyaḥ.
ātmānaṃ vindate yastu sa sarvaṃ vindate dvijaḥ .. 20.23 ..
1.20.d:
एवं हि योगी संयुक्तः शुचिर्द्दान्तो जितेन्द्रियः।
आत्मानं विन्दते यस्तु स सर्वं विन्दते द्विजः ॥ 20.23 ॥
1.20.m:
Thus the yogin who is unified, pure, self-controlled, with conquered senses,
who finds the self—that twice-born man finds everything.

1.20.s:
ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni vedopaniṣadastathā.
yogajñānādavāpnoti brāhmaṇo dhyānacintakaḥ .. 20.24 ..
1.20.d:
ऋचो यजूंषि सामानि वेदोपनिषदस्तथा।
योगज्ञानादवाप्नोति ब्राह्मणो ध्यानचिन्तकः ॥ 20.24 ॥
1.20.m:
Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman verses, and likewise the Upanisads of the Vedas,
the brāhmaṇa contemplating in meditation obtains through the knowledge of yoga.

1.20.s:
sarvabhūtalayo bhūtvā abhūtaḥ sa tu jāyate.
yogī saṅkramaṇaṃ kṛtvā yāti vai śāśvataṃ padam .. 20.25 ..
1.20.d:
सर्वभूतलयो भूत्वा अभूतः स तु जायते।
योगी सङ्क्रमणं कृत्वा याति वै शाश्वतं पदम् ॥ 20.25 ॥
1.20.m:
Having dissolved all beings, he becomes beyond material existence;
having made the transition, the yogin goes indeed to the eternal state.

1.20.s:
api cātra caturhastāṃ dhyāyamānaścaturmukhīm.
prakṛtiṃ viśvarūpākhyāṃ dṛṣṭvā divyena cakṣuṣā .. 20.26 ..
1.20.d:
अपि चात्र चतुर्हस्तां ध्यायमानश्चतुर्मुखीम्।
प्रकृतिं विश्वरूपाख्यां दृष्ट्वा दिव्येन चक्षुषा ॥ 20.26 ॥
1.20.m:
Moreover, meditating here on the four-armed, four-faced
primal matter called the omniform, having seen it with the divine eye:

1.20.s:
ajāmetāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇāṃ bahvīḥ prajāḥ sṛjamānāṃ svarūpām.
ajo hyeko juṣamāṇo'nuśete jahātyenāṃ bhuktabhogāmajo'nyaḥ.
aṣṭākṣarāṃ ṣoḍaśapāṇipādāṃ caturmukhīṃ triśikhāmekaśrṛṅgām.
ādyāmajāṃ viśvasṛjāṃ svarūpāṃ jñātvā budhāstvamṛtatvaṃ vrajanti.
ye brāhmaṇāḥ praṇavaṃ vedayanti na te punaḥ saṃsarantīha bhūyaḥ .. 20.27 ..
1.20.d:
अजामेतां लोहितशुक्लकृष्णां बह्वीः प्रजाः सृजमानां स्वरूपाम्।
अजो ह्येको जुषमाणोऽनुशेते जहात्येनां भुक्तभोगामजोऽन्यः।
अष्टाक्षरां षोडशपाणिपादां चतुर्मुखीं त्रिशिखामेकश्रृङ्गाम्।
आद्यामजां विश्वसृजां स्वरूपां ज्ञात्वा बुधास्त्वमृतत्वं व्रजन्ति।
ये ब्राह्मणाः प्रणवं वेदयन्ति न ते पुनः संसरन्तीह भूयः ॥ 20.27 ॥
1.20.m:
The unborn female, red, white, and black, producing many offspring like herself,
one unborn male lies beside and serves, while another unborn male abandons her once his enjoyment has been enjoyed.
Knowing the unborn, primordial female—having eight syllables, sixteen hands and feet, four faces, three crests, and a single horn, the form of the creators of the universe—the wise attain immortality.
Those brāhmaṇas who know the praṇava do not wander again in the cycle of rebirth in this world.

1.20.s:
ityetadakṣaraṃ brahma paramoṅkārasaṃjñitam.
yastu vedayate samyak tathā dhyāyati vā punaḥ .. 20.28 ..
1.20.d:
इत्येतदक्षरं ब्रह्म परमोङ्कारसंज्ञितम्।
यस्तु वेदयते सम्यक् तथा ध्यायति वा पुनः ॥ 20.28 ॥
1.20.m:
Thus is this imperishable Brahman named the supreme syllable Om.
He who knows it properly or meditates upon it again,

1.20.s:
saṃsāracakramutsṛjya muktabandhanabandhanaḥ.
acalaṃ nirguṇaṃ sthānaṃ śivaṃ prāpnotyasaṃśayaḥ.
ityetadvai mayā proktamoṅkāraprāptilakṣaṇam .. 20.29 ..
1.20.d:
संसारचक्रमुत्सृज्य मुक्तबन्धनबन्धनः।
अचलं निर्गुणं स्थानं शिवं प्राप्नोत्यसंशयः।
इत्येतद्वै मया प्रोक्तमोङ्कारप्राप्तिलक्षणम् ॥ 20.29 ॥
1.20.m:
having abandoned the wheel of the cycle of rebirth, freed from the bondage of bonds,
attains without doubt the unshakeable, quality-less, auspicious state of Śiva.
Thus indeed has the character of the attainment of the syllable Om been proclaimed by me.

1.20.s:
namo lokeśvarāya saṅkalpakalpagrahaṇāya mahāntamupatiṣṭhate tadvo hitaṃ yadbrahmaṇe namaḥ.
sarvatra sthānine nirguṇāya sambhaktayogīśvarāya ca ..
1.20.d:
नमो लोकेश्वराय सङ्कल्पकल्पग्रहणाय महान्तमुपतिष्ठते तद्वो हितं यद्ब्रह्मणे नमः।
सर्वत्र स्थानिने निर्गुणाय सम्भक्तयोगीश्वराय च ॥
1.20.m:
Homage to the Lord of the worlds, who grasps resolve and aeon. One approaches the Great One; that is for your benefit: homage to Brahman!
To the omnipresent, the qualityless, and the Lord of yogins who is shared [by all].
As a lotus leaf is cleansed by water, one should approach Brahman: the purifier among purifiers, filled with what purifies, by what purifies—short, long, and protracted. One should meditate upon this sacred syllable Oṃ, soundless, touchless, formless, tasteless, and odourless. Homage to the Lord of ignorance, of universal form—he has no equal—homage to the Lord of ignorance, to the Lord of yogins! By whom the fierce heaven and the firm earth [are held], by whom thunder sounds, by whom the sky is the atmospheric realm between both of them, these most excellent ones; the heart of the gods, of universal form—he has no likeness to incoming and outgoing breath. Oṃ is the universe; the universe is sacrifice; sacrifice is the Veda; the Veda is reverence; reverence is Rudra; homage to Rudra, the sovereign lord of yogins! Homage!
Thus is the invocation of attainment at evening, morning, and noon: 'Homage!'
Rudra yields the fruit of all desires.
As a ripe fruit falls from its stalk when shaken by the wind, / so through reverence to Rudra sin is destroyed.

1.20.s:
puṣkaraparṇamivādbhirviśuddhamiva brahmamupatiṣṭhetpavitraṃ pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ pavitreṇa paripūritena pavitreṇa hrasvandīrghaplutamiti tadetamoṅkāramaśabdamasparśamarūpamarasamagandhaṃ paryupāsīta avidyeśānāya viśvarūpo na tasya avidyeśānāya namo yogīśvarāyeti ca yena dyaurugrā pṛthivī ca dṛḍhā yena svastanitaṃ yena nākastayorantarikṣamime varīyaso devānāṃ hṛdayaṃ viśvarūpo na tasya prāṇāpānaupamyaṃ cāsti oṅkāroviśvaviśvā vai yajñaḥ yajño vai vedaḥ vedo vai namaskāraḥ namaskāro rudraḥ namo rudrāya yogeśvarādhipataye namaḥ.
iti siddhipratyupasthānaṃ sāyaṃprātarmadhyāhne namaḥ iti..
1.20.d:
पुष्करपर्णमिवाद्भिर्विशुद्धमिव ब्रह्ममुपतिष्ठेत्पवित्रं पवित्राणां पवित्रं पवित्रेण परिपूरितेन पवित्रेण ह्रस्वन्दीर्घप्लुतमिति तदेतमोङ्कारमशब्दमस्पर्शमरूपमरसमगन्धं पर्युपासीत अविद्येशानाय विश्वरूपो न तस्य अविद्येशानाय नमो योगीश्वरायेति च येन द्यौरुग्रा पृथिवी च दृढा येन स्वस्तनितं येन नाकस्तयोरन्तरिक्षमिमे वरीयसो देवानां हृदयं विश्वरूपो न तस्य प्राणापानौपम्यं चास्ति ओङ्कारोविश्वविश्वा वै यज्ञः यज्ञो वै वेदः वेदो वै नमस्कारः नमस्कारो रुद्रः नमो रुद्राय योगेश्वराधिपतये नमः।
इति सिद्धिप्रत्युपस्थानं सायंप्रातर्मध्याह्ने नमः इति॥

1.20.s:
sarvakāmaphalorudraḥ.
yathā vṛntāt phalaṃ pakvaṃ pavanena samīritam.
namaskāreṇa rudrasya tathā pāpaṃ praṇaśyati .. 20.30 ..
1.20.d:
सर्वकामफलोरुद्रः।
यथा वृन्तात् फलं पक्वं पवनेन समीरितम्।
नमस्कारेण रुद्रस्य तथा पापं प्रणश्यति ॥ 20.30 ॥

1.20.s:
yathā rudranamaskāraḥ sarvadharmaphalo dhruvaḥ.
anyadevanamaskāro na tat phalamavāpnuyāt .. 20.31 ..
1.20.d:
यथा रुद्रनमस्कारः सर्वधर्मफलो ध्रुवः।
अन्यदेवनमस्कारो न तत् फलमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 20.31 ॥
1.20.m: Just as homage to Rudra unfailingly yields the fruit of all dharmas, / homage to any other god does not attain such a fruit. // 20.31

1.20.s:
tasmāt triṣavaṇaṃ yogī upāsīta maheśvaram.
daśāvistārakaṃ brahma tathā ca brahma vistaram .. 20.32 ..
1.20.d:
तस्मात् त्रिषवणं योगी उपासीत महेश्वरम्।
दशाविस्तारकं ब्रह्म तथा च ब्रह्म विस्तरम् ॥ 20.32 ॥
1.20.m: Therefore, the yogin should worship Maheśvara at the three junctures of the day, / the Brahman that expands into ten, and the expansion of Brahman. // 20.32

1.20.s:
oṅkāraṃ sarvataḥ kāle sarvaṃ vihitavān prabhuḥ.
tena tena tu viṣṇutvaṃ namaskāraṃ mahāyaśāḥ .. 20.33 ..
1.20.d:
ओङ्कारं सर्वतः काले सर्वं विहितवान् प्रभुः।
तेन तेन तु विष्णुत्वं नमस्कारं महायशाः ॥ 20.33 ॥
1.20.m: The Lord ordained everything, the Oṅkāra, everywhere in time; / by each of these, indeed, Viṣṇu-hood [arose], the renowned homage. // 20.33

1.20.s:
namaskārastathā caiva praṇavastuvate prabhum .
praṇavaṃ stuvate yajño yajñaṃ saṃstuvate namaḥ.
namastuvati vai rudrastasmādrudrapadaṃ śivam .. 20.34 ..
1.20.d:
नमस्कारस्तथा चैव प्रणवस्तुवते प्रभुम् ।
प्रणवं स्तुवते यज्ञो यज्ञं संस्तुवते नमः।
नमस्तुवति वै रुद्रस्तस्माद्रुद्रपदं शिवम् ॥ 20.34 ॥
1.20.m: Homage and the Praṇava praise the Lord; / sacrifice praises the Praṇava, and homage praises sacrifice; / Rudra praises homage, and therefore the state of Rudra is auspicious. // 20.34

1.20.s:
ityetāni rahasyāni yatīnāṃ vai yathākramam.
yastu vedayate dhyānaṃ sa paraṃ prāpnuyātpadam .. 20.35 ..
1.20.d:
इत्येतानि रहस्यानि यतीनां वै यथाक्रमम्।
यस्तु वेदयते ध्यानं स परं प्राप्नुयात्पदम् ॥ 20.35 ॥
1.20.m: These are the secret teachings for ascetics in due order; / he who understands this meditation shall attain the supreme state. // 20.35

1.20.s:
iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte oṅkāraprāptilakṣaṇaṃ nāma viṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 20 ..
.. sūta uvāca ..
ṛṣīṇāmagnikalpānāṃ naimiṣāraṇyavāsinām .
ṛṣiḥ śrutidharaḥ prājñaḥ sāvarṇirnnāma nāmataḥ .. 21.1 ..
teṣāṃ sopyagrato bhūtvā vāyuṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ.
sātatyaṃ tatra kurvantaṃ priyārthe satrayājinām.
vinayenopasaṃgamya papraccha sa mahādyutim .. 21.2 ..

1.20.d:
इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते ओङ्कारप्राप्तिलक्षणं नाम विंशोऽध्यायः ॥ 20 ॥
॥ सूत उवाच ॥
ऋषीणामग्निकल्पानां नैमिषारण्यवासिनाम् ।
ऋषिः श्रुतिधरः प्राज्ञः सावर्णिर्न्नाम नामतः ॥ 21.1 ॥
तेषां सोप्यग्रतो भूत्वा वायुं वाक्यविशारदः।
सातत्यं तत्र कुर्वन्तं प्रियार्थे सत्रयाजिनाम्।
विनयेनोपसंगम्य पप्रच्छ स महाद्युतिम् ॥ 21.2 ॥
॥सावर्णिरुवाच ॥
विभो पुराणसं बद्धां कथां वै वेदसंमिताम्।
श्रोतुमिच्छामहे सम्यक् प्रसादात्सर्वदर्शिनः ॥ 21.3 ॥
हिरण्यगर्भो भगवान् ललाटान्नीललोहितम्।
कथं तत्तेजसं देवं लब्धवान् पुत्रमात्मनः ॥ 21.4 ॥
कथं च भगवान् जज्ञे ब्रह्मा कमलसंभवः।
रुद्रत्वं चैव सर्वस्य स्वात्मजस्य कथं पुनः ॥ 21.5 ॥
कथं च विष्णो रुद्रेण सार्द्धं प्रीतिरनुत्तमा।
सर्वे विष्णुमया देवा सर्वे विष्णुमया गणाः ॥ 21.6 ॥
1.20.m:
Thus ends the twentieth chapter, titled 'The Characteristics of the Attainment of Oṅkāra', in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa uttered by Vāyu. // 20

The Sūta said:
Among the seers resembling fire, residing in the Naimiṣa forest, / was a wise seer who preserved the scriptures, named Sāvarṇi by name.

Standing at their head, eloquent in speech, / he approached with humility the immensely radiant Vāyu, / who was constantly staying there for the welfare of those performing the sacrificial session, and asked: // 21.2

Sāvarṇi said:
O lord, we wish to hear properly the narrative connected with the Purāṇa, / commensurate with the Veda, through the grace of the all-seeing one.

How did the blessed Hiraṇyagarbha obtain from his forehead / the god Nīlalohita of such splendour as his own son? // 21.4

And how was the blessed Brahmā born from the lotus? / And how did his own son, Śarva, attain the state of Rudra? // 21.5

And how did Viṣṇu come to have supreme affection for Rudra? / All gods are manifestations of Viṣṇu, all hosts are manifestations of Viṣṇu, // 21.6

1.20.s:
na ca viṣṇusamā kācidgatiranyā vidhīyate.
ityevaṃ satataṃ devā gāyante nātra saṃśayaḥ.
bhavasya sakathaṃ nityaṃ praṇāmaṃ kurute hariḥ .. 21.7 ..
..sūta uvāca ..
evamukte tu bhagavān vāyuḥ sāvarṇimabravīt.
aho sādhu tvayā sādho pṛṣṭaḥ praśno hyanuttamaḥ .. 21.8 ..
bhavasya putrajanmatvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ so'bhavadyathā.
brahmaṇaḥ padma yonitvaṃ rudratvaṃ śaṃkarasya ca .. 21.9 ..
dvābhyāmapi ca samprītir
viṣṇoścaiva bhavasya ca .
yaccāpi kurute nityaṃ praṇāmaṃ śaṃkarasya ca.
vistareṇānupūrvyācca śrṛṇuta bruvato mama .. 21.10 ..
